title: Create a Ride
summary: Pick public or private, set the day, time and meeting point, choose a mapped route or freeride, and share your new ride.
headings: How Many Rides You Can Create
Create a Ride for an Event
text: You lead. Create a ride, tell everyone where and when to meet, and OnMyLead gives you a link, a code and a QR code to share. Public rides show up for riders nearby. Private rides are only for the people you invite. Create Your Ride On the Rides tab, tap Create a Ride . Under What Kind of Ride? , tap Public (open to anyone, found by riders near you or in your state) or Private (only friends you invite by link, text or email). Type a Ride Name . Under When , pick the day (see Pick the Day below). Set the time in Meet At (see Pick the Time below). Set the Meeting Point . You can search in Search a Place or Address , tap Use My Current Location , or paste Coordinates like "38.57, -109.55". Add a Place Name if you like, such as "Gas station on Main St". Under The Route , tap Mapped (you draw the route or import a GPX file next) or Freeride (no set route, everyone follows the leader). Under Who's Riding , pick the Vehicles Welcome . Tap Create Public Ride or Create Private Ride . From 2.1 a satellite map sits under Search a Place or Address , on every device. It opens near where you are. Tap it to drop the meeting point there, then drag the pin to fine-tune the spot. Searching a place, Use My Current Location and typed Coordinates move the pin too. (The map needs a signal; without one, set the point by search, location or coordinates as before.) Found a park in Scout? Tap Create a Ride Here on its page: Create a Ride opens as a public ride with the meeting point and Place Name already set to the park. Move the pin if your group meets somewhere else, such as the park's gate or a gas station nearby. Planning a rally or a ride weekend with several rides? That's an event, not one ride. Tap Event or Public Ride? at the top of Create a Ride to see the difference, or see Events. If you picked Mapped , the route builder opens right away so you can draw the trail. See Build a Route. Once the ride is saved you land on its page, ready to invite riders. Ride One of Your Trails This is a Pro feature. Open a trail in Navigate and tap Plan a Group Ride on This Trail . The new ride starts with the trail's name, the trail as its route and its start as the meeting point, under a Riding banner. Pick the day, change anything you like and create it. If the trail has a width limit, the Riding banner shows it (and whether your Garage machines fit), and the ride's Instructions for Joined Riders start with a line like "Trail width limit: 50". Wider machines won't fit." so everyone who joins sees it. Edit or delete that line like any other. Only riders who have joined see the exact meeting spot. Public pages show the general area, within about a mile. A Mapped ride, where you draw the route, is a Pro feature. See Free and Pro. On a Free account, Mapped carries a Pro tag; pick Freeride to create the ride for free. Pick the Day Under When , tap Today , Tomorrow , Sat or Sun for the coming weekend. For any other day, tap Calendar . Then either type the date or pick it on the calendar: Type a Date: tap the box and type the month, day and year, such as 06/12/2027. The number pad is enough; the slashes go in for you. The calendar jumps to that day. Tap a day: use the arrows to go to another month, or tap the month's name (such as "November 2026") to choose a year and month, then tap the day. You can schedule a ride for any day from today up to three years out, so rides next year and the year after are fine. Past days and days further out are greyed out. The day you picked shows under When , with how far away it is, such as "In 8 Weeks". Tap Done to fold the calendar away. On a tablet, the calendar sits in the same form, with bigger day buttons. Pick the Time No typing needed. Meet At starts at 8:00 AM. To change it, tap the time, then: Tap AM or PM . Tap the hour, 1 to 12 . Tap the minute, from :00 to :55 in 5-minute steps. title: Create and Manage a Riding Group
summary: Save the people you ride with as a group, invite friends with a link, and invite the whole group to a ride in one tap.
headings: Invite Friends With the Group Link
Invite Your Group to a Ride
Remove a Rider, Leave or Delete a Group
text: A riding group is your regular crew, saved once. When you create a ride, you can invite everyone in the group in one tap instead of sending the invite to each rider. Each group also has its own Group Chat. Your groups live on the Groups tab, on the Riding Groups screen. It shows Your Groups (the ones you run) and Groups You’re In (the ones someone else runs). The top of the Groups tab also has Out Riding , to see who's out riding near you, Messages , your direct messages, and Friends . See See Who's Out Riding Nearby and Add Friends. This is a Pro feature. You need Pro to create a group and to add or remove riders. See Free and Pro. Joining a group with its link, the group chat, inviting a group to your rides and getting the group's ride invites are free for everyone. On the Free plan, the buttons that need Pro carry a small gold Pro tag, so you know before you tap. Tapping one shows what Pro includes. During your Pro Trial and on Pro there are no tags. Create a Group Tap the Groups tab. Tap New Group . Type a Group Name , like Saturday Crew. Names can be up to 60 characters. Under Add Riders You’ve Ridden With , tick the riders you want in the group. Tap Save Group . The list only shows people you have been on a ride with, the ones you ride with most at the top. If nobody shows up yet, save the group anyway and send friends the group link (see below). A group holds up to 100 riders. Invite Friends With the Group Link The group link is for friends who aren't on OnMyLead yet, or anyone you haven't ridden with. Anyone in the group can share it. On the Groups tab, tap the group. Scroll to Invite by Link . Tap Share Group Link , or tap Text , Email or Copy . When your friend opens the link, they see the group's name, who runs it and how many riders are in it. They don't see who the riders are until they join. If the group has a group photo, the link shows it at the top too, so your friend can tell it's your crew. They tap Join Group , or Create a Free Account to Join if they don't have an account yet. The card also shows the Group Code , the end of the group's link. The rider who runs the group can tap Choose Your Own Code to make it something like SATURDAY-CREW, or type one under Group Code (Optional) when creating the group. See Choose Your Own Code. If a link got shared somewhere it shouldn't, the rider who runs the group can tap Make a New Link . The old link stops working, and everyone already in the group stays in. Add More Riders If you run the group: Open the group. Tap Add Riders You’ve Ridden With . Tick the riders and tap Add Riders . Invite Your Group to a Ride You can invite a group you're in to any upcoming ride you organize or co-organize. There are two ways. From the group: Open the group. Tap Invite to a Ride . Tap Invite next to the ride. From the ride: Open the ride and go to Riders . Under Invite a Group , tap Invite All next to the group. Or plan a new ride for the group: on Home, tap Plan a Group Ride on the Your Group card. The new ride has that group ticked under Your Riding Groups , so everyone is invited when you create it. Everyone in the group gets a notification and sees the ride under Ride Invites on their home screen. They can tap Join Ride , with no waiting for approval, or No Thanks . Riders who are already on the ride, waiting, or who said no thanks are left alone. To get these invites, keep Ride Invites on in Notification Settings. Add a Group Photo If you made the group, you can give it a photo, like the crew lined up by the trailhead. Everyone in the group sees it at the top of the group page, next to the group's name on the Riding Groups screen, on the Your Group card on Home and under Invite a Group on a ride. It also shows on the group link. Until you add one, the group shows its initials. Adding or changing a group photo is part of OnMyLead Pro, including the Pro Trial. title: Draw a Route
summary: Tap the map to lay down your ride's route. It snaps to trails for you, and every rider sees it in Ride Mode.
headings: Check Who Can Ride a Trail
text: A route is the line your group will follow. Once it's saved, every rider on the ride sees it on the ride page and in Ride Mode, with everyone placed along it. You draw it by tapping points on a satellite map, and OnMyLead follows the trails between your taps for you. Drawing a route is a Pro feature. See Free and Pro. On a Free account, Mapped on Create a Ride and Build the Route carry a Pro tag. Freeride rides, and following the leader's route on a ride, stay free. Bringing one in from a GPX file is covered in Import a GPX Route. To ride one of your own trails from Navigate, tap Use One of My Trails in the route builder and pick it. The trail is used as the route just as you recorded or drew it. This is a Pro feature, like GPX import. Clear it to draw your own. On the Free plan, the buttons that need Pro carry a small gold Pro tag, so you know before you tap. Tapping one shows what Pro includes. During your Pro Trial and on Pro there are no tags. Who Can Draw the Route The ride's organizer and any co-organizers can build or change the route, until the ride has ended or been cancelled. Everyone else on the ride sees the finished route but can't change it. See Organizer Controls. Open the Route Builder When you create a ride and pick Mapped under The Route , the route builder opens as soon as the ride is created. To open it later: Open the ride and tap the Map tab. Tap Build the Route . If the ride already has a route, tap Edit Route . For a Freeride, tap Map a Route Anyway . A Freeride that gets a saved route becomes a mapped ride. Draw Your Route The map opens at the ride's meeting point. Tap the map where the ride starts. That's point 1, shown in green. To get there fast, tap Search at the top and type a trailhead, park or town. Tap further along the trail. The route follows the trail between your two taps. Keep tapping along the way. Each new point is numbered, and the last one is shown in white. Watch the miles add up at the top of the panel at the bottom of the screen. Tap Save Route when you're done. After you save, you're taken back to the ride. Only riders on this ride can see the route. Follow Trails or Straight Line Two choices in the panel decide how the next points are joined: Follow Trails : each tap lands on the nearest trail or road, and the line between taps runs along it. While it works this out you'll see a dashed straight line and Finding the trail… . Straight Line : draws straight from point to point. Use it for open ground, a wash or a park nobody has mapped. You can switch between them as you go. Points you already placed keep the way they were drawn. The app remembers your choice for next time. If no mapped trail joins two points, that part is drawn as a straight line and the app tells you so. Add a point on the trail, or zoom in and try again. Points very far apart are also joined with a straight line, so tap more often on long stretches. Trails come from OpenStreetMap, so snapping works best where riders have mapped the trails. Zooming in before you tap helps each point land on the trail you meant. Fix Mistakes Undo takes back the last point. Drag any numbered point to move it. If the line next to it was following a trail, it snaps again. Clear removes every point. Nothing is saved until you tap Save Route . To see more of the map, swipe the panel down or tap its handle. It folds down to the miles and an Undo button. For the whole screen, tap Full Map on the panel's grab bar. The top bar, layers button and panel tuck away, and a slim bar keeps the miles and Undo . Keep tapping the map to add points, and tap Controls (or swipe the bar up) to bring everything back. See Full Map. Search for a Place To jump the map to a trailhead, park, forest or town before you draw: Tap Search at the top of the screen. Type a name, an address or coordinates. Tap a result. The map moves there and marks it. Searching only moves the map. Nothing is added to your route. See Search for a Place. Check Who Can Ride a Trail Whil

title: Find a Ride
summary: Browse public rides near you, near a place you search, or anywhere in a state, on a map or in a list.
headings: Public Rides Near You on Home
text: Looking for people to ride with? The Find tab shows public rides near you or anywhere in a state. Private rides never show here. You need an invite link or code for those. See Join a Ride. Looking for somewhere to ride instead of a group? Tap Places to Ride at the top of the Find tab to open Scout: off-road parks, OHV areas, trail systems and trailheads near you. See Find Places to Ride With Scout. Find Rides Near You Tap the Find tab (or Find a Ride on the Rides tab). Make sure Near Me is selected at the top. Allow location if asked. If location is off, tap Use My Location , or pick your state instead. Under How Far Will You Go? , pick 25 Miles , 50 Miles , 100 Miles or 250 Miles . Rides show on the map and in a list under it, nearest first, with how far away each one is. Public Rides Near You on Home Home also shows Public Rides Near You as cards you swipe sideways, nearest first. Tap the distance chip ( Within 500 mi at first) to pick 50 mi , 100 mi , 250 mi , 500 mi , 1,000 mi or Anywhere . Home never asks for your location: if you haven't allowed it, it shows every upcoming public ride. The Find a Ride card shows how many there are. See Your Home Screen. Find Rides Near a Place Planning a trip somewhere else? Search a park, trailhead or town. On the Find tab, tap Search Near a Place . Type the place and pick it from the results. The list shows Rides Near that place. Tap Back to Near Me to go back to rides around you. Find Rides in a State On the Find tab, tap By State . Pick a state. Rides in that state show soonest first. To switch states, tap the state's name in the corner of the map. Use the Map Each dot is a ride. Blue dots are upcoming rides. Red, glowing dots are live now. Tap a dot to see the ride's name, time and distance, then tap Open Ride . Tap the map away from a dot to close the ride's card. The map is drawn by Mapbox, the same on the phone and the website. Move or zoom the map, then tap Search This Area to see rides there. To return, tap the button under the map that starts with Back to , such as Back to Rides Near Me . Use the + and - buttons to zoom, and the location button to recenter the map. Tap the Full Map button above the zoom buttons to make the map fill the screen (on a tablet or a wide screen, the list tucks away). Tap it again ( Exit Full Map ) to bring the list back. See Full Map. On a wide screen, such as the website on a computer, the search and the list of rides sit on the left and the map fills the rest of the screen. Dots sit on the ride's general meeting area, within about a mile. The exact meeting spot is shown only to riders who join. What You'll See Find shows public rides that are coming up or live right now. Each ride in the list shows its date, time, general area, difficulty, distance and the vehicles welcome. Tap a ride to open its page and join. See Join a Ride. If there are no rides yet, tap Create a Public Ride to start one. See Create a Ride. Looking for a rally or a ride weekend? Those are events. Tap Event or Public Ride? under the search to see the difference and See Events to browse them. See Events. The Rides tab also lists a few upcoming Public Rides . Tap Find Rides on the Map (or See All on the Map , which shows how many there are) to see them all.

title: Fix Common Problems
summary: What to check when riders don't show on the map, alerts don't arrive, a download stops or sign-in fails.
headings: A Rider Shows as a Hollow Dot or "Last Seen"
A Rider Shows Miles From Where They Are
My Group Can't See Me With My Phone Locked
I Tapped a Status Button With No Signal
Nearby Riders Don't Show Up Over Bluetooth
Part of My Route Is a Straight Line
I Turned On Trails but See No Lines
I Turned On Land but See No Boundaries
I Don't See a Fuel Check on My Ride
My Password Reset Link Says It Has Expired
The Starlink Page Can't Reach My Dish
text: Start here when something doesn't work the way you expect. If your problem isn't listed, contact us. A Rider Shows as a Hollow Dot or "Last Seen" A rider's dot turns hollow when their last position is more than a minute old, and shows No Signal with a dashed grey ring after about 3 minutes. A sharing phone checks in at least every 15 seconds while it has service, so this usually means that rider lost service. A live rider's dot is a solid disc with a white rim and an arrow inside it (blue for the leader, violet for the tail gunner, graphite for everyone else). A last-seen rider's dot is a thin grey ring with no arrow instead. If everyone suddenly shows as last seen, it's probably your phone. After about 35 seconds without hearing from the server, Ride Mode shows No Service. Riders Show Where They Were Last Seen . It doesn't mark the others as lost because of your own dropout. See Share Your Location. A Rider Shows Miles From Where They Are If a rider right beside you shows up a mile or two away, their phone is giving every app a rough location (Google Maps or Apple Maps on that phone shows the same wrong spot). On that phone, turn on Precise Location for OnMyLead and, on Android, Google Location Accuracy , then calibrate. Step by step: Make Your Location Accurate. My Group Can't See Me With My Phone Locked Open your iPhone's Settings OnMyLead Location . Choose Always . Open Ride Mode again. If your share is still running, it picks back up. On Android, check that the Sharing Your Location notification is showing while you share. If it isn't, open Ride Mode again to restart it. If your phone has a battery saver that closes apps, set OnMyLead's battery use to Unrestricted in Settings Apps OnMyLead Battery . If sharing drains your battery too fast on long days, try Battery Saver. Your group sees you less often, so switch back to Best Accuracy when you can charge. If Ride Mode shows Location Is Off , location is turned off for OnMyLead, so your group can't see you move. Turn it back on in your phone's Settings , then open Ride Mode again. Closing Ride Mode or locking your phone doesn't stop sharing. Sharing ends when your timer runs out, the ride ends, you leave the ride, or you tap Stop . I Tapped a Status Button With No Signal It waits on your phone as Waiting for Signal and sends by itself as soon as you have service, stamped with the time you tapped it. You can tap Retry Now or Cancel . See Status Buttons. Nearby Riders Don't Show Up Over Bluetooth Bluetooth Sharing reaches about 30 to 100 meters between phones. Check that Bluetooth is on in the phone's settings, that OnMyLead is allowed to use Bluetooth (iPhone and iPad: Settings OnMyLead Bluetooth ; Android: Settings Apps OnMyLead Permissions Nearby devices ), that Bluetooth Sharing is on in the You tab (or the no-service banner in Ride Mode says Bluetooth On ), and that you opened Ride Mode once with service. On Free, riders' spots and messages over Bluetooth don't show (they're Pro); status taps, including EMERGENCY, Need Help, Crash Alerts and I'm OK, still do. Riders only send their spot while they share with the ride. See Share With Nearby Riders With No Service. I'm Not Getting Alerts Check that notifications are allowed for OnMyLead in your iPhone's Settings Notifications OnMyLead . In the app, open You and check your notification settings, including quiet hours. On Android, check Settings Apps OnMyLead Notifications , including the Rider Alerts , Ride Chat and Ride Updates categories. Need Help and EMERGENCY alerts from your group always come through, even in quiet hours, as long as iPhone notifications are allowed for OnMyLead. The Spoken Alerts Sound Robotic Your phone may only have its small standard voice. Open You Voice to hear the voices on your phone, and follow the steps there to download a free Premium or Enhanced voice. See Choose the Voice for Spoken Alerts. title: Free and Pro
summary: What every OnMyLead account gets for free, what OnMyLead Pro adds, and how the Free monthly ride works.
text: OnMyLead is free to download and use. Free accounts can join as many rides as they like, and every safety feature is free on every plan. OnMyLead Pro is for riders who lead a lot of rides and want extras like offline maps and GPX import. Pro is $4.99 a month or $29.99 a year in the US. Other countries see the price in local currency. Every new account starts with a free 30-day Pro Trial. What's Included This is the same comparison as the Free and Pro table on the Pro screen. Safety never depends on your plan. On every plan you get Ride Mode, live tracking, Need Help, EMERGENCY, Mechanical Issue alerts, Crash Alert, Ride Bubble, location sharing, family links, ride chat, the status buttons and the leader's route and waypoints on the ride map. Directions to a rider who needs help are free too. The Free Monthly Ride Free accounts create one ride each calendar month. The month follows UTC time, so a new month can start a few hours earlier or later than midnight where you live. A ride counts when you create it. Deleting or cancelling it doesn't give the ride back. Using Ride Again to copy a ride counts as creating a ride. Rides you create on the website count too. Joining other riders' rides is always unlimited. When you create a ride on a Free account, the Create a Ride screen shows how many you've created this month, like Rides Created This Month: 0 of 1 . If you've used it, the app tells you the date your next free ride opens, and you can tap See OnMyLead Pro or Not Now . Free Map Mode Time Free accounts get 8 hours of Map Mode every calendar month (UTC time). Pro has no limit. The clock only runs while Map Mode is open on your screen. It stops when you leave Map Mode or put the app in the background. It never runs while you're sharing your location on a group ride, so riding with a group and following the leader stay unlimited. Your time is counted on your OnMyLead account, so it's the same on every device and doesn't reset if you reinstall the app. Map Mode shows the time you have left, like Free Map Mode: 5 h 20 m Left This Month . When the time is used up, Map Mode tells you and offers See OnMyLead Pro . It opens again at the start of the next month. title: Get Started With OnMyLead
summary: What OnMyLead is, how to get the app on iPhone, iPad or Android, make your account, and find your way around the Rides, Find, Groups and You tabs.
text: OnMyLead is a group ride app for off-road riders. The leader creates a ride, the crew joins with a code, link or QR code, and on the trail everyone shares one live map, a group chat and quick taps like Need Fuel and Flat Tire that tell the whole group at once. Get the App OnMyLead runs on iPhone, iPad, Android phones and Android tablets. Download OnMyLead free from the App Store on an iPhone or iPad, or from Google Play on an Android phone or tablet, then open it. It's the same account, rides and Pro plan on every device, and iPhone and Android riders ride together on the same map. Agree Before You Ride The first time you open the app, the Before You Ride screen shows the Rider Safety and Liability Agreement. Read it, tick the box and tap I Agree . On onmylead.com it shows after you sign in. See The Rider Safety and Liability Agreement. Make Your Account You can look around without an account, but you need one to create rides, save your Garage and keep riding groups. On the Rides tab, tap Sign In or Create a Free Account . Tap Create Account at the top. Use one of the Continue with buttons, or enter Your Name , Email and a Password of at least 8 characters, then tap Create Account . If we email you a link, tap it on the same iPhone to confirm your email and finish signing in. See Sign In and Create an Account for every way to sign in. Next, pick your ride name. It's what other riders see on the map, the rider list and in chat. Until you pick one, Home shows Pick Your Ride Name and other riders see you as Rider. See Your Ride Name and Profile. New accounts start with a free Pro Trial. See The Pro Trial. Find Your Way Around Four tabs run along the bottom of the screen: Rides , Find , Groups and You . In the middle, the blue Map Mode button opens your offroad map from any tab. See Navigate Offroad and Map Your Own Trails. On a tablet they run down the left edge instead, with Map Mode under Find . See Use OnMyLead on a Tablet. Rides Your home screen. Join a Ride is the big red card at the top: type the invite code and tap Join . Joining is always free and unlimited. Create a Ride shows how many rides you have left this month on Free, or Unlimited on Pro. Find a Ride shows how many public rides are near you. Map Mode : Open Map Mode , Map a Custom Trail and the Track Line switch. Your Next Ride , Ride Invites and Past Rides ; Your Group ; Public Rides Near You ; your Feed ; Your Badges ; Your Toolkit ; and Help & Support . The bell and your picture at the top right open your notifications and the You tab. Events , the gold card right under Create a Ride and Find a Ride , with Map Mode under it. Join, Create, Find, Events and Map Mode all fit on the first screen. See Your Home Screen for each part. Find Public rides on a map. Choose Near Me or By State , or use Search Near a Place to look around a trailhead, park or town. See Find a Ride. Groups Your riding groups, the groups you're in, and Leaders You Follow . Tap New Group to save your crew. You need an account for this tab; if you're signed out, it takes you to sign in. See Riding Groups. At the top: Out Riding , to see which riders are out near you and message them, and your Messages . See See Who's Out Riding Nearby. You Everything that isn't a ride: Your ride name and plan at the top. Your Gear : Garage, Trip Planner and Offline Maps. On the Trail : Share My Location and Starlink. On the Trail also has Navigate and Rider Trails on Maps , which shows or hides trails other riders shared. Follow Me on Maps , also under On the Trail , turns off (or back on) the map moving with you in Ride Mode and Navigate. See Follow Me on the Map. Music Controls , also under On the Trail , shows or hides the Music button in Ride Mode and Navigate. See Control Your Music While You Ride. title: Share Your Location
summary: Choose who sees your location and for how long, from a few hours to until you turn it off. You can stop it any time.
headings: Share with Chosen Riders or Family
text: OnMyLead only shares your location when you turn it on, only with the people you choose, and only for as long as you pick. These rules are enforced by OnMyLead's server, not just the app. There are two ways to share: With a ride: everyone on the ride sees you on the Ride Mode map. On a Freeride, if you're the leader, each rider's phone keeps the path you've ridden while they're in Ride Mode, built from the same live location they already see, to measure how far behind you everyone is. It stays on their phone, isn't uploaded, and is cleared after 18 hours or when they open another Freeride. With chosen people: riders you pick, a family link, or both, from Share My Location . Share with Your Ride When you open Ride Mode on a live ride and aren't sharing yet, the app asks Share Your Location with This Ride? Open Ride Mode. See Use Ride Mode. Pick how long to share: 2 Hours , 4 Hours , 8 Hours or Until I Turn It Off . Or tap Pick an End Date , pick the day on the calendar (or type it), set Stop Sharing At , and tap the Share Until button. See Pick an End Date. If your iPhone asks for location access, allow it. Choose Always so the group keeps seeing you with the phone locked. Only riders on this ride see you. Tap Not Now to skip. You can start sharing later by tapping the Off pill at the top of Ride Mode. Check or Stop Ride Sharing The pill at the top of Ride Mode shows the time left, such as 1h 20m , or On when you picked Until I Turn It Off . A share that runs for more than a day shows days, such as 3d . Tap the pill. A banner shows Sharing and the time left. Tap Stop to stop sharing now, or Hide to fold the banner back into the pill. When Ride Sharing Ends Sharing with a ride stops on its own at the first of these: Your timer runs out, or the end date you picked arrives. The organizer ends or cancels the ride. You leave the ride. You tap Stop . Even Until I Turn It Off stops when the ride ends or you leave it. Sharing with a ride never carries on after the ride. Closing Ride Mode, or locking your phone, doesn't stop sharing. If the app was closed or your phone restarted, opening Ride Mode picks your share back up. Share with Chosen Riders or Family Tap the You tab. Under On the Trail , tap Share My Location . Under Who Can See You , tap the riders you want. Only people you've been on a ride with are listed. To share with someone who doesn't have the app, turn on Family Link . See Share a Family Link. Under For How Long , pick 15 Min , 1 Hour , 4 Hours or 8 Hours , tap Until I Turn It Off , or tap Pick an End Date to choose a day and time on a calendar. Until I Turn It Off has no time limit. It keeps sharing, even for days, until you tap Stop Sharing . The app asks you to confirm before it starts. While you share, Share My Location shows a card for each share with Sharing Now and when it ends: the time left, the end date (such as until Sat, Nov 14, 6:00 PM ), or until you turn it off . On the You tab, the Share My Location row also says you're sharing and until when, so a long share is never forgotten. Tap Add 1 Hour to keep going longer. In the last 10 minutes, the button says Ending Soon · Add 1 Hr . A share set to Until I Turn It Off doesn't need it, so it isn't shown. Tap Stop Sharing to end it now. Pick an End Date Both the ride sharing sheet and Share My Location let you pick exactly when sharing stops, up to a year out. Tap Pick an End Date . A calendar opens. Tap a day, or type the date in the box above the calendar. Use the arrows to change months. Check Stop Sharing At . It starts at 6:00 PM (or about an hour from now, later today). To change it, tap the time, then tap AM or PM , the hour and the minute. Tap the button, such as Share Until Sat, Nov 14, 6:00 PM . A share with an end date still stops early if you tap Stop Sharing , and a ride share still stops when the ride ends. Location in the Background To keep your group updated while your phone is locked or in your pocket, OnMyLead needs location access set to Alway

title: Sign In and Create an Account
summary: Sign in with Apple, Google or Facebook, an email and password, or an emailed sign-in link, and reset a forgotten password.

Create an Account With Email and a Password

Opening an Email Link on Another Device
text: You need an account to create rides, keep a Garage and save riding groups. You can sign in with a social account, with your email and a password, or with a link we email you. Open the Sign-In Screen On the Rides tab or the You tab, tap Sign In or Create a Free Account . At the top, choose Sign In if you already have an account, or Create Account if you're new. Tapping something that needs an account, like the Groups tab, also opens this screen. Sign In With Apple, Google or Facebook Depending on what's turned on, you'll see Continue with Apple , Continue with Google and Continue with Facebook at the top of the screen. Tap the button for the account you want to use. Follow the steps on the Apple, Google or Facebook screen. You're signed in and taken back to OnMyLead. If you were new, your account is created. With Apple, the name on your Apple Account is used as your ride name the first time you sign in, if Apple shares it. You can change it any time. See Your Ride Name and Profile. On the website and on Android, Continue with Apple uses Apple's web sign-in: the page goes to Apple and comes straight back. It's only there when it's been switched on; if you don't see it, use Apple in the iPhone app or sign in another way. The Android app needs version 2.1 or later for it. Create an Account With Email and a Password Tap Create Account at the top. Enter Your Name . This is what riders will see, and you can change it later. Enter your Email . Enter a Password of at least 8 characters. Tap Create Account . If the app says Almost done , open the email we sent and tap the link on the same iPhone. Your email is confirmed and you're signed in. Sign In With Email and a Password Tap Sign In at the top. Enter your Email and Password . Tap Sign In . Sign In With an Email Link (No Password) Enter your Email . Tap Or email me a sign-in link instead (no password) . Open the email on the same iPhone and tap the link. The link signs you in and opens Home, even if the sign-in screen was still open. If you don't have an account yet, it creates one. Reset a Forgotten Password Tap Sign In at the top. Enter your Email . Tap Forgot your password? Email me a reset link . Open the email on your iPhone and tap the link. Enter a New Password of at least 8 characters. Tap Save Password . If you see This Link Has Expired , tap Back to Sign In and ask for a new reset link. Opening an Email Link on Another Device If you tap a link from us in a browser on an iPhone, you may see Open OnMyLead . Tap Open in the App to finish in the app, or Continue on the Website to stay in the browser. If you see Your Email Is Confirmed and a request to sign in again, the link opened somewhere other than where you signed up. Your email is confirmed. Tap Sign In and sign in once more with your email and password. Sign Out Go to the You tab. Scroll down and tap Sign Out . This signs you out on this device only. If you're also signed in on another device or the website, you stay signed in there, and any location you're sharing from that device keeps going. If Something Goes Wrong That email and password don't match : check for typos, or use the reset link above. Please confirm your email first : tap the link in the email we sent you, then sign in. title: Use Ride Mode
summary: The live group map for ride day. See every rider, who is live and who was last seen, where you are on the route, and the one-tap buttons.
headings: See Where You Are on the Route
See the Whole Group in Order
See How Spread Out the Group Is
See the Group Behind the Leader on a Freeride
Fold the Panel to See More Map
text: Ride Mode is the screen you use on the trail. It puts the whole group on one map, shows how fresh each rider's position is, places everyone along the route, and gives you big one-tap buttons for telling the group what's going on. Ride Mode is free on every plan. Open Ride Mode Ride Mode opens once the organizer starts the ride. Organizers: on the ride page, tap Start Ride Mode . The ride goes live for everyone and Ride Mode opens. Riders: once the ride is live, open the ride page and tap Enter Ride Mode . Riders on the ride also get a notification when the ride starts. The map opens centered on you, zoomed in to about 10 miles across so nearby trails show, and clear of the panels over the map. If your phone hasn't found you yet, the map centers on you as soon as it does, unless you've already moved the map yourself. If OnMyLead can't use your location, the map opens on the group, the route or the meeting point instead. The first time you open Ride Mode on a ride, it asks Share Your Location with This Ride? Pick how long to share, or tap Not Now . You can see the group without sharing, but the group can't see you. See Share Your Location. Your screen stays on while Ride Mode is open, so the map is ready when you glance at it. Keep a charger handy on long rides. What's on the Screen The Top Bar ‹ (back): the round button on the left goes back to the ride page. Ride name and sharing: under the ride's name a green dot and Sharing · 1h 20m Left (or just Sharing when there's no timer) show you're sharing. When you aren't, it says Not Sharing · Tap to Share ; tap it to start. While you share, tap the name to show Sharing, 1 hr 20 min left with Stop and Hide . If you've turned on Battery Saver, that banner also names the setting, such as Sharing, 1 hr 20 min left · Balanced . Together or 2 Separated (on the right): green when the group is together, red with a count when Ride Bubble sees riders who have dropped away. Tap it to open the Riders list. The Map The map shows the ride's route, waypoints, planned stops and any regroup point. Every rider who is sharing shows as a dot with their ride name beside it. Tap a rider's dot to see their name, whether they're live, and their latest status. Each rider is a white ring with a dark center and a dark name tag, easy to spot on satellite, topo and the dark map. The leader is the bigger solid blue dot with a blue name tag, so you can find them at a glance. Every dot sits on the rider's exact position and stays there as you zoom in and out. When a rider is moving, a small white arrow on the edge of their dot points the way they're heading, even when you turn the map. A rider who is stopped, or whose position is only last seen, has no arrow, because a phone can only tell direction while it moves. From 2.1 every live rider is a glossy disc with a white rim and a white arrow built into it, pointing the way they're heading. The leader is the biggest dot, in blue with a blue name tag; the tail gunner is the next biggest, in violet with a violet name tag; everyone else is graphite with a dark name tag. A rider keeps their arrow, pointing the last way they were heading, while they're stopped and still live. A rider whose position is only last seen is a hollow ring with no arrow, as before. Your own dot is Red, White and Blue unless you pick another Dot Style in Map Settings, with a soft beam ahead of it. Its arrow always shows which way you're facing: the way you're riding while you move, and your phone's compass when you stop. Riders glide smoothly to each new position instead of jumping, and with Follow Me on, the map moves with you in one steady motion. A blue line follows behind the leader, showing exactly where they rode. When the leader crosses back over it or doubles back, the older pass fades so the fresh line stands out. The leader can turn it off. See Follow the Leader's Trackline. You don't need to leave Ride Mode to see new riders. Someone who joins the ride while you're on the map appears

title: What's New in OnMyLead 2.1
summary: Bluetooth Sharing with no service, the Emergency Siren, Map Settings, 3D Terrain, the Badge Leaderboard and the rest of 2.1, with a link to the guide for each.
keywords: what's new, changes, release notes, bluetooth, no service
text: OnMyLead 2.1 keeps your group talking where the signal ends. It works the same on iPhone, iPad, Android phones and Android tablets, except CarPlay, which is iPhone only. Here are the big changes, with the guide for each. The full list is on the Release Notes page. The Big Changes Bluetooth Sharing with no service. When there's no cell service, phones on the same ride pass spots, status taps, messages and EMERGENCY to each other over Bluetooth, about 100 to 300 feet between phones, and every phone passes them along the group. Seeing riders and sharing your spot, taps and messages over Bluetooth is Pro. On every plan your phone passes everything along, and EMERGENCY, Need Help and Crash Alerts go out over Bluetooth. It isn't a satellite messenger and can't reach 911. See Share With Nearby Riders With No Service. Emergency Siren. When another rider on your ride sends EMERGENCY, or their Crash Alert goes out, your phone sounds a loud siren on a full-screen alert until you tap Silence Siren or Show Me Where. See Hear the Emergency Siren. Map Settings. One round button in the top-left corner of every riding map opens everything about the map: the map style, roads, trails and land boundaries, how the map follows you, and your own dot. See Map Layers and Trails. A smoother map that keeps you on screen. The map moves smoothly while you ride, your dot stays on screen, and the map zooms in at intersections so you see the turn. See Follow Me on the Map. A new rider dot. Every live rider is a glossy dot with an arrow pointing the way they're heading: the leader in blue, the tail gunner in violet. With Pro you pick your own dot's style and size in Map Settings. See Use Ride Mode. Group Spread and Leader Trackline. A measuring line under the rider line shows how far the last rider is behind the leader, and a blue line behind the leader shows exactly which way they went. See Follow the Leader's Trackline. 3D Terrain. Satellite on the real shape of the land in Ride Mode and Map Mode, and you can save it in Offline Maps. See 3D Terrain. Badge Leaderboard. See where you rank in your state, your country or everywhere, by the badges you earned riding. See See the Badge Leaderboard. Group Photos. Give your riding group a photo of the crew. Everyone sees it; adding one is Pro. See Create and Manage a Riding Group. CarPlay (Pro, iPhone). Your ride on the car screen, with big buttons for status taps and EMERGENCY. See Use OnMyLead on CarPlay. Edit Ride Details, drop a waypoint by holding the map, Scout for places to ride and offroad park trails on every map. See Edit, Cancel or Delete a Ride, Waypoints and Planned Stops, Find Places to Ride With Scout and Offroad Park Trails. Always call 911. The Rider Safety and Liability Agreement (version 2) says plainly that OnMyLead's alerts only reach riders on your ride. After you update, the Before You Ride screen shows once more so you can read it and tap I Agree. See The Rider Safety and Liability Agreement. See your version. The bottom of Home shows which version you have, like Version 2.1 (10). A Fresh Pro Trial Bluetooth Sharing, CarPlay, customizing your dot and adding group photos are part of OnMyLead Pro from 2.1. So nobody loses anything the day 2.1 arrives, every rider who doesn't have Pro gets a fresh 30-day Pro trial, and Home shows the date it ends. Safety stays free on every plan. See Your Free 30-Day Pro Trial and Free and Pro. Get the Update Open the App Store on iPhone or iPad, or Google Play on Android, and update OnMyLead. Everything you had before, your rides, groups, garage and trails, is still there.

title: Full Map
summary: Hide the bars and panels on any map so the map fills your screen, and bring them back with one tap.
text: Every map in OnMyLead can fill your whole screen. Full Map tucks the top bar and the panel away, and leaves one slim bar at the bottom so you can bring everything back with one tap. The round Map Settings button stays in the top-left corner and the compass in the top-right, so you can change the map without leaving Full Map. Turn On Full Map Tap Full Map at the right end of the panel's grab bar, at the top of the panel over the map. It's in the same place in: Ride Mode Navigate Draw a Route Waypoints and Planned Stops Or swipe the panel down: a long swipe (or a quick flick) goes straight to Full Map. A short swipe folds the panel down to its grab bar as before, and swiping down again on the folded panel goes to Full Map. On a tablet, where the panel hangs from the top beside the map, swipe it up instead. In Find a Ride, tap the Full Map button at the top of the buttons on the map's right edge. Scout ( Places to Ride on the Find tab) has the same Full Map button. Bring the Buttons Back Tap Controls in the bar at the bottom, or swipe the bar up. The bar has a small grab handle on top as a reminder that it swipes up. Everything comes back the way you left it. In Find a Ride, tap the same corner button again ( Exit Full Map ). Your phone remembers Full Map for each map, so it opens the same way next time. Find a Ride always opens with its list. What Stays on Screen The bar keeps only what you shouldn't have to dig for: Map In the bar or on the map --- --- Ride Mode The rider line with every rider (on a Freeride, the group behind the leader), EMERGENCY , calls for help from other riders, Center on Me , Follow Me , and Music if you use Music Controls Navigate Your speed, the miles left on a trail you're following, or the length you're measuring, a red Rec while recording, Undo while measuring, Center on Me and Follow Me (not while measuring) Draw a Route The route's miles and Undo . Tapping the map still adds points Waypoints Just the map and its pins. Press and hold the map to drop a waypoint On every map, the No Signal tag stays when you have no service, and tapping a trail line still shows its card. Phones, Tablets and the Website Full Map works the same on iPhone, iPad, Android phones and Android tablets. On a tablet the bar sits in the bottom-left corner. On onmylead.com, press F to turn on Full Map and Esc to bring the controls back (not while you're typing in a box).

title: Follow Me on the Map
summary: Keep the map moving with your dot as you ride, see which way you're heading, and turn Follow Me on or off.
headings: How the Map Keeps Up With You
text: With Follow Me on, the map in Ride Mode and Navigate moves with you as you ride, so your dot stays in view and you never have to drag the map to find yourself. How the Map Keeps Up With You Your dot moves freely through the middle of the map. The first time it gets within about a tenth of the screen of an edge of the open part of the map (clear of the panels), the map zooms out one step. The next time your dot reaches an edge, the map centers on your dot and from then on moves with you, keeping your dot in the middle so it's always on screen. The map never turns. Tapping Center on Me , or picking Follow Me back up after a pause, starts fresh: the map may zoom out one step again the next time you near an edge. Zoom In at Intersections While the map is following you and you're moving, it zooms in as you come up on a junction of roads or trails, about 9 seconds before you reach it, so you can see the turn up close. Once you're through, it zooms back out to where it was. It works with any road, track or trail drawn on the map, including on a downloaded map with no signal. Zoom In at Intersections is on until you turn it off, either in Map Settings under Following or in the You tab under On the Trail . Your choice follows your account to your other devices. Your Dot Your own dot has an arrow built into it and a soft beam ahead of it (Red, White and Blue unless you pick another Dot Style in Map Settings, a Pro feature). The arrow always shows which way you're facing: the direction you're riding while you move, and your phone's compass when you're stopped, so it turns as you turn. The beam is long while you ride and shorter when you stop. The dot takes its stopped look as soon as your phone reports you've stopped, or after a short while with no new location (about 8 seconds; in Ride Mode on Android phones and tablets using the basic map instead of Mapbox, about 25 seconds with Balanced and about 37 seconds with Max Battery Saver, which update less often). It stays true when you turn the map. On the Mapbox map in the iPhone, iPad and Android apps, if your device has no compass reading while you're stopped, the dot shows a round centre with no arrow instead of guessing a direction; the basic map and the website keep pointing the last way you were heading. The Follow Me Button Follow Me sits on the map just left of the round Center on Me button. What you see What it means --- --- Blue Following The map is moving with you. Tap it to turn Follow Me off. Blue outline, Paused You dragged or pinched the map, so it stopped following to let you look around. Tap it, or Center on Me , to follow you again. Plain Follow Me Follow Me is off. The map stays where you put it. Tap it to turn Follow Me on. Follow Me is on until you turn it off. Your phone remembers the choice for Ride Mode and Navigate alike, and you can also switch it in the You tab under On the Trail : Follow Me on Maps . From 2.1 these switches are also under Following in Map Settings (the round Map Settings button on Ride Mode's and Map Mode's map): Follow Me , Zoom Out at the Edge and Zoom In at Intersections . Turn Zoom Out at the Edge off and the map centers on your dot and moves with you the first time you near an edge, without zooming out first; it's also on the You tab under On the Trail . The zoom switches work while Follow Me is on. With Follow Me off, Center on Me still centers the map on you once, and Navigate doesn't move the map by itself, even while you record or follow a trail. In Navigate the map holds still while the Measure tab is open, and when you jump to a place with search. In Full Map In Full Map, Follow Me stays on the map as a round arrow button next to Center on Me , so the map stays as big as it can be. On Each Device iPhone and Android phones: Follow Me and Center on Me sit on the right, just above the bottom panel. If the panel fills the screen, fold it to see them. iPad and Android tablets: both sit at the bottom of the map, just left of the buttons pane

title: Find Places to Ride With Scout
summary: Scout shows off-road parks, OHV areas, trail systems, trailheads and motocross tracks near you, up to 1,000 miles away.
headings: Show Only Some Kinds of Places
On a Tablet or the Website
text: Scout finds places to ride near you: off-road parks, OHV areas, trail systems, trailheads and motocross tracks. It looks 250 miles around you to start, and you can change that from 10 to 1,000 miles. Open Scout Tap the Find tab. Tap Places to Ride at the top. ( Rides takes you back to public rides.) Allow location if asked. If location is off, tap Use My Location , or search a town or park instead. Places show on the map as teal signs, with a picture of the kind of place (a flag on a peak for an off-road park, a quad for an OHV area, a forked trail for a trail system, a signpost for a trailhead and a checkered flag for a motocross track), and in a list under it (beside it on a tablet or a wide screen), nearest first. Each place shows what kind it is, where it is, how far away it is and how many public rides are coming up there. Change How Far Scout Looks Under How Far to Look , drag the slider, tap along it, or tap - and + to move one step: 10, 25, 50, 75, 100, 150, 200, 250, 300, 400, 500, 750 or 1,000 miles. The list and the circle on the map update when you let go. Scout remembers the distance on this device for next time. Look Somewhere Else Planning a trip? Tap Look Around a Town or Park , type a place and pick it from the results. Scout shows Places Near that place. Tap Back to Near Me to look around you again. Show Only Some Kinds of Places Under the slider, tap a kind, such as Off-Road Parks or Trailheads , to show only that kind. Tap more than one to see each of them. Tap a kind again to turn it off. Each chip shows how many places of that kind Scout found. Open a Place Tap a place in the list, or tap its sign on the map and then Open Place . Its page shows: what kind of place it is, where it is and how far away it is; Create a Ride Here , which starts a public ride with the meeting point already on the place; its website, when we have one; Directions in your maps app (see Directions); Public Rides Here : public rides meeting within 15 miles that you can join; a short description, when the source has one. Place details come from the US Forest Service, the Bureau of Land Management and OpenStreetMap (© OpenStreetMap contributors), plus places riders suggested. Each page says where its details came from. Check the rules, hours, fees and which vehicles are allowed with the park or agency before you go. Suggest a Place We're Missing At the bottom of the Scout list, tap Know a Place We're Missing? Enter the name and pick what kind of place it is. Show us where it is: search for it, tap the map, or tap I'm There Now if you're standing at it. Add the website and anything we should know if you like, then tap Send Suggestion . You need to be signed in to suggest a place. We check every suggestion before it shows in Scout. Riders never see who suggested a place. On a Tablet or the Website On an iPad, an Android tablet or a wide browser window, the slider, the filters and the list sit on the left and the map fills the rest of the screen. Tap Full Map to make the map fill the whole screen. On the website, Scout is at onmylead.com under Find once you sign in.

title: Follow the Leader's Trackline
summary: A line in the leader's blue shows where the leader went in Ride Mode. Older passes fade when the leader crosses back over it. The leader can turn it off.
headings: When the Leader Crosses Their Own Line
text: In Ride Mode, a line follows behind the leader on every rider's map, in the same blue as the leader's dot. It shows exactly where the leader rode, so at a fork, a wash or a faint two-track you can see which way they went. The line starts when you open Ride Mode and grows as the leader moves. The leader sees it on their own map too. When the Leader Crosses Their Own Line If the leader crosses the line, rides a loop back to where they started, or doubles back down the same trail, everything from before that point turns faded, thinner and dashed. The line from there on stays bright solid blue and is drawn on top. So where two passes share a trail, the bright line is always the newest one, the one to follow. Short wiggles, a tight hairpin, or wandering a few yards off the old line on the way back don't start a new pass. Turn It Off (Leader) The line is on for every ride unless the leader turns it off. Turning it off hides it for everyone on the ride, and turning it back on brings it back for everyone, including the part ridden while it was off. In Ride Mode, tap the round Map Settings button on the map. Under Leader Trackline , tap the row to switch between On for Everyone and Off for Everyone . The switch shows for the leader and the ride's organizers. If nobody has the Leader role, the organizer leads. Riders see the line but not the switch. With no signal the switch can't save; try again when you have service. Good to Know Each phone draws the line from the leader's live position, which riders on the ride already see. Nothing new is uploaded. Your phone keeps the line for the ride you're on, so closing Ride Mode and coming back doesn't lose it, and the next ride's line replaces it. If your phone stops hearing from the leader for a while (no signal, or Ride Mode was closed), the line has a gap rather than a straight line across the map. A stop, like lunch or a regroup, doesn't fade the line behind the leader. Open Ride Mode early to see the whole ride. If the leader changes partway through the ride, the line starts again from the new leader. iPhone, iPad, Android phones and Android tablets: the line shows on every map style, including 3D Terrain and the flat Apple or Google map. Website: the line shows on the live Mapbox map. Where the website shows only a sketch of the route, there's no line.

title: Make Your Location Accurate
summary: If a rider shows up a mile or more from where they really are, turn on Precise Location and, on Android, Google Location Accuracy, then calibrate.
text: OnMyLead shows each rider where their phone says they are. If a rider sitting right next to you shows up a mile or two away, their phone is giving every app a rough location, not just OnMyLead. Open Google Maps or Apple Maps on that phone: if its blue dot is in the same wrong spot, follow the steps below on that phone. On Android Turn on precise location for OnMyLead. Open Settings Apps OnMyLead Permissions Location and turn on Use precise location . Turn on Google Location Accuracy. Open Settings Location Location Services Google Location Accuracy and turn on Improve Location Accuracy . With it off, the phone has only GPS, and indoors or under trees the dot can land miles away. Calibrate. Open Google Maps, tap your blue dot and choose Calibrate , then follow the steps (it may ask you to point the phone at buildings, or move it in a figure 8). Menu names differ a little between phone makers. Search Settings for "precise" or "location accuracy" if you can't find them. On iPhone and iPad Open Settings Privacy & Security Location Services OnMyLead and turn on Precise Location . If the dot still wanders, open Settings Privacy & Security Location Services System Services and turn on Compass Calibration . Everywhere Go outside or near a window with a clear view of the sky for a minute. Then open Ride Mode again: the dot moves to where the rider really is with the next update. What OnMyLead Does for You When you start sharing on Android , OnMyLead asks once to change to a precise location if you allowed only an approximate one, and shows Android's prompt to turn on Google Location Accuracy if it's off. Ride Mode shows a yellow banner when your own location isn't sharp: Precise Location Is Off , Google Location Accuracy Is Off , or Your Phone Has a Rough Location Right Now . Tap it to fix it: Android asks or opens Location settings, iPhone and iPad open Settings, and a rough location shows the steps above. Other riders see Approximate Location in the riders list under a rider whose phone shares only a rough spot, so nobody goes looking for them a mile away. Ride Bubble leaves out the distance a rough location could be off by, so a rider beside you isn't called separated.

title: Navigate Offroad and Map Your Own Trails
summary: Use Map Mode (called Navigate before 2.0) as your offroad map, map your own trails, share them with every rider, rate trails and measure distances.
headings: Name a Spot While You Record
Map a Custom Trail or Measure a Distance
Share a Trail With Every Rider
When Riders Rate a Trail as Inaccurate
Use a Trail for a Group Ride
text: Map Mode (called Navigate before version 2.0) is OnMyLead's offroad map for when you're not on a group ride. It has the same trails and roads as the rest of the app, shows where you are, and lets you map your own trails by drawing or recording them, keep them on your phone or share them with every rider. Free accounts get 8 hours of Map Mode a month, with the standard map and following trails. The clock never runs while you're sharing your location on a group ride, and Pro has no limit. Map layers, drawing, recording, saving, rating and sharing trails, Track Line, named spots and planning group rides on your trails are part of OnMyLead Pro. On a Free account, the top of Map Mode shows your time left, like Free Map Mode: 5 h 20 m Left This Month . The clock only runs while Map Mode is on your screen. When the month's time is used up, Map Mode offers See OnMyLead Pro and opens again at the start of the next month. See Free and Pro. Open Map Mode From any tab, tap the blue Map Mode button in the middle of the bar at the bottom of the screen. On a tablet, and on onmylead.com on a computer, it's in the menu down the left edge, under Find . On Home, tap Open Map Mode (or the little map) on the Map Mode card. To map a trail that isn't marked anywhere, tap Map a Custom Trail on the same card. Map Mode opens on the Draw tab. Or on the You tab, tap Map Mode under On the Trail . At the bottom of the map are three tabs: Explore , Record and Draw . Swipe the panel down to see more of the map, and up to bring it back. Map Mode opens on where you are, close enough to see the trails. If your phone is still finding your location (say, right after you turn it on), the map moves to you as soon as it does, unless you've already moved the map yourself. For the whole screen, tap Full Map on the panel's grab bar. A slim bar keeps your speed (or the miles left on a trail you're following, or the length you're measuring, with Undo ), a red Rec while you record, and Center on Me stays. Tap Controls , or swipe the bar up, to bring everything back. See Full Map. On a tablet, the panel sits beside the map in landscape, and floats over the corner of the map in portrait. Explore Explore shows your speed big on the left, with the map centered on you. Use the round Map Settings button for Satellite or Topo and trail lines (see Map Layers and Trails), the search box to jump to a place, and the round Center on Me button to center on you again. Tap any line to see what it is. Next to your speed are four readings: Elevation , in feet. Heading , the way you're facing, such as NE 62° . While you're moving it comes from GPS. When you stop, it comes from your phone's compass. The website shows it only while you're moving. Trip , the miles you've covered since you last reset it, like the trip meter on a dash. Moving , how long you've been moving on this trip (minutes, then hours and minutes). To start a new trip, press and hold Trip . Trip and Moving only count while Map Mode is open, and they're kept on your phone only. When you follow a trail, the big number shows the miles left, and Speed moves into the readings in place of Moving . Under the readings, the Tilt tile shows your Roll and Pitch , turning amber, then red, near your limits. Until you calibrate the tilt meter it says Calibrate Tilt . Tap it for the full tilt meter. See Use the Tilt Meter and Crash Alert. The Map Follows You With Follow Me on (it is unless you turn it off), the map moves with you so your dot stays in view, and while you're moving your dot has a white arrow pointing the way you're heading. The Follow Me button sits just left of Center on Me and shows Following . To look around, drag or pinch the map. It pauses (the button shows Paused ) until you tap it or Center on Me again. The map also holds still while the Measure tab is open, and when you jump to a place with search. Tap Following to turn Follow Me off; the map then stays where you put it, even while you record. title: Use Battery Saver
summary: Choose how often your phone sends your location while you share, to make the battery last longer on long days.
text: Sharing your location keeps the GPS on and sends your position to your group. Battery Saver lets you trade how often your group sees you move for a longer-lasting battery. It starts on Best Accuracy , which is what we recommend whenever you can charge your phone. The Three Settings Setting Your dot updates about every What your group notices --- --- --- Best Accuracy (Recommended) 15 seconds or 25 m (80 ft) Your dot follows you closely. Best for following the leader and for finding someone who stopped. Balanced 30 seconds or 75 m (250 ft) Your dot can trail up to 30 seconds behind you. Max Battery Saver 45 seconds or 200 m (650 ft) Your dot can trail up to 45 seconds behind you and be off by up to about 100 m (330 ft). For multi-day trips with no way to charge. On every setting, a phone that is parked still checks in often enough that your group sees you as live, not as No Signal . Taps like Need Help and EMERGENCY always send right away. Battery Saver also slows Ride Mode's own work on your phone: your blue dot on the route moves in bigger steps, and the backup check for other riders runs less often. Other riders still appear the moment their phones send. Change the Setting Go to the You tab and tap Battery Saver . You can also tap Change next to Battery Saver at the bottom of Share My Location . Tap the setting you want. If you picked Balanced or Max Battery Saver , the app tells you what your group loses and asks you to confirm. Tap Use Balanced or Use Max Battery Saver , or Keep Current to leave it. The change takes effect right away, even in the middle of a share. While you're on Balanced or Max Battery Saver, the sharing banner in Ride Mode shows the setting's name, and Switch Back to Best Accuracy is at the top of the Battery Saver screen. Battery Saver is set on each phone or tablet separately, and other riders aren't told which setting you picked. Other Ways to Save Battery Download an offline map before you lose service, so the phone isn't searching for map tiles. Stop sharing when you don't need to. See Share Your Location. Keep the phone on a charger or a 12V outlet on long rides.

title: Your Home Screen
summary: What's on the Rides tab from version 2.0. Join, create and find rides, Map Mode, your group, public rides near you, your feed, badges and toolkit.
text: The Rides tab is your home screen. It puts the three things riders do most at the top (join, create and find a ride), then Map Mode, events, your rides, your crew and what your friends have been up to. Join a Ride, Create a Ride, Find a Ride, Events and Map Mode all fit on the first screen, without scrolling, in that order. Scroll down for your rides, your crew and what your friends have been up to. On small phones like the iPhone SE, the greeting line is left out to make room. At the Top Good morning , Good afternoon or Good evening with your ride name. When friends are out riding, a line under it says how many. Tap it for Who's Riding. The flag shows the language the app is in (for example 🇺🇸 EN). Tap it to pick another. It shows when you're signed out too. See Change the App's Language. The bell opens your notifications, with a red number for new ones. See See and Clear Your Notifications. Your picture (or your first letter) opens the You tab. Join, Create and Find Join a Ride , the big red card: type the invite code from the ride leader and tap Join . You can also open a ride's link or scan its QR code with your phone's camera. Joining is Unlimited on every plan. See Join a Ride. Create a Ride , the dark card with the red flag under Join: the label says how many rides you have left this month on Free ( 1 Left This Month , or None Left This Month ), or Unlimited on Pro and during the trial. Tap the label on Free to see what Pro adds. See Create a Ride and Free and Pro. Find a Ride : opens the map of public rides. The label shows how many are coming up near you, like 12 Within 500 mi . See Find a Ride. When one of your rides is live, a card says Your ride is live. Tap to open Ride Mode . Events Right under Create a Ride and Find a Ride , the gold Events card opens the Events area: rallies, poker runs and ride weekends. It shows your next event (one you host or said you're going to), or else the next public event near you, and how many are coming up. See Events. Map Mode Your offroad map for when you're not on a group ride. It's the blue card under Events . Open Map Mode opens Map Mode. The blue Map Mode button in the tab bar opens it too, from any tab. Map a Custom Trail opens Map Mode ready to draw a trail that isn't marked on any map. Track Line draws where you've been, a new colour each day: today red, yesterday blue, older days gold. The Track Line switch is the small switch in the top corner of the Map Mode card. Tap it to turn the line on or off. See Navigate Offroad and Map Your Own Trails. Your Rides Ride Invites : rides your riding groups invited you to. Your Next Ride : the soonest ride you're on. If you're on more than one, tap All to see them all. Past Rides : rides that ended. Free shows your last few; see Free and Pro. Swipe a ride left to delete it (if you organize it) or leave it. On onmylead.com, click Delete or Leave at the end of the row. The app always asks first. Your Group Your riding group with the newest group chat message (or your first group), with how many riders are in it, how many of them are out riding now, and the newest message. Group Chat opens the group's chat. Plan a Group Ride starts a new ride with that group already picked to invite. Creating rides follows your plan's ride limit. Tap the group's name for its page. With more than one group, All opens the Groups tab. The card shows the group's photo next to its name, if the rider who made the group added one, or the group's initials. See Add a Group Photo. No group yet? Ride With the Same Crew? takes you to the Groups tab. See Riding Groups. Public Rides Near You Upcoming public rides, nearest first, as cards you swipe sideways. Each shows how far away its meeting area is, the date and time, and the area. Tap one to open it. To change how far it looks, tap the distance chip ( Within 500 mi at first) and pick 50 mi , 100 mi , 250 mi , 500 mi , 1,000 mi or Anywhere , then Done . Your phone remembers it. title: Create a Ride on the Website
summary: Plan a ride on onmylead.com from your computer, drop the meeting point on a map, and find it in the app on your phone as soon as you save.
headings: Create a Ride on the Web
Draw the Route on the Web
text: You can plan a ride on the big screen at onmylead.com. It's the same ride as one made in the app: the ride, its route and its stops show up in the OnMyLead app on your phone or tablet as soon as you save. Ride Mode and live tracking stay in the app. Using OnMyLead on the website is a Pro feature. See Free and Pro. On a Free account, the website still lets you join a ride, open your rides and follow the leader in Ride Mode. Create a Ride on the Web Go to onmylead.com and click Create a Ride on the Web . Sign in with your OnMyLead account if you aren't already. You go straight to Create a Ride after signing in. Pick Public or Private under What Kind of Ride? Fill in the Ride Name , the day under When , and the Meet At time. Click Calendar , then type the date (such as 06/12/2027) in Type a Date or click it on the calendar. Click the month's name to jump to another year and month. Any day from today up to three years out works. For Meet At , click the time, then click AM or PM , the hour and the minute; no typing needed. You can also press Tab to move between them and Enter to pick. Set the Meeting Point : type a park, trailhead, town or address in Search a Place or Address (just above the map) and pick it, or click the satellite map to drop the pin, then drag the pin to fine-tune it. You can also use your location or type coordinates, and the pin moves there. From 2.1 the meeting-point map is Mapbox's satellite map, the same one the app uses, and it opens near where you are if the browser shares your location. Clicking and dragging work the same. Under The Route , pick Mapped or Freeride . Fill in anything else you want, then click Create Public Ride or Create Private Ride . The rest of the form works the same as in the app. See Create a Ride for every option. Draw the Route on the Web If you picked Mapped , the route builder opens after you create the ride. Click along the trail and the route follows it. Drawing a route is free. Importing a GPX file is a Pro feature. See Build a Route and Free and Pro. To find a trailhead or park by name while you draw, click Search at the top of the map and pick a result. The map jumps there. You can also add numbered planned stops for fuel, lunch or camp. See Waypoints and Planned Stops. The waypoints map has the same Search , so you can jump to a place before you click to drop a stop. Change It Later Open the ride on onmylead.com and click Edit Ride Details in the You're Organizing card to change the name, day, time, meeting point (click the map to move the pin) and the rest. See Edit, Cancel or Delete a Ride. Share It After saving, your ride page shows the invite code, a QR code and share buttons, the same as in the app. See Invite Riders. Free accounts create one ride each month, whether on the website or in the app. See Free and Pro. When someone opens a ride link on a computer, the page shows the ride's QR code. They can scan it with their phone's camera to open the ride on their phone. Stuck while planning? Click Help at the top of onmylead.com to open these guides.

summary: Quick answers about free rides, the Pro Trial, privacy, editing rides, iPhone, iPad and Android, updates, and the website.

text: Is OnMyLead Free? Yes. Free accounts create one ride each calendar month and can join as many rides as they like, and the safety features are always free. OnMyLead Pro adds unlimited rides and more. From version 2.0, Free also includes 8 hours of Map Mode a month, and joining a ride and following the leader stay free and unlimited on every device. Using OnMyLead on an iPad, an Android tablet or the website, and extras like map layers, drawing routes, waypoints and directions, are part of Pro. I Deleted the Ride I Made This Month. Can I Make Another on Free? No. A ride counts when it's created, so cancelling or deleting it doesn't give it back, and copying a ride or using Ride Again counts as a new ride. Your next free ride opens on the 1st of next month (UTC). Will I Be Charged When My Pro Trial Ends? No. The Pro Trial needs no payment and never turns into a paid subscription. Your account moves to Free, and your rides, routes, groups and maps stay. My Pro Trial Ended Mid-Month and I Can't Create a Ride. Why? Rides you created during the trial count toward that month's one free ride. Can I Buy Pro or Use a Promo Code on the Website? No. Subscribing, Restore Purchases and promo codes work only in the app on your phone or tablet. Pro bought in the app also works when you sign in on the website. Does Deleting My Account Cancel My Pro Subscription? No. Apple bills Pro, so also cancel it in your Apple subscriptions so you aren't billed again. See Manage Your Subscription. If you bought Pro on Android, Google Play bills it: cancel it in Google Play too. Can I Change My Ride's Time or Meeting Point? Yes, until the ride goes live. On the ride page, tap Edit Ride Details in the You're Organizing card, change the day, time or meeting point and save. Everyone on the ride gets a notification, and the ride page shows what changed. See Edit, Cancel or Delete a Ride. My Ride Still Says Live. How Do I End It? Rides don't end on their own. The organizer taps End Ride for Everyone on the ride page. Ending a ride stops everyone's location sharing for that ride. Why Can't I See the Exact Meeting Spot? Only riders who have joined see it. Before you join, you see the general area, within about a mile. See Privacy. Why Isn't My Ride Showing on Find? Find lists only public rides that are upcoming or live. Private rides never appear there, and rides drop off a few hours after their meeting time. See Find a Ride. Why Do Other Riders See Me as "Rider"? You haven't picked a ride name yet. Tap Pick Your Ride Name on the Rides tab, or your name at the top of You . See Your Ride Name and Profile. Does "Until I Turn It Off" Sharing Ever End? Only when you stop it. Sharing with chosen riders or a family link set to Until I Turn It Off has no time limit: tap the You tab, then Share My Location , then Stop Sharing . A ride share set to Until I Turn It Off also ends when the ride ends or you leave it. If you'd rather it end on its own, tap Pick an End Date instead. See Share Your Location. Does Live Tracking Work With No Cell Service? Yes, for riders close to you. With no service, OnMyLead phones on the same ride pass spots, status taps, EMERGENCY and Ride Mode messages to each other over Bluetooth, about 100 to 300 feet between phones in the open, and each phone passes them along the group, up to six phones down the line. Riders out of Bluetooth range show where they were last seen, and the first phone to get signal sends everything it heard to OnMyLead. Seeing riders, sharing your spot and messages over Bluetooth are part of OnMyLead Pro (every new account gets 30 days free); on every plan your phone passes things along and EMERGENCY goes out over Bluetooth. It's on by default. See Share With Nearby Riders With No Service, and download the ride's offline map before you go. Why Does the App Ask Me to Agree to a Safety Agreement?
