title: Import a GPX Route
summary: Bring in a track from Gaia, onX or any GPX file and use it as your ride's route. A Pro feature.
text: Already have the trail you want to ride as a track in another app? Export it as a GPX file and import it as your ride's route. Riders see it in Ride Mode just like a route drawn in OnMyLead. This is a Pro feature. See Free and Pro. Drawing a route on the map stays free: see Draw a Route. On the Free plan, the buttons that need Pro carry a small gold Pro tag, so you know before you tap. Tapping one shows what Pro includes. During your Pro Trial and on Pro there are no tags. Import a File You need to be the ride's organizer or a co-organizer. Open the ride, tap the Map tab, and tap Build the Route (or Edit Route ). Tap Import GPX . Pick the GPX file. On iPhone it opens your Files, so save the file there first. Check the track on the map. The panel shows its miles and how many track points it has. Tap Save Route . If you're on the Free plan, tapping Import GPX shows what Pro includes instead of opening the file picker. A trail you recorded or saved in Navigate doesn't need a GPX file: tap Use One of My Trails instead. That's also a Pro feature. What Gets Imported If the file has a track, the track is used. If it has no track, its route is used. If it has neither, its waypoints are joined in order. The track's name from the file is kept with the route. Very long tracks are simplified a little so they load and draw quickly on every rider's phone. Waypoints inside a GPX file aren't added as OnMyLead waypoints. To mark camp, fuel or a planned stop, see Waypoints and Planned Stops. Change an Imported Route An imported track is shown as it is, so you can't drag or add points to it. To use a different file, tap Clear , then Import GPX again. To draw your own instead, tap Clear and start tapping the map. Tapping a line on an imported route's map shows that trail's name and who can ride it. See Map Layers and Trails. GPX import works with Pro from either store: the App Store on iPhone and iPad, or Google Play on Android. If Your Pro Plan Ends A route you already imported stays on the ride. Importing a new GPX file needs Pro. On the Website Import GPX works the same way in the website's route builder. Pick the file from your computer. Troubleshooting "That file is not a GPX file." Go back to the other app, export the track as GPX (not KML or another format) and try again. "That GPX file has no track in it." The file doesn't have at least two points to draw. Export the track itself, not just a single waypoint.

title: Join a Ride
summary: Join with an invite link, a QR code or a code, or from Find. Learn what public and private rides show before and after you join.
headings: Rides That Are Part of an Event
text: Joining a ride is free, with no limit on how many rides you join. You need a free OnMyLead account. Join With a Link Tap the ride link someone sent you. If you have OnMyLead on your phone or tablet, the ride opens in the app. If not, it opens the ride's page on onmylead.com, with a button to get the app from the App Store or Google Play. Tap Join Ride . If you aren't signed in, the button says Sign In to Join . See Sign In. Join With a Code On the Rides tab, type the invite code in the Join a Ride card at the top, for example 7F3A9C21. Tap Join . On the ride page, tap Join Ride . Some organizers pick their own code, like MOAB-2026. Type it with the dashes. Capital or small letters both work. Join With a QR Code Point your phone's camera at the ride's QR code and tap the link that appears. See QR Codes. Join From Find Public rides are listed on the Find tab. Open one and tap Join Ride . See Find a Ride. Join From a Group Invite When someone invites your riding group, you get a notification and the ride shows under Ride Invites on the Rides tab. Tap the ride. In the You're Invited card, tap Join Ride , or No Thanks to turn it down. You don't wait for approval when you're invited. If you say no thanks, you can still join later with the ride's link or code. On a ride where the organizer approves riders, you then ask to join like anyone else. Public and Private Rides Public rides can be found on the Find tab, and anyone can open their page. Private rides (marked Private, Invite Only ) never show in Find. You need the link, QR code or invite code to see one. Before you join either kind, the ride page shows the name, time, general area and details. After you join, you also see: The exact meeting point, and directions to it The organizer's instructions for joined riders The route and planned stops Who's going The ride chat After You Join The ride shows under Your Rides on the Rides tab. On the ride page you'll find Details , Map , Riders and Chat sections. When you get to the meeting spot, tap I'm Here and Ready to check in. See Check In. When the organizer starts the ride, tap Enter Ride Mode . See Ride Mode. If the ride is full, you go on the waitlist. If the organizer approves riders, you wait for them to say yes. See Approvals and the Waitlist. Leave a Ride Open the ride page. Leave Ride is the red-outlined button at the bottom, whichever section you're on (on a tablet, it's at the bottom of the left column). Tap Leave Ride . A box tells you what happens; tap Leave Ride again to confirm, or Stay . In Ride Mode, tap Together (or Separated ) at the top to open Riders , and Leave Ride is under the list. On a tablet it's at the bottom of the Riders sidebar. You go back to the Rides tab when you've left. Leaving always stops your phone sharing your location for that ride, whether or not the ride has started. Organized the ride? See Leave a Ride You Organize. Or, on the Rides tab, swipe left on the ride and tap Leave (on onmylead.com, click Leave at the end of the ride's row). Your spot opens up for someone else. You can rejoin with the ride's link or code if there's room. If the ride is live, leaving also stops sharing your location with the group. You can't join a ride that has ended or been cancelled. Rides That Are Part of an Event A ride that belongs to an event shows Part of and the event's name at the top of its page; tap it to see the event's agenda and its other rides. You can also join a ride from the event's Group Rides with See Ride and Join . See Events.

title: Send a Status or Quick Reply
summary: Tell the whole group what's happening with one tap, see who got it, and take it back if you tapped by mistake.
headings: When Another Rider Taps a Status
text: Ride Mode has big buttons so you can tell the group what's going on without typing. Every rider on the ride sees your tap, and you can see whose phone has it. Don't use your phone while you're moving. Pull over first, then tap. Typing your own message and saving your own quick replies are Pro features. See Free and Pro. On a Free account, the Message button carries a Pro tag. The status buttons, Need Help, EMERGENCY and Mechanical Issue stay free. Quick Replies Quick replies send a short message to the group. They also show in the ride chat. On My Way , Need a Minute and All Good sit on the bottom panel. Tap More for Running Late , Beverage Break and every status. On My Way Running Late Need a Minute All Good Beverage Break Type Your Own Message Need to say something the buttons don't cover, like "Gas stop at the next town"? Pull over first, then: Tap Message at the top left of the bottom panel (across from Full Map ). Type your message. It's one line of up to 120 characters, and the counter shows how many are left. Tap Send to Everyone , or the send key on your keyboard. It goes out just like a quick reply: the same Sending and Sent to the Group card with a light for each rider, Cancel to take it back, and it waits for signal if you have none. Riders get a notification titled with your name and the message, and it shows in the ride chat in italics. To put the keyboard away without sending, tap Done above it on iPhone and iPad, use the back key on Android, or swipe the sheet down. My Quick Replies Check Save as One of My Quick Replies before you send, and the message is kept on this phone or tablet. Next time, tap Message and tap it under My Quick Replies to send it in one tap. You can keep up to 6; saving a seventh drops the oldest. Tap Edit , then a reply, to remove it. Saved replies stay on the device you saved them on. On a tablet the message sheet opens as a card in the middle of the screen. Status Buttons Tap More on the bottom panel to open Tell the Group . It has every quick reply, then your status, in two groups: On the Move ( OK and Stopped ) and Trouble ( Need Fuel , Mechanical Issue , Flat Tire , Stuck , Lost and Need Help ). Regroup Here (for organizers and leaders) and EMERGENCY are at the bottom. Tap one to send it; the sheet closes so you see the Sending card. Swipe the sheet down or tap Done to close it without sending. The statuses: OK Stopped Need Fuel Mechanical Issue Flat Tire Stuck Lost Need Help EMERGENCY Need Help sends right away and shows in red for the group. EMERGENCY asks you to confirm first. See Emergencies and Safety. An EMERGENCY also sounds a siren on every other rider's phone until they silence it. See Hear the Emergency Siren. In Full Map, the quick replies and status buttons are tucked away and only EMERGENCY stays on screen. Tap Controls , or swipe the bar up, to bring the rest back. Send a Status In Ride Mode, tap a quick reply or a status button. A card appears above the buttons. It says Sending , then Sent to the Group . Watch the row of lights on the card, one per rider, with their first initial: A solid green light means that rider's app has it. A blue ring means a notification went to their phone, but their app hasn't shown it yet. An empty light means it hasn't reached them yet. Under the headline, the card spells it out, for example "Seen by Sam and Alex. 2 notified by push." or "All 5 riders got it." Tap ✕ to hide the card. It also goes away on its own after 10 minutes. A blue ring also means a nearby rider's phone got it over Bluetooth, and the line says Reached Sam over Bluetooth until it shows on their screen. See Share With Nearby Riders With No Service. Take It Back Tapped the wrong button? Tap Cancel on the card. The status or quick reply is taken back for everyone, the group is told to ignore it, and the notification they got is replaced with one saying you cancelled it. With No Signal If your tap can't go out within a few seconds, the card says Is Waiting for Signal . Your

title: Share a Family Link
summary: Send a read-only web link so family at home can see where you are, without the app or an account. It stops working when sharing ends.
text: A family link is a web link you can text to someone at home. They open it in any web browser, with no app and no account, and see your last known location and when sharing ends. It's free on every plan. Send a Family Link Tap the You tab. Under On the Trail , tap Share My Location . Turn on Family Link . Under For How Long , pick how long to share, or tap Pick an End Date to choose a day and time. If you pick Until I Turn It Off , tap Share to confirm. Your phone's share sheet opens with a message like "Follow my location until 5:30 PM" (or just "Follow my location" when you picked Until I Turn It Off ) and the link. Pick Messages, or any app, and send it. You can pick riders under Who Can See You at the same time, or send just the family link. What They See The link opens a simple page with: Your ride name. Last update: when your phone last sent its location. Sharing ends: when the link stops working, with the date for a share that runs past today. For a share set to Until I Turn It Off , Sharing ends says When they turn it off . Open in Maps: opens your last location in Google Maps. The page checks for a new location every 30 seconds. If your phone hasn't sent a location yet, it says No location received yet. The page shows your last update, not a guaranteed live position. With no service on the trail, Last update stays at the last time your phone got through. Tell your family what time you expect to be back, and what to do if they don't hear from you. Stop or Extend the Link The family link lasts exactly as long as the share it belongs to. Tap the You tab, then Share My Location . Find the card that says Includes a family link . Tap Add 1 Hour to keep it going, or Stop Sharing to end it now. Once the share ends, the link shows No Longer Shared and This location link has ended. Your location can't be seen from it again. Anyone who has the link can see your location until the share ends, so only send it to people you trust.

title: Use Your Riding Group's Chat
summary: Talk with your whole riding group between rides, link a message to a ride, mute a busy group and clear messages.
text: Every riding group has its own chat: a group text for everyone in the group. Use it to plan the next ride or talk about the last one. It's separate from ride chat, which is for the riders on one ride. Group chat is free for everyone in the group. Only the riders in the group can read it or post in it. Open the Chat Tap the Groups tab. Tap the newest message under a group, or open the group and tap Group Chat . Groups with messages you haven't read show a red count. Send a Message Type in the box at the bottom. Tap the send button. Your message shows Sending , then Sent . If it can't go through, for example with no signal, it shows Not Sent . Tap Retry to send it again, or Remove to drop it. Messages can be up to 500 characters. If you send a lot of messages in a row, the app asks you to wait a minute. Talk About a Ride You can tie a message to one of your rides, so everyone knows which ride you mean. Tap About a Ride above the message box. Under Which Ride Is This About? , pick the ride. Type your message and send it. The list shows rides you've joined that are happening now, coming up, or ended in the last 30 days. To send without a ride, tap the ride's name above the message box to remove it. Rides the group has talked about show in a strip at the top of the chat. Tap a ride to see only the talk about it, and tap Open the Ride to go to its page. Tap All Talk to see every message again. Mute a Group Tap Mute at the top of the chat to stop notifications from that group. Tap Unmute to turn them back on. To turn off notifications for all your groups' chats, switch off Riding Group Chat in Notification Settings. Clear a Message Your own message: press and hold it, then confirm Clear . It disappears for everyone, and this can't be undone. If you run the group: press and hold anyone's message and tap Clear . Report or Block a Rider Press and hold someone else's message, then tap Report Rider or Block Rider . Messages from riders you've blocked aren't shown to you. See Report and Block.

title: Your Free 30-Day Pro Trial
summary: Every new account gets 30 days of OnMyLead Pro with no payment, and it never turns into a paid subscription on its own.
headings: See How Many Days Are Left
text: When you make a new OnMyLead account, you get 30 days of OnMyLead Pro for free. It starts on its own. There's nothing to sign up for and no payment details to enter. You're never charged when the trial ends. It does not turn into a paid subscription. Your account simply moves to Free unless you choose to subscribe. A Fresh Trial With 2.1 OnMyLead 2.1 makes a few more things Pro: Bluetooth Sharing with no service, CarPlay, customizing your dot and group photos. So nobody loses anything the day it arrives, every rider who doesn't have Pro gets a fresh 30-day Pro trial when 2.1 comes out, even if you already had a trial or are partway through one. Riders who subscribe, or have Pro from OnMyLead, keep it as before. While a trial runs, Home shows Your Pro Trial Runs Until and the date. Close it with the × ; it comes back only if your trial's end date changes. See How Many Days Are Left On the You tab, under Settings , tap Subscription . Your Plan shows Pro Trial with the days remaining, the date it ends, and a row of 30 marks that fills in as the days go by. The trial is the same on Android. It belongs to your account, not your phone, so it shows the same days left on every device you sign in to. Trial Reminders OnMyLead reminds you a week, 3 days and a day before your trial ends, and again when it ends. To turn off the notifications, switch off Badges and Pro Trial in Notification Settings. That also stops badge notifications and the notice when a trail you shared is hidden. The same reminders come by email too. Switch off Email Me Too to stop the emails. When the Trial Ends Your account moves to Free. Nothing you made during the trial is deleted: Your rides, routes, groups and downloaded maps stay yours. New Pro actions, like downloading another map area or importing a GPX file, need Pro again. Free accounts create one ride a month. Rides you created earlier in the same month, during the trial, count toward that month. See Free and Pro for exactly what changes. Keep Pro After the Trial On the You tab, under Settings , tap Subscription . Tap Keep Pro After the Trial . Choose Annual or Monthly . Tap the Subscribe for button under the plans and confirm with Apple. Apple charges you when you confirm, and your paid subscription starts right away. See Subscribe to Pro. Good to Know Each account gets one trial when it's made, plus the 2.1 trial above. The trial is part of OnMyLead, not an Apple free trial, so it doesn't show in your Apple subscriptions.

title: Your Ride Name and Profile
summary: Pick the ride name other riders see on the map, the rider list and in chat, and choose whether to show your Apple, Google or Facebook profile.
headings: Pick or Change Your Ride Name
Where Your Name Comes From at First
Show Your Apple, Google or Facebook Profile
text: Your ride name is how the group knows you. It shows on the group map, the rider list and in ride chat. A nickname works fine. Under your name on the You tab you also see your rank and badges. See Earn Badges and Ranks. The same screen also has your Profile Picture . See Add a Profile Picture. The screen is called Your Name and Picture . Pick or Change Your Ride Name Go to the You tab and tap your name at the top. If you haven't picked one yet, it says Pick Your Ride Name . You can also tap Pick Your Ride Name on the Rides tab. Type your name in Ride Name . Check the preview at the top. It shows your pin on the map and a chat line, the way the group sees you. Tap Save Name . The button changes to Name Saved . Until you pick a name, other riders see you as Rider. Keep it to 24 characters or fewer so it fits on the map. Extra spaces are tidied up when you save. Where Your Name Comes From at First If you created your account with your name, or signed in with Apple, Google or Facebook, your ride name may already be filled in from that. You can change it any time. Show Your Apple, Google or Facebook Profile If you signed in with Apple, Google or Facebook, you can let the riders you ride with see that account's name and photo. It helps people recognize who joined. Go to the You tab. Under Account , find Show My Google Profile (or Show My Apple Profile or Show My Facebook Profile , depending on how you signed in). Turn the switch on. When it's on, your photo replaces your initial, and a line like "Your Name on Google" shows under your ride name in a ride's rider list and in your riding groups. When it's off, nobody else sees it. It's off until you turn it on. Who Can See It Only riders who have been on a ride with you or share a riding group with you. Never strangers browsing public rides. Never someone you've blocked, or who has blocked you. The name and photo come from the account you signed in with, and the app keeps them up to date each time you open the You tab. You can only turn the setting on or off. If you signed in with email only, this setting doesn't appear. Your Email Under Account on the You tab, Email shows the email on your account. Only you see it.

title: Add a Profile Picture
summary: Take or choose a photo so riders know who's who. It shows next to your name in rider lists, chat, Messages, Friends and Out Riding.
text: Add a profile picture so the riders you meet know who's who. It shows in place of your initial wherever riders see you: the rider list on a ride page (who's going) and the riders in your riding groups ride chat and group chat Messages and your conversations Friends and Out Riding your name at the top of the You tab Until you add one, riders see your initial, the same as before. Riders on the live ride map still show as colored dots, so the leader, tail gunner and anyone who stopped sharing stay easy to spot. Add or Change Your Picture Go to the You tab and tap your name at the top. Under Profile Picture , tap Take Photo to use the camera, or Choose Photo to pick one from your photo library. Move and zoom the photo so your face (or your machine) sits in the square, then tap Choose (or the check mark). The picture saves straight away and the screen says Picture saved . To change it, do the same again: the button says Choose New Photo . Your old picture is replaced. The first time, the app asks to use your camera or your photos. Only the photo you pick is uploaded. If you said no, turn access back on in your device's Settings app under OnMyLead. Every picture is cropped square and made smaller before it's uploaded, so it loads quickly even on one bar of signal. Pictures are kept under 200 KB, and anyone can tap a rider's picture to see it full size. On the Website On onmylead.com, tap your name on the You page, then Choose Photo . Your browser opens its file chooser; on a phone it also offers the camera. The picture is cropped to the middle square for you. Remove Your Picture Go to the You tab and tap your name at the top. Under Profile Picture , tap Remove , then Remove again to confirm. Riders see your initial again. Who Can See It Your picture follows the same rule as your ride name: riders who are signed in to OnMyLead see it next to your name. OnMyLead never shows it to people who aren't signed in, and its web address is a long random one that only signed-in riders are given. Like any photo, someone who has that address could still pass it on. It never shows where you are. Your Apple, Google or Facebook photo is separate. It only shows if you turn on Show My Google Profile (or Apple or Facebook), and your uploaded picture comes first when you have both. See Your Ride Name and Profile. Keep It Friendly Pictures that are offensive or break the rules can be removed by the OnMyLead team. You can upload a new one afterwards. If you see a picture that shouldn't be there, report the rider and pick Inappropriate Photo . See Report or Block a Rider. When you delete your account, your picture is deleted with it.

title: Earn Badges and Ranks
summary: Earn Bronze, Silver and Gold badges for leading, riding, miles and trails, see your rank on the You tab, and spot other riders' top badge.
text: Badges show what you have done on OnMyLead. Each badge has three levels, Bronze , Silver and Gold , and the levels you earn add up to your rank. The Badges Badge What earns it Bronze Silver Gold --- --- --- --- --- Trail Boss Lead group rides 1 ride 10 rides 25 rides Tail Gunner Ride at the rear as tail gunner 1 ride 10 rides 25 rides Crew Rider Ride with a group 1 ride 10 rides 50 rides Mile Eater Miles on your rides 100 miles 1,000 miles 5,000 miles Trailblazer Share trails you mapped with every rider 1 trail 5 trails 20 trails Mapmaker Your shared trails rated accurate by other riders 1 trail 5 trails 20 trails Trail Scout Rate trails for accuracy 5 trails 25 trails 100 trails Leading counts when you are the ride's leader as it ends: the organizer, or the rider the organizer made Leader or handed the lead to. See Leader, Sweep and Tail Gunner. How a Ride Counts A ride counts once it ends. It counts for you when your own location track on that ride covers at least half a mile, so share your location in Ride Mode while you ride. Trail Boss , Tail Gunner and Crew Rider also need at least two riders with a track, so a ride you end on your own doesn't count toward them. Your miles on it still do. Miles come from your own track, with GPS jumps and time stopped left out, the same way as the ride summary. Rough locations, GPS bounces and time with your location off are left out of your miles too, the same as the ride summary. No signal on the trail? Your track uploads when your phone gets service again, and the ride counts then. Badges are worked out by OnMyLead's server from what you really ride, so nobody can add one by hand. Once you earn a badge, you keep it. Brand Ambassador and OnMyLead Founder OnMyLead gives two special badges. They have no Bronze, Silver or Gold, you can't earn them by riding, and they don't count toward your rank. Badge Who has it Looks like --- --- --- OnMyLead Founder The rider who started OnMyLead A red patch with a flag planted on a summit Brand Ambassador Riders who represent OnMyLead A blue patch with the OnMyLead mountains and red arrow If OnMyLead gives you one: You get a notification, for example You're an OnMyLead Brand Ambassador . It shows at the top of Badges and first in the badge row on the You tab. It shows beside your name instead of your top riding badge, and on the Feed and your profile. Your Rank Every level you earn counts once toward your rank. There are 21 levels in all. Rank Levels earned --- --- Rookie 0 Rider 1 Veteran 4 Expert 9 Legend 15 See Your Badges Go to the You tab. Under your name you see your rank and a row of all seven badges. Earned badges are in their Bronze, Silver or Gold color; the rest are outlines. Tap the row to open Badges . Each badge shows its level, what earns it and how far you are from the next level, for example 4 of 10 rides led for Silver . A badge you just earned is marked New until you open Badges . On a tablet, Badges shows two columns in portrait and three in landscape. When You Earn a Badge You get a notification, for example New Badge: Trail Boss Silver . Tap it to open Badges . To turn these off, switch off Badges and Pro Trial in Notification Settings. Other Riders' Badges Each rider's top badge shows as a small patch beside their name in the ride's Going list, the Riders list in Ride Mode and the riders list beside the map on a tablet. Other riders see your badges and rank level, never your exact ride count or miles. The Leaderboard See how your badge levels compare with other riders, everywhere or in your country and state, from Leaderboard on Badges . See See the Badge Leaderboard.

title: See and Clear Your Notifications
summary: The bell on the Rides tab lists the notifications OnMyLead sent you in the last 30 days. Open them, mark them read, or clear one or all.
text: Missed a notification, or swiped one away too soon? OnMyLead keeps the ones it sent you, so you can find them again and clear them when you're done. Open Your Notifications Tap the bell at the top right of the Rides tab. A red number on the bell shows how many are new. Notifications are listed newest first under Today , Yesterday and Earlier . Each one has a colored icon, so a rider alert like Need Help stands out from chat and ride changes. New ones have a dot. Several messages from the same chat are kept together in one line, with +2 More (or however many) under the latest message, so a busy chat doesn't bury anything else. Open One Tap a notification to go straight to what it's about, the same as tapping it on your lock screen: Ride Mode for a rider's status or a ride going live, the ride's chat for a message, Friends for a friend request, and so on. It's marked read. A new waypoint from the leader opens Ride Mode with that waypoint showing. To mark everything read without opening it, tap Mark All Read . Clear Notifications Clear one : swipe it to the left and tap Clear , or swipe all the way to clear it straight away. On onmylead.com, click the X on the right of the notification. Clear all : tap Clear All at the top, then Clear All again to confirm. Clearing in OnMyLead also clears the same notifications from your phone or tablet's own notification list, and Clear All resets the number on the OnMyLead app icon. What's Kept Every notification OnMyLead sent you: ride chat, announcements, status buttons, ride changes, new riders, invites, riding group chat, direct messages, friend requests, badges and Pro Trial reminders. What you turned off in Notification Settings isn't sent, so it isn't kept either. The same goes for quiet hours (except help alerts) and riders you blocked. If a rider cancels a status like Need Help , the cancellation replaces it. If someone deletes a chat message, it's removed here too. Notifications are kept for 30 days, up to the 100 newest. Ride reminders are set on your phone itself, so they don't appear in the list. Your notifications are private to you, and they're the same on every device you sign in on. On the Website The bell is on the Rides page at onmylead.com too, with the same list. It shows the notifications OnMyLead sent to the app on your phone or tablet, so if you haven't allowed notifications in the app, the list stays empty. Notification Settings To choose what you're told about, tap Notification Settings at the bottom of the list. See Notification Settings.

title: See Who's Out Riding Nearby
summary: Switch on Out Riding to see which riders are out near you right now, roughly how far away they are, and send them a message.
keywords: who's riding, friends nearby, out riding, park, weekend, direct message, dm, message a rider, inbox, messages, tablet
headings: Add a Rider as a Friend
text: Heading to a park for the weekend, or just out on the trail? Switch on Out Riding and OnMyLead shows you which other riders are out near you right now, like friends showing online in a game. You can message any of them. Out Riding is off until you switch it on, and other riders never see where you are. They see your ride name and roughly how far away you are, in whole miles. Switch On Out Riding Go to the Groups tab and tap Out Riding at the top. Under Who Can See Me , pick one: Riders I Know : only your friends, and riders you've been on a ride with or share a riding group with. This is the default. Everyone Nearby : also any other OnMyLead rider who is Out Riding near you and picked Everyone Nearby too. Under Turn Off After , pick 4 Hours , Today or This Weekend . If you like, type where you're riding under Where You're Riding (Optional) , like the park's name. Riders who can see you see it. Tap Go Out Riding . Allow location if your phone asks. The Out Riding card on the Groups tab turns green and shows who's out within 10 miles. OnMyLead only uses your location while the app is open to work out your rough area, and it keeps an area of about a mile, never your exact spot. Out Riding doesn't share your live location. For that, see Location Sharing. See Who's Out Near You While you're Out Riding, the Out Near You list shows each rider with roughly how far away they are (like Under a Mile or About 6 Miles ), where they said they're riding, and whether they're your friend or you've ridden with them. Friends are listed first. Tap 10 Mi , 25 Mi or 50 Mi to look farther. If you picked Everyone Nearby , switch between Riders I Know and Everyone Nearby to see only your riders or everyone. The rings at the top show the same riders by distance. They never show which way anyone is. Riders you know are green. You only see other riders while you're Out Riding yourself, and you only see riders outside your own riders while they can see you too. Message a Rider In the list, tap the blue message button next to a rider (or tap their dot on the rings). Type your message and tap send. Only the two of you see the conversation. You can start one with a friend, a rider you see Out Riding near you, or a rider you've ridden with. Until they reply, you can send up to 3 messages. Find all your conversations under Messages on the Groups tab or the Out Riding screen. In a conversation: Mute stops notifications for that conversation. ••• opens Add Friend , Report Rider , Block Rider and Delete Conversation . Deleting removes it from your Messages only; the other rider keeps their copy. Long press one of their messages to report it. The message goes with your report. Meeting up with someone new? Meet at a trailhead or staging area. Add a Rider as a Friend In the list, tap ••• next to a rider, then Add Friend . Once they accept, they see you whenever you're both Out Riding with Riders I Know , and you can message each other any time. See Add Friends. Change or Turn It Off Open Out Riding from the Groups tab. Tap Change to switch who can see you or where you're riding, or Turn Off to stop. Out Riding also turns itself off at the time you picked, or after 6 hours without opening OnMyLead. Opening the app while it's on updates your rough area. Blocking If you block a rider, neither of you sees the other in Out Riding, their messages are hidden from you, and they can't message you. They aren't told. See Report or Block a Rider. On a Tablet On a tablet in landscape, or a wide window, your Out Riding status is on the left and the rings and list are on the right. Conversations sit in a readable column in the middle of the screen.

title: Share With Nearby Riders With No Service
summary: With no cell service, riders on the same ride pass spots, status taps and messages to each other over Bluetooth, and phones pass them along the group.
text: When there's no cell service, OnMyLead phones on the same ride talk to each other over Bluetooth. Riders close to you keep moving on your map, and your status taps, quick replies and typed messages reach them, with no service at all. Each phone passes on what it hears, so the rider at the back can reach the front through the riders in between. It works on iPhone, iPad, Android phones and Android tablets, and they all work with each other. Seeing nearby riders, sharing your spot, and sending messages over Bluetooth are part of OnMyLead Pro, including the free Pro Trial. On every plan, your phone passes everything along for the group, and status taps go out and come in over Bluetooth, so EMERGENCY, Need Help and Crash Alerts always get through, and so does the I'm OK that ends one. On Free, the switch shows the Pro tag. With service, everything works as always on every plan. See Free and Pro. What It Does Spots. If you're sharing your location with the ride, nearby riders on the ride see your dot move. Their details say Via Bluetooth when the spot came phone to phone. When one phone gets a newer spot for any rider, from Bluetooth or from the internet, it passes that on too, so everyone in range sees the freshest spot the group has. Status taps and EMERGENCY. A status you tap goes to nearby riders at once over Bluetooth, with or without service, and still sends over the internet when you have signal. An EMERGENCY alerts nearby riders just like it does with service, and always goes out first. The Emergency Siren over Bluetooth. An EMERGENCY from a nearby rider sounds the siren on your phone with no service, and a notification with the siren if OnMyLead is in the background. See Hear the Emergency Siren. Quick replies and messages. Your quick replies and the messages you type in Ride Mode reach nearby riders too. Their phones read them out loud, and they show in Ride Chat marked Via Bluetooth . Every Ride Mode message goes over Bluetooth whole, in any language. Got it, seen it. The card under your tap says who has it: Reached (name) over Bluetooth when their phone got it, and Seen by (name) once it showed on their screen. While your tap is Waiting for Signal , the card still names the nearby riders who got it over Bluetooth. Passed along. Each phone passes on what it hears, up to six phones down the line, so a strung-out group can still hear each other when the riders in between are in range. A phone with service helps the rest. Any phone on the ride that has signal puts what OnMyLead knows about the group, the other riders' spots, status taps and messages, on the air for the riders near it with none. Uploaded when anyone gets signal. When any phone on the ride gets service, it passes what it heard to OnMyLead, including messages and who has seen what, so riders elsewhere and people at home see the group too. When it's working, the no-service banner in Ride Mode says No Service. Sharing With 2 Nearby Phones Over Bluetooth. Range Bluetooth reaches about 30 to 100 meters (100 to 300 feet) between phones in the open, and less through trees, hills, bodies and steel. It works best when the group is bunched up, at a regroup, or riding close. Riders a half mile apart are usually out of range of each other unless riders in between pass it along. Riders farther away than that show where they were last seen, as before. See Use Ride Mode. Before You Lose Service Open Ride Mode once with service. Your phone gets the ride's Bluetooth keys from OnMyLead then and keeps them for that ride. Joining a ride needs service. Allow Bluetooth. The first time, iPhone and iPad ask to use Bluetooth, and Android asks for Nearby devices . Say yes. Keep Bluetooth on. If Bluetooth is off in the phone's settings, nothing goes out. Download the ride's map. See Offline Maps. Turn It On or Off Bluetooth Sharing is on by default. Turn it off or back on in either place: You: switch Bluetooth Sharing off or on. Ride Mode: when you have no service, the no-service banner

title: Use OnMyLead on More Than One Device
summary: Sign in with the same account on your iPhone, iPad, Android phone, tablet or the website, and your settings and Map Mode trails follow you.
headings: Signing In With a Different Account
text: Sign in with the same account on every device you use (iPhone, iPad, Android phone or tablet, and onmylead.com) and OnMyLead keeps them in step. Change a setting on your phone and your tablet has it too. Record a trail on your phone and it's in My Trails on your iPad. Your rides, chats, friends, groups, Garage, trips, Starlink setup, notification settings and profile were always kept with your account. Now your app settings and your own trails are too. Syncing your settings and trails is a Pro feature. See Free and Pro. On a Free account, the Sync row on the You tab carries a Pro tag. Your account, rides, chats, friends and groups are on every device for free. What Follows Your Account Settings The map style (Satellite or Topo) and the trail layer switch Rider Trails on Maps and Follow Me on Maps Zoom In at Intersections Zoom Out at the Edge Dot Style and Dot Size The Track Line switch (the line itself stays on each device, see below) Directions : which maps app Navigate opens. If you picked Apple Maps, an Android phone asks each time, since it doesn't have Apple Maps. Music Controls Appearance : Dark, Light or Match Phone, your theme and Color Blind Mode Language : the language you picked, or Match Phone (then each device follows its own language) Tilt : your warning angles, Warn Me, the spoken warnings, the Tilt Meter switch, and Crash Alert (the Zero stays on each device) Voice : the voice that speaks your alerts. A device that doesn't have that voice uses its best one. Your saved quick replies for ride chat Which panels you keep open or folded in Ride Mode, Map Mode, Route Builder and Waypoints The search distance in Find a Ride and Events Announcements you closed, and the Starlink page connecting by itself Map Mode trails Every trail in My Trails (ones you recorded, drew or saved from other riders), with its details, named spots and photos, is backed up privately to your account. Sign in on another device and they're there. Delete a trail on one device and it's deleted on the others too. The backup is private: only you can see it. Sharing still works exactly as before. A trail only becomes public when you tap Share with Everyone . Map Mode waypoints Waypoints you drop in Map Mode on your own (press and hold the map) are backed up privately the same way, so they show on your other devices, and a waypoint you remove on one is removed on the others. See Waypoints and Planned Stops. Offline map areas The areas you download aren't copied between devices (they're big), but your other devices know about them. Open Offline Maps on another phone or tablet and they're listed under On Your Other Devices . Tap Download to save the same area on this one, or Hide to stop seeing it. Downloading is part of Pro, the same as any download. What Stays on Each Device Some things are about one device, so they stay on it: Battery Saver : it's about this device's battery, and an iPad on the charger may not need it. Track Line : the line of where you've been is location history, so it never leaves the device. The tilt meter's Zero : each phone sits differently in its mount. A recording in progress (it backs up as soon as you save the trail). The downloaded map squares themselves. The Rider Safety and Liability Agreement: you agree once on each device you install OnMyLead on. Your live location is never part of sync. It's only sent while you share it with a ride or with riders you pick, as always. See Privacy and Your Location. Check or Sync Now Tap You . Under Settings , Sync Across Devices says when this device last synced. Tap it to sync right away. Devices sync when you open the app, when you sign in, a moment after you change a setting or a trail, and when you tap Sync Across Devices . With no signal, your changes wait on the device and go up the next time you're connected. If you change the same setting on two devices before either syncs, the change you made last wins. Other settings aren't affected. Signing In With a Different Account Each

title: Add Friends
summary: Add riders as friends so you see each other when you're out riding nearby and can message any time.
keywords: who's riding, message a friend, dm, remove friend, tablet
headings: Cancel a Request or Remove a Friend
text: Add the riders you ride with as friends . Friends see each other in Out Riding when they're out near each other, and can message each other any time. Being friends never shares where you are. In Out Riding, friends see your ride name and roughly how far away you are, in whole miles, the same as any rider you know. Open Friends Go to the Groups tab and tap Friends near the top. The row shows how many friends you have, how many are out riding, and any friend requests waiting for you. Tap a friend's picture to see it full size, or their name in Social to see their profile, rides, badges and posts. See Like, Comment and Post in Social. Add a Friend There's no search by name, so nobody can look you up. You can add a rider in any of these ways: Riders you know : on the Friends screen, Riders You Know lists riders you've been on a ride with or share a riding group with. Tap Add . On a ride : on the ride's page, tap a rider in the Going list, then Add Friend . You can also tap Message there. In Out Riding : tap ••• next to a rider, then Add Friend . In a conversation : tap ••• at the top, then Add Friend . With your friend link : anyone else, like a buddy you met at the trailhead, can add you with your friend link (below). They get a notification and see your request at the top of their Friends screen. You're friends once they tap Accept . If they had already asked you, adding them makes you friends straight away. Share Your Friend Link On the Friends screen, find Your Friend Link . It shows your friend code. Want one that's easy to say, like MOAB-RIDER? Tap Choose Your Own Code . See Choose Your Own Code. Tap Share Friend Link , or Text , Email or Copy . When your buddy opens the link (or types your code under Got a Friend Code? and taps Look Up ), they see your name and tap Add Friend . They need to be signed in to OnMyLead. Accept their request on your Friends screen. To stop an old link working, tap Make a New Link . Your friends stay friends. If your buddy is new to OnMyLead and creates their account with your link, it also counts as an invite: when they finish their first ride, you both get 50% off Pro Annual. See Invite Friends and Get 50% Off Pro. Answer a Friend Request Requests waiting for you are at the top of the Friends screen under Friend Requests . Tap Accept or Decline . Declining just removes the request; the other rider isn't told. See Friends Out Riding On the Friends screen, friends who are out near you are listed first, in green, with roughly how far away they are, like Out Riding, About 3 Miles . You only see this while you're Out Riding yourself, and only for friends within 50 miles. Tap a friend, or the blue message button, to message them. In Out Riding, friends show up when you've both switched it on with Riders I Know (or Everyone Nearby ). They're listed first and marked Friend . Message a Friend Tap the blue message button next to a friend. You can message a friend any time, Out Riding or not. See See Who's Out Riding Nearby for muting, reporting and deleting conversations. Cancel a Request or Remove a Friend Under Requests You Sent , tap Cancel . Next to a friend, tap ✕ , then Remove . They aren't told. Limits To keep requests friendly, you can send up to 30 friend requests a day, and ask the same rider at most twice a week. Blocking If you block a rider, you stop being friends and any request between you is removed. Neither of you can send a new one. See Report or Block a Rider. Notifications Friend requests, and requests someone accepted, come as notifications. Tapping one opens Friends . Turn them off under Friend Requests in Notification Settings. On a Tablet On a tablet in landscape, or a wide window, your friend link and Got a Friend Code? are on the left, and your requests, friends and riders you know are on the right.

title: See the Badge Leaderboard
summary: See where you rank against other riders by badges earned, everywhere or in your country and state, and choose whether you're listed.
text: The Leaderboard ranks riders by the badges they earned by riding. Look at everyone, or narrow it to a country and then a state or province. Open the Leaderboard On Badges , tap Leaderboard under your rank. On Home , tap Leaderboard beside Your Badges . You need to be signed in. It opens on the state or country you ride from, if you picked one. How Riders Are Ranked Each badge level you earn by riding counts once, the same as your rank: Bronze is 1, Silver 2, Gold 3, for up to 21 levels. See Earn Badges and Ranks. Ties go to the rider with more Gold, then more Silver, then whoever reached that total first. OnMyLead Founder and Brand Ambassador don't count, but they still show beside the rider's name. Each row shows the place, the rider's picture and name with their top badge, their rank, where they ride from, their total levels and how many Gold, Silver and Bronze they hold. Tap a rider to open their profile. Your own row is highlighted. If you're further down than the list goes, your place shows at the bottom. Filter by Country and State Under Country , tap Everywhere or a country. For the United States, Canada, Mexico and Australia, a State (or Province ) row appears. Tap one, or All of the country. Only places with riders on the board are listed, plus your own. Pick Where You Ride Riders show on a country or state board only after they pick where they ride from. On the Leaderboard, tap Where You Ride . On iPhone, iPad and Android, tap Use My Location to fill it in. Your phone works out the country and state itself, and only those two are saved, never where you are. Or pick your country (type to search) and then your state or province. Tap Save . To take it off, open Where You Ride and tap Remove My Area . On the website, pick it from the list (there's no Use My Location there). Leave the Leaderboard Turn off Show Me on the Leaderboard . You disappear from every board right away, and you can still look at it. Turn it back on any time. If Who Sees Your Activity in your Feed settings is Nobody , you start off the leaderboard until you turn Show Me on. Riders you've blocked, or who blocked you, never see each other on the leaderboard. See What Other Riders Can See. On a Tablet On an iPad or Android tablet, and on a wide window on the website, your place, Where You Ride , Show Me and the filters sit in a column beside the board.

title: Like, Comment and Post in Social
summary: See what your friends are up to, like and comment on rides, badges and trails, reply to comments, post ride reports with a photo, and share them.
headings: Share to Facebook, Instagram or X
text: Social is where you see everything your friends and the riders you follow have been up to: finished rides, badges, shared trails, group rides and posts. You can like anything, read every comment, and open any rider's profile. Open Social On the Rides tab, tap Open Social next to Feed , or tap any post in the feed. Or tap Friends & Social in your toolkit. On a phone, Social has three tabs: Activity (everyone's posts), Friends and My Posts . On an iPad, an Android tablet or a big window, your friends sit on the left and the posts on the right, so you can switch without losing your place. Like and Comment Tap the heart under a post to like it. Tap it again to take the like back. Tap Comment , or tap the post, to open it on its own page with every comment and who liked it. Type in the box at the bottom (up to 500 characters) and tap the red arrow. You can delete your own comments. You can also delete any comment on your own posts, rides, badges and trails. Like and Reply to Comments Tap Like under a comment to like it. The heart turns red and shows how many riders liked it. Tap it again to take the like back. Tap Reply under a comment. "Replying to" and the rider's name show above the box; type your reply and tap the red arrow. Tap ✕ to go back to a plain comment. Replies sit under the comment they answer, a step in. Replying to a reply keeps it in the same conversation and starts it with @ and the name of the rider you answered. The rider whose comment you like or answer gets a notification. Deleting a comment deletes its replies too. Post on Your Profile In Social, tap Post a ride report… at the top (it's also at the top of your own profile). Write up to 500 characters about the ride, the trail or the crew. Tap Take Photo or Add Photo to add one picture, if you like. Tap Post . Your post shows on your profile and in the feeds of the riders your Who Sees Your Activity setting allows (see Your Home Screen). To delete it, tap ⋯ on the post, then Delete Post . Its likes and comments go with it. Photos are made smaller before they upload: no more than 1,280 pixels on the long side and under 1 MB. Nothing about where you took the photo is added. Rider Profiles Tap a rider's name anywhere in Social to open their profile: their picture, the PRO tag if they have OnMyLead Pro, when they joined, their rides, miles and badges, and their posts, rides, badges and trails, newest first. Tap the picture to see it full size. From a profile you can Message a friend, Add Friend , or Report them. You see a rider's activity only if their Who Sees Your Activity setting allows it. See a Picture Full Size Tap any profile picture, in Social, Friends, Messages, chats or Who's Riding, to see it big. Tap a post's photo to see the whole photo. Tap anywhere to close it. Share to Facebook, Instagram or X Tap Share under one of your own rides, badges or posts, or under a shared trail. Tap Share Picture to share a picture card with the miles, badge or trail name, or Share Text Only . The picture is a 1080 by 1350 PNG named OnMyLead, about 1 to 2 MB, so Facebook, Instagram and Messages take it right away. Pick Facebook, Instagram, X, Messages or any other app. Every share links to onmylead.com. Your location is never in a share, and you can't share other riders' rides or posts, or who's out riding right now. On the website, Share Picture opens your browser's share menu. If your browser doesn't have one, the picture downloads and the text is copied so you can paste it into your post. Free and Pro Free Pro --- --- --- See Social and every comment Yes Yes Like posts Yes Yes Comment No Yes Post on your profile No Yes Share to Facebook, Instagram and X No Yes Liking a comment is free. Replying to a comment is part of commenting, so it needs Pro. Riders with Pro (or the Pro Trial) show a gold PRO tag next to their name. See Free and Pro. title: Contact Us
summary: Send the OnMyLead team a message from the app or the website about a problem, an idea, billing, your account or safety.
headings: Send a Message From the App
Send a Message From the Website
Open These Guides From the App
text: Questions, problems or ideas for OnMyLead go straight to the team at RUS Offroad. A real person reads every message. OnMyLead is not an emergency service. In an emergency, call 911 or your local emergency number first. Send a Message From the App Go to the You tab. Under Help , tap Contact Us . Under What's It About? , pick a topic: Something Isn't Working Feature Request Billing and Pro Account and Sign-In Safety or a Rider General Feedback Something Else Check Your Name (optional) and Your Email . If you're signed in, they're filled in for you. Write Your Message . The hint under the box suggests what to include for your topic. Tap Send Message . You'll see Message Sent . We reply to the email you gave, usually within a day. Report a Bug If something in the app isn't working, tell us with a screenshot so we can fix it fast. Take a screenshot of the problem: iPhone : press the side button and volume up together. iPad : press the top button and a volume button together. Android phone or tablet : press the power and volume down buttons together. Go to the You tab. Under Help , tap Report a Bug . The form opens with Something Isn't Working already picked. Tap Add a Screenshot and pick your screenshot. Tap Change Screenshot or Remove if you picked the wrong one. Write what you tapped, what happened and what you expected, then tap Send Message . Your report also includes your phone model, your OnMyLead version, the screen you were on before you opened the form, and a short log of what the app just did (the screens you opened, errors and requests that failed). The log never includes your location, your messages or anything you typed, and it's kept only in memory: it's gone when you close the app. On onmylead.com/contact, pick Something Isn't Working to add a screenshot the same way. Your browser goes with the report instead of a phone model. Send a Message From the Website Go to onmylead.com/contact. The same form works there, and you don't need to sign in. Email Us You can also email support@rusoffroad.com. Tips for a Quick Answer Something Isn't Working : tell us what you tapped, what happened and what you expected. The ride name helps if it's about a ride. Billing and Pro : purchases are billed by Apple, and refunds go through reportaproblem.apple.com. We're still glad to help. On Android, the hint says purchases are billed by Google Play, with refunds through your Google Play order history. Account and Sign-In : if you sign in with a different email than the one on the form, tell us which. Safety or a Rider : to report a rider, you can also press and hold their message in a ride. See Report or Block a Rider. Help and Support Page Under Help on the You tab, Help and Support has short answers to common questions about joining rides, location and battery, Pro, blocking and deleting your account. Under each answer, Read the Guide opens the full guide for that topic. Open These Guides From the App The step-by-step guides you're reading now (onmylead.com/help) are one tap away in the app: On the You tab, under Help , tap Help Center: How-To Guides . Or tap Help & Support on the Home tab, or Help and Support on the You tab, then tap Help Center: How-To Guides at the top. The guides open inside OnMyLead. Tap Done (iPhone and iPad) or the close button at the top (Android phones and tablets) to go back to the app. On onmylead.com, the link opens the Help Center in the same tab. In the Android app, those answers give the Android steps where they differ, such as allowing location While Using the App .

title: Edit, Cancel or Delete a Ride
summary: Change your ride's name, day, time, meeting point, route and details, call a ride off so riders hear about it, or delete it for good.
text: Plans change. As the organizer (or a co-organizer) you can update the ride's details, change the route and stops, cancel the ride so everyone knows it's off, or delete it entirely. Edit Ride Details Open the ride page. In the You're Organizing card on Details , tap Edit Ride Details . Change what you need and tap Save Changes . Cancel leaves everything as it was. You can change the name, the day and meeting time, the departure and expected finish times, the meeting point (search a place, use your location, type coordinates, or tap the map on onmylead.com), the place name, the state a public ride is listed in, the description, destination, route length, difficulty, experience, the vehicles welcome, whether you approve riders, the vehicle and rider limits, what to bring, required equipment, fuel notes and the instructions joined riders see (on a ride whose meeting point never saved, the instructions box appears once you pick the point, and stays while it holds text). The box above Save Changes says what the save will do before you tap it, or Not Ready to Save with the reason while something stops it (a blank name, a time that doesn't read, a half-typed meeting point, instructions before a meeting point): A new time or meeting point sends everyone on the ride (including riders waiting for approval or on the waitlist) a notification, and the ride page shows Updated with what changed for a week, so nobody turns up at the old spot. Ride reminders move to the new time. Other details (the description, limits, what to bring and so on) just update on the ride page, marked Updated. No notification. Lowering a vehicle or rider limit never removes anyone who already joined. A private ride stays open to anyone with its code. Co-organizers can edit the ride too. Riders can't. Once the ride is live , the day, times and meeting point are locked, because everyone is already out riding. The name and the other details can still change. A ride that has ended or been cancelled can't be edited: tap Ride Again or Copy This Ride to plan the next one. The same Edit Ride Details button is on the ride page at onmylead.com, so you can make changes on a big screen. On an iPad or Android tablet turned sideways, the day, times and meeting point sit on the left and the rest of the details on the right. The Route, Stops and Roles The route. Open the Map section and tap Edit Route (or Build the Route if there isn't one yet, or Map a Route Anyway on a freeride). See Build a Route. Planned stops. In the Map section, tap Add a Planned Stop . See Waypoints and Planned Stops. Who leads and who rides at the rear. See Leader, Sweep and Tail Gunner. Cancel a Ride Cancel when the ride is off but you want everyone to see that it was called off. The ride stays in their list as Cancelled. Open the ride page. In the You're Organizing card on Details , tap Cancel Ride . Read the message. It tells you how many riders will hear about it. Tap Cancel Ride to confirm, or Keep Ride to go back. Everyone who joined, asked to join or is on the waitlist gets a notification and an email saying the ride is cancelled. Cancelling can't be undone. You can cancel a ride that hasn't started yet or one that's live. A ride that has already ended can't be cancelled. Delete a Ride Delete removes the ride for everyone, along with its chat and route. Only the ride's organizer can delete it. Open the ride page. In the You're Organizing card, tap Delete Ride . Tap Delete Ride to confirm. If the ride hadn't ended yet, everyone on it gets a notification and an email saying it's cancelled. Deleting can't be undone. You can also delete a ride from the Rides tab. Swipe left on the ride under Your Rides or Past Rides and tap Delete . On onmylead.com there's nothing to swipe: each ride on the Rides page has its own button at the end of the row. Click the trash can ( Delete ) on a ride you organize, then confirm. On a ride someone else organizes the button is Leave (or Decline for an invite). Cancel or Dele

title: Follow a Ride Leader
summary: Follow the riders who organize and lead your favorite rides and get a notification when they post a new public ride.
text: Liked a ride? Follow the rider who organized or led it, and you'll hear when they post their next public ride. Following is free. Follow a Leader Open the ride's page. If you've joined the ride, go to Riders . Find the organizer or ride leader. Each one is labeled Organizer or Ride Leader . Tap Follow . The button changes to Following . To stop, tap Following on a ride page, or use Unfollow on the Groups tab (see below). You can't follow yourself, so your own name doesn't get a Follow button. What You Get A notification when a leader you follow posts a new public ride. Private and unlisted rides are never announced to followers. On the Groups tab, under Leaders You Follow , a list of the leaders you follow, and under Their Upcoming Rides , their upcoming public rides. To turn these notifications off, switch off Leaders You Follow in Notification Settings. Unfollow a Leader Tap the Groups tab. Under Leaders You Follow , tap Unfollow next to the leader. Who Sees a Follow Only you and the leader can see that you follow them. If riders follow you, the Groups tab shows how many.

title: Invite Riders
summary: Send your ride by text, email or any app, copy its link, show a QR code, or invite a whole riding group in one tap.
text: Every ride has a link, an invite code and a QR code. Send any of them and your friends can open the ride and join. Find the Invite Card Right after you create a ride, its page opens with the invite card at the top. Later, open the ride page and tap Riders to find the Invite Riders card. Anyone on a ride can share it, not just the organizer. On a public ride, anyone who can see the ride page can share it. On a private ride, only riders who have joined see the invite card. Send the Invite On the invite card, tap: Share Invite to send it with any app on your phone Text to open a new text message Email to open a new email Copy Link to copy the ride's link, then paste it anywhere The message includes the ride name, the link and the invite code. When your friend taps the link, the ride opens in OnMyLead if they have it, or on onmylead.com with a button to get the app. On Android, ride and riding group links open straight in the OnMyLead app once it's installed. Share the Code The Invite Code is shown in big letters on the card. Friends can type it on the Rides tab under Join a Ride . See Join a Ride. Want a code that's easy to say out loud, like MOAB-2026? The ride's organizers can tap Choose Your Own Code under the QR code, type a new one and tap Save Code . OnMyLead checks right away that no other ride uses it. The old link, QR code and code stop working; riders already on the ride stay on it. See Choose Your Own Code. Show a QR Code Tap Show QR Code (or the small QR code) to show it full screen, so riders at the trailhead can scan it off your phone. See QR Codes. Invite a Riding Group Organizers can invite everyone in a riding group at once. Each rider gets a notification and sees the ride on their Rides tab, and they join with one tap. From the ride page: Open the ride page and tap Riders . On the invite card, under Invite a Group , tap Invite All next to the group. Each group shows its group photo (or its initials) beside its name. From the group: On the Groups tab, open the group. Tap Invite to a Ride . Tap the ride. It lists the upcoming rides you organize. You can also pick groups under Invite a Group when you create the ride. See Create a Ride. Invited riders skip approval, even on a ride where you approve riders. Saving a riding group is a Pro feature, but inviting a group you're already in to your ride is not. See Riding Groups and Free and Pro. Public or Private? Public rides can also be found by riders near you or in your state on the Find tab. Private rides are only found by people you send the link, QR code or code to. Anyone holding them can join, so share them only with people you want on the ride.

title: Keep the Group Together with Ride Bubble
summary: Ride Bubble watches for riders who drop back, run ahead or stop moving, and warns the leader and tail gunner before anyone gets lost.
headings: What the Leader and Tail Gunner See
text: Ride Bubble keeps an eye on the gaps in the group while Ride Mode is open. When a rider gets too far from everyone else, stops while the group keeps moving, or goes quiet, Ride Bubble flags them. It's free on every plan. How It Decides Each rider is measured against the nearest other rider, not just the leader. That way a rider who has run far ahead counts too, and the tail gunner at the back is measured against the last rider rather than the whole pack. A rider turns yellow or red when: They're too far from the nearest rider. The distances depend on the ride's Ride Bubble setting (below). They've stopped while at least half the group is moving. Yellow after 2 minutes stopped, red after 5 minutes. Their phone has gone quiet. No update for 5 minutes turns a rider red, with a message like "No update from Sam for 6 minutes. Showing last known location." Only riders who are sharing their location are part of Ride Bubble. A rider who isn't sharing can't be measured. A rider whose phone shares only an approximate location (Precise Location turned off) can show up a mile or more from where they are. Ride Bubble leaves out the distance their rough location could be off by, so a rider beside you isn't called separated. See Make Your Location Accurate. Ride Bubble Settings The organizer picks the setting when creating the ride, under Add Route, Difficulty and More , in Ride Bubble . Setting Yellow when the nearest rider is more than Red when the nearest rider is more than --- --- --- Standard 0.5 miles 1.5 miles Tight Trail 0.1 miles 0.25 miles Desert 0.75 miles 2 miles Highway 1 mile 3 miles The stopped and no-update times are the same for every setting. What Everyone Sees A yellow or red ring around a rider's dot on the map. With Color Blind Mode on ( You Appearance ), the ring is yellow or orange-red, OK riders show sky blue, and a ! or ✕ appears before the rider's name. See Change the Look. At the top of Ride Mode, Together in green, or the number of red riders, such as 2 Separated , in red. Tap it to see every rider and when they last updated. What the Leader and Tail Gunner See The ride's leader, tail gunner, organizer and co-organizers also get: An alert card for each yellow or red rider, such as "Mike is 1.7 miles behind the group. Last moving 4 minutes ago." Tap Navigate for directions to them. Leaders and organizers can also tap Regroup to set a regroup point at their location. A spoken alert and a buzz the moment a rider turns red, so you don't have to look down. The alert cards hide when the bottom panel is folded. Tap Buttons ▲ to open the panel and see them. Spoken alerts pause while your own phone has no service. When you lose signal everyone looks quiet, and that's your signal dropping, not theirs. Spoken alerts use the most natural voice on your phone. To hear and pick another, see Choose the Voice for Spoken Alerts. Tips Ask everyone to share their location for the whole ride so Ride Bubble can see them. See Share Your Location. Give someone the tail gunner role so the back of the group is covered. See Leader, Sweep and Tail Gunner.

title: Notification Settings
summary: Choose which ride, chat, group and account notifications you get, set a ride reminder and quiet hours. Help and EMERGENCY alerts always come through.
headings: What You Can Turn On or Off
text: You decide what OnMyLead tells you about. Every change saves as soon as you make it, and your choices apply on any device you sign in on. Open Notification Settings Go to the You tab. Under Settings , tap Notifications . The line under it sums up your settings, like Everything on or 2 turned off . You can also tap the bell at the top of the Rides tab, then Notification Settings at the bottom of the list. Always On: Help and EMERGENCY When someone in your group taps Need Help or EMERGENCY , you're always told, even during quiet hours. This can't be turned off. Emergency Siren , just below, starts on: an EMERGENCY from your group sounds a loud siren until you silence it. Tap Play Siren to hear it, or switch it off to get EMERGENCY notifications with the normal sound. See Hear the Emergency Siren. What You Can Turn On or Off Everything below starts on. On the Trail Rider Status : status buttons and quick replies from Ride Mode, like On My Way , Need Fuel and Flat Tire , and when a rider cancels one. Announcements : what the organizer tells the whole group. Announcements also cover new waypoints the leader shares while the ride is live. See New Waypoint Alerts. Messages riders type in Ride Mode with ✎ Message follow the Rider Status setting too. Ride Chat Group Chat : messages and quick replies from your group. Messages to the Leader : leader-only messages, when you're leading. Show Message Text : turn this off to keep messages off your lock screen. You'll see who wrote, not what. Before the Ride Ride Changes : a ride starts, is cancelled, or gets a new time or meeting spot, or you get a spot or a role. New Riders : someone joins or asks to join a ride you organize. Email When a Ride Is Cancelled : an email as well as the notification if a ride you joined is cancelled or removed. Your Riding Groups Ride Invites : someone invites you, or a group you're in, to a ride. Riding Group Chat : new messages in your riding groups' chats. To mute just one group, do it from that group's chat. See Group Chat. Leaders You Follow : a leader you follow posts a new public ride. Direct Messages : a rider messages you, say after seeing you Out Riding. To mute one conversation, do it from inside it. See See Who's Out Riding Nearby. Friend Requests : a rider asks to be your friend, or accepts your request. See Add Friends. Likes and Comments : a rider likes or comments on your post, ride, badge or trail, or replies after you comment. Likes on one post come at most once every 15 minutes. See Like, Comment and Post in Social. Likes and Comments also covers a rider liking or replying to your comment. Likes on one comment come at most once every 15 minutes too. Your Account Badges and Pro Trial : when you earn a badge (see Earn Badges and Ranks), and a week, 3 days and a day before your Pro Trial ends. It also tells you when a trail you shared is hidden from the public map (see Navigate Offroad and Map Your Own Trails). Email Me Too : the same Pro Trial reminders by email. Tapping a Notification Tapping a notification takes you straight to what it's about, whether OnMyLead was open, in the background or closed: A status tap like Need Help , a quick reply, or a ride going live opens Ride Mode for that ride. A ride chat message opens the ride's Chat . A riding group message opens that group's chat. Ride changes, new riders, invites and reminders open the ride. A new badge opens Badges . A direct message opens the conversation. A friend request, or a request someone accepted, opens Friends . A trail of yours being hidden opens My Trails . A like or a comment opens that post with all its comments. Notifications you've missed or swiped away are kept under the bell on the Rides tab for 30 days. See See and Clear Your Notifications. Ride Reminder Get a heads-up before each ride you've joined, with the meeting spot. Under Ride reminder , pick Off , 30 Min , 1 Hour , 2 Hours or Day Before . It starts at 1 Hour . Quiet Hours Under Quiet hours , turn on Silence Over

title: Subscribe to OnMyLead Pro
summary: Choose the monthly or annual plan and subscribe to OnMyLead Pro in the app, billed through your Apple Account or Google Play.
headings: Already Have Pro From the Other Store?
text: OnMyLead Pro adds unlimited rides, offline maps, GPX import, saved riding groups and more. See Free and Pro for the full list. Prices Plan US Price --- --- Monthly $4.99 a month Annual $29.99 a year, about $2.50 a month. Saves about 50% compared with paying monthly. Outside the US, the app shows the price in your local currency. Subscribe Invited by a friend, or invited one? When the new rider finishes their first ride, you both get Pro Annual at 50% off for the first year. See Invite Friends and Get 50% Off Pro. On the You tab, under Settings , tap Subscription . Tap Upgrade to Pro . During your free trial, this button says Keep Pro After the Trial . Choose Annual (marked Best Value ) or Monthly . Tap the Subscribe for button under the plans, for example Subscribe for $29.99 a Year . Confirm the purchase in Apple's window. On Android, step 5 is Google Play's window instead, and the payment goes to your Google Play account. When it's done, the app says You’re on OnMyLead Pro. Thanks for riding with us. and your plan shows Pro . You can also reach the Pro screen by tapping See OnMyLead Pro on any Pro prompt, or Unlimited With Pro on the Create a Ride screen. You can subscribe in the OnMyLead app only, on iPhone, iPad or Android. The website can't sell subscriptions, but Pro you buy in the app also works when you use OnMyLead on the website. Already Have Pro From the Other Store? Pro belongs to your OnMyLead account, so a subscription from the App Store works on Android and one from Google Play works on iPhone and iPad. If you already pay for Pro through one store, the Pro screen on a device that uses the other store says so instead of showing the plans, so you aren't charged twice. To move your subscription to the other store, cancel it in the store you pay now and subscribe on the other device after it ends. Billing Payment is charged to your Apple Account when you confirm the purchase. The subscription renews automatically unless you turn it off at least 24 hours before the end of the current period. Renewal is charged within the 24 hours before the period ends. You can manage or cancel anytime in your Apple Account settings. See Manage or Cancel Your Subscription. On Android, payment is charged to your Google Play account when you confirm. The subscription renews automatically at the end of each period until you cancel it in Google Play, and Pro stays on until the end of the period you paid for. The free Pro Trial for new accounts is separate. It needs no payment and never turns into a paid subscription on its own. The Pro screen links to the Terms of Use and Privacy Policy . If Something Goes Wrong "Waiting on Apple to approve the purchase." This happens with Ask to Buy or when your bank needs to check the payment. Once it's approved, Pro starts on its own. "Waiting on Google Play to approve the purchase." This happens when you pay with a method Google confirms later, such as cash at a store. Pro starts on its own once the payment goes through. "The purchase didn’t go through. You weren’t charged." Check your connection and try again. Your plan still says Free after buying. Make sure you have signal, then close and reopen the app. If it still says Free, tap Restore Purchases . See Restore Purchases.

title: Waypoints and Planned Stops
summary: Mark camp, fuel, water, a gate or a hazard on a ride's map, and let the leader plan numbered stops for the whole group.
text: Waypoints are named spots you drop on a ride's map, such as camp, fuel, water, a viewpoint, a hazard or parking. Your own waypoints are only for you. The ride's leader can also share waypoints with everyone on the ride, and plan numbered stops the whole group will make. Waypoints are never public. Shared ones and planned stops show only to riders on that ride. Adding waypoints and planned stops is a Pro feature. See Free and Pro. On a Free account, Add Waypoint , Add a Waypoint , Add a Planned Stop and Add at My Location carry a Pro tag. Seeing the leader's waypoints and stops on a ride, and following them in Ride Mode, stay free. Who Sees What Your waypoints : only you see them, unless you can share (below). Shared waypoints : the leader or an organizer can share a waypoint with everyone on the ride. Planned stops : always shared. Every rider sees them numbered on the map, in order. The leader is the rider with the Leader role, or the organizer when nobody has it. See Leader, Sweep and Tail Gunner. You need to have joined the ride to add or see its waypoints. Add a Waypoint Open the ride and tap the Map tab. Under Waypoints , tap Add a Waypoint (or Open Waypoints Map if there are some already). Press and hold the map where you want it (click it on onmylead.com). To mark where you're standing, tap Add at My Location instead. Pick its symbol. The name fills in for you. See Waypoint Symbols below. Change the Name if you like, and add a Note (Optional) . If you're the leader or an organizer, choose who it's for under What It Is (see below). Tap Save Waypoint . Changed your mind? Swipe the sheet down, or tap Cancel , to close it without saving. To find a spot by name, tap Search at the top of the waypoints map and type a park, trailhead, town or address, such as "Hidden Falls Adventure Park". Pick a result and the map moves there and labels it. Then press and hold (or click) the map at that spot to drop the waypoint. Search only moves the map; nothing is added until you drop it. See Search for a Place. In Ride Mode, tap Add Waypoint to drop one where you are, or press and hold the map. See Ride Mode. Press and Hold the Map In Ride Mode and Map Mode, press and hold anywhere on the map. The New Waypoint sheet opens for that spot: pick a symbol, change the name if you like, add a note and tap Save Waypoint . On onmylead.com, right-click the map in Map Mode instead (or press and hold on a touch screen). On a group ride (Ride Mode, or Map Mode while you're sharing your location with a live ride): the waypoint goes on that ride. If you're the leader or an organizer it starts as Everyone on the Ride , so the whole group sees it. Other riders' waypoints are just for them. In Map Mode on your own : the waypoint is yours and saved on your phone, so it works with no signal. With Sync Across Devices (Pro) it also shows on your other devices. While the Draw tab is open in Map Mode, taps add points to the line, so press and hold doesn't drop waypoints until you switch tabs. To change one later, tap it on the map, then tap Edit (name, symbol, note) or Remove . New Waypoint Alerts When the leader or an organizer shares a waypoint or a planned stop while the ride is live, everyone else on the ride gets a notification with a sound, like "Lou added a new waypoint: Fuel Stop". Tap it to open Ride Mode with that waypoint showing. It also goes into your Notifications. It goes out once per waypoint: when it's added for everyone, or when a Just Me waypoint is switched to Everyone on the Ride . Editing it afterwards, or switching it to Just Me and back, doesn't send another. Waypoints set up before the ride starts don't send alerts. They're on the map when riders open Ride Mode. New waypoint alerts follow the Announcements switch in Notification Settings and your quiet hours. Names can be up to 60 characters and notes up to 280. Waypoint Symbols Every waypoint has a symbol, so you can tell what it is at a glance on the map. There are 15: Symbol Use it for

title: What Other Riders Can See
