summary: Your location is never public. See what strangers, riders on your ride and family links can see, and how OnMyLead's server enforces it.
text: OnMyLead is built so your location is never public. You choose who sees it and for how long, and sharing always ends. These rules are enforced by OnMyLead's server, not just hidden in the app. Before You Join a Ride Anyone can see a ride's public page: its name, time, description and details such as difficulty and vehicles. What they don't get: The exact meeting point. Public listings and the ride map show a meeting area rounded to about a mile. The ride page says Shown after you join , or Near and the area's name. The route, the meeting instructions and the roster. Only riders who have joined the ride get these. The exact meeting point and the route are stored separately from the public ride, and the server only hands them to riders on the ride. Riders on Your Ride Once you've joined a ride, the other riders on it can see: Your ride name. If you turned on Show My Google (or Apple or Facebook) Profile , they also see that account's name and photo. See Your Ride Name and Profile. Your profile picture, if you added one. Like your ride name, any signed-in rider can see it, never people who aren't signed in. See Add a Profile Picture. That you're on the ride, your role, and whether you've checked in. Your messages in the ride chat, except leader-only messages, which only you and the leader can read. Your status taps and quick replies from Ride Mode (and, from 2.0, messages you type there). A status tap carries your phone's location at the moment you tapped it. Your live location, but only while you're sharing with the ride. If you're the leader, the path you've ridden while sharing, drawn as the Leader Trackline. Each rider's phone draws it from the live positions it already gets; nothing extra is uploaded. You can turn it off for the ride. Your Live Location The server only lets someone read your location while all of these are true: You have turned sharing on. Your share hasn't run out or been stopped. They are someone your share covers: a rider on that ride, a rider you picked, or someone with your family link. For ride sharing, the ride is still going and you're still on it. When the ride ends, every ride share on it stops at once. When you leave a ride, your share for it stops. See Share Your Location. Your Ride Track While you share with a ride, your phone keeps a track of where you rode for your ride summary. Only you can see your own track. The group summary shows totals only, never anyone's route. Waypoints Waypoints you drop are only yours, unless you're the ride's leader and choose to share one with the ride. See Waypoints and Planned Stops. Family Links Anyone with your family link can see your last location until that share ends. See Share a Family Link. Out Riding Out Riding is off until you switch it on. While it's on, riders who can see you get your ride name, where you said you're riding (if you typed it) and roughly how far away you are in whole miles, never your location. OnMyLead keeps only an area of about a mile, and deletes it when you turn Out Riding off. It turns itself off at the time you picked, or after 6 hours without opening the app. By default only your friends, and riders you've ridden with or share a group with, can see you. Friends Only you and the other rider can see that you're friends, or that one of you sent a request. Nobody can search for riders by name: a rider can only send you a request if they've ridden with you, share a riding group with you, can see you in Out Riding, have messaged with you, or have your friend link. Being friends never shares your location. See Add Friends. Reports The OnMyLead team can't read your direct messages or chats. The one exception is a report: when a rider reports another rider, their messages with that rider (direct messages, and what either of them wrote in the last 30 days in a group or ride chat they share) are saved with the report so the team can look into it. Only the OnMyLead team can read them, and every time they're opened it's logged. See Report

title: Choose Your Own Code
summary: Give your ride, riding group or friend link a code that's easy to say, like MOAB-2026, instead of the one OnMyLead made.
headings: What Happens to the Old Code
text: Every ride, riding group and friend link has a code: it's the end of the link (onmylead.com/r/MOAB-2026) and what riders type to open it. OnMyLead makes one for you, like 7F3A9C21. You can type your own instead, so it's easy to say out loud at the trailhead. Choosing your own code is a Pro feature. See Free and Pro. On a Free account, every ride, group and friend link still gets its own code that works, and the code box shows a Pro tag. What a Code Can Be 6 to 20 letters and numbers Dashes between words, like SATURDAY-CREW (a space turns into a dash as you type) Capital or small letters both work: moab-2026 opens the same ride as MOAB-2026 Codes that pass for OnMyLead itself (like ONMYLEAD or SUPPORT) and rude words aren't allowed. As you type, OnMyLead checks the code. A green Available means you can use it. Another ride already uses this code means someone got there first, so try another. A Ride's Code When you create it: under Invite Code , type it in Your Own Code (Optional) . Leave it empty to get one made for you. See Create a Ride. Later: on the ride's invite card, tap Choose Your Own Code , type the new code and tap Save Code . Only the ride's organizers see this, and only before the ride ends. On a private ride, anyone with the code can join, so pick one that's hard to guess. A Riding Group's Code When you create it: type it in Group Code (Optional) . Later: open the group, scroll to Invite by Link and tap Choose Your Own Code . Only the rider who runs the group sees this. Your Friend Link On the Friends screen, under Your Friend Link , tap Choose Your Own Code . See Add Friends. What Happens to the Old Code When you change a code, the old link, QR code and code stop working, the same as Make a New Link . Riders already on the ride or in the group stay in, and your friends stay friends. Send the new link to anyone who still needs it. It works the same on iPhone, iPad, Android phones, Android tablets and onmylead.com.

title: Check Your Fuel Range for a Ride
summary: See if your machine's tank covers the ride's miles, using the thirds rule, before you leave and in Ride Mode.
headings: Where the Ride's Miles Come From
text: Trail miles burn more fuel than you think. OnMyLead compares a ride's miles with your machine's range from your garage and tells you, in plain words, whether you have enough. How Range Is Worked Out Your range is your fuel (tank plus any extra fuel you carry) times your miles per gallon. The check uses the thirds rule: a third out, a third back and a third in reserve. Enough Range : the ride is within two thirds of your full range, so you keep a reserve. Range Is Tight : the ride eats into your reserve. Bring extra fuel or plan a fill-up. Not Enough Range : the ride is longer than your full range. The check says about how many miles short you are. When you have enough, it also says roughly how much fuel you'll have left at the end. Set Up Your Machine The check needs your machine's tank size and mileage. Open your machine in the Garage and edit it. Under Fuel and Mileage , enter Tank (gal) . If you carry spare fuel, enter Extra Fuel (gal) . Enter Miles per Gallon . Use your real-world trail mpg, not the sticker number. Save. Your machine's page then shows its Full Range , Safe Turnaround and Safe Trip miles. See Your Garage. Where the Ride's Miles Come From If the ride has a mapped route, its miles come from the route. See Draw a Route. If not, the organizer can enter Route Length (Miles) when creating the ride, under Add Route, Difficulty and More . A ride with neither has no miles to check against. Check Before the Ride Join the ride, open it and tap the Details tab. Find the fuel card. Until there's a result, it's called Your Machine . Under Bringing , pick the machine you're taking, or None / Riding Along . Read the result: Enough Range , Range Is Tight or Not Enough Range , with one line of advice. If you have only one machine with a tank size and mpg, it's checked until you pick one. You can change your machine while the ride is scheduled or live. If the card says to add tank size and mpg, tap Edit Machine . If your garage is empty, tap Add Your Machine to the Garage . In Ride Mode When the ride has a mapped route, Ride Mode shows your range check with the route progress, colored green, yellow or red. It uses the route's length and the machine you picked for the ride. See Ride Mode. Running low on the trail? Use the Need Fuel status button to let the group know. See Status Buttons. Good to Know The check is worked out for you from your own garage. It's a planning guide, not a gauge. Hills, sand, mud, load and speed all change real fuel use. The Trip Planner has a fuel check too. See Trip Planner.

title: Manage or Cancel Your Subscription
summary: Change between monthly and annual or cancel OnMyLead Pro in your Apple Account settings, and see what happens when Pro ends.
headings: Cancel or Change Your Plan in the App
Cancel or Change It on Android
Cancel or Change It in iPhone Settings
text: OnMyLead Pro is billed by Apple, so you change or cancel it in your Apple Account settings. The app takes you straight there. Cancel or Change Your Plan in the App On the You tab, under Settings , tap Subscription . Tap Manage Subscription . Apple's subscription screen opens. Choose a different plan, or cancel your subscription. If you pay for Pro, the Pro screen also has a Manage Subscription button where the plans usually are. Cancel or Change It on Android On Android, Pro is billed by Google Play. Manage Subscription opens Google Play's subscription page for OnMyLead, where you can change plans or cancel. You can also do it in the Play Store app: tap your profile picture, then Payments & Subscriptions Subscriptions OnMyLead . If you bought Pro on a different kind of device (on an iPhone while you're on Android, or the other way round), Manage Subscription tells you which store bills it and opens that store's subscription page. Cancel it there. Cancel or Change It in iPhone Settings Open the Settings app on your iPhone. Tap your name at the top. Tap Subscriptions . Tap OnMyLead , then choose a plan or cancel. To avoid being charged for the next period, cancel at least 24 hours before your current period ends. The subscription renews automatically until you turn it off. Check When It Renews On the Subscription screen, Your Plan shows Pro and the date it renews or ends. What Happens When Pro Ends When a subscription you cancelled reaches the end of the period you paid for, your account moves to Free. Nothing is deleted: Rides: every ride you created stays. Free accounts create one new ride a month. Routes: routes you already imported from GPX stay and stay editable. Importing a new GPX file needs Pro. Offline maps: maps already on your phone keep working. Downloading new map areas needs Pro. Riding groups: your groups stay, with their chats, and you can still invite them to your rides. Creating a group or adding and removing riders needs Pro. Polls: polls already sent can still be voted on. Creating a new poll needs Pro. Ride history: Home shows your last 5 past rides. The rest are saved, and show again if you upgrade. Trips: your trips stay. Free plans one active trip at a time. See Free and Pro for the full comparison. Good to Know Deleting your OnMyLead account does not cancel the Apple subscription. Cancel it in your Apple subscriptions too, so you aren't billed again. See Delete Your Account. If your plan says Complimentary Pro , it was given to you by OnMyLead and isn't billed by Apple, so there's nothing to cancel. Deleting your OnMyLead account doesn't cancel a Google Play subscription either. Cancel it in Google Play too. On Android, Your Plan also says which store bills your Pro. Subscriptions can only be managed in the app on your phone or tablet. On the website, the Subscription screen says so.

title: Organizer Controls
summary: Everything you can do as a ride's organizer, from starting Ride Mode and approving riders to ending the ride for everyone.
text: When you create a ride, you're its organizer. You're also its leader until you hand that job to someone else. Here's what you can do from your ride page. Before the Ride Invite riders. Share the link, code or QR code, or invite a whole riding group. See Invite Riders. Approve requests. If riders asked to join, the Riders section shows a red count and a Waiting for You list with Approve and Decline . See Approvals and the Waitlist. Build or edit the route and add planned stops in the Map section. See Build a Route. Pick a leader and a tail gunner from the roster in Riders . See Leader, Sweep and Tail Gunner. Post announcements in the ride chat. Your latest announcement is pinned near the top of the ride page for everyone on the ride. See Ride Chat. You get a notification when someone joins or asks to join a ride you organize. You can turn these off in Notification Settings. Start the Ride Open the ride page. Tap Start Ride Mode . The ride goes live, riders on it get a notification that it started, and Ride Mode opens for you. Everyone else on the ride sees Enter Ride Mode on the ride page, and a banner on their Rides tab. See Ride Mode. End the Ride When everyone is off the trail: Open the ride page. In the You're Organizing card on Details , tap End Ride for Everyone . Ending the ride stops everyone's location sharing for this ride. Riders then see their ride summary on the ride page. See Ride Summary and Ride Again. A live ride doesn't end by itself. Remember to tap End Ride for Everyone when you're done, so location sharing for the ride stops. Hand Off the Whole Ride If you can't make it, give the ride to another rider who has joined. Open Riders , tap their name and tap Give Them the Ride . They become the organizer and leader, and you stay on the ride as a rider. You can't undo this yourself. See Leader, Sweep and Tail Gunner. Or tap Leave Ride at the bottom of the ride page: pick who takes over under Who Takes Over? and tap Give Ride and Leave . They run the ride and you're off it. Change the Details Tap Edit Ride Details in the You're Organizing card to change the name, day, time, meeting point and the rest. Riders hear about a new time or meeting point. See Edit, Cancel or Delete a Ride. Call It Off Use Cancel Ride or Delete Ride in the You're Organizing card. See Edit, Cancel or Delete a Ride. Run It Again Tap Copy This Ride (or Ride Again after it ends) to start a new ride with the same details and route. See Ride Summary and Ride Again. As the organizer you can't leave your own ride. Hand it to another rider first if you need to step away. Ride Managers for Event Rides When a ride is one of an event's group rides, an event host who organizes the ride can pick a Ride Manager on the event's page. The Ride Manager becomes a Co-Organizer of the ride (after joining it, if they weren't on it). See Events.

title: QR Codes
summary: Show your ride's QR code so riders can scan it at the trailhead, share it as a picture, or scan one to join a ride.
headings: Share the QR Code as a Picture
Scan a QR Code to Join
text: Every ride has its own QR code. It's the quickest way to get riders on your ride at the trailhead: they point their camera at your screen and they're in. Show Your Ride's QR Code Open the ride page. Right after creating a ride, the invite card is at the top. Later, tap Riders to find it. Tap Show QR Code , or tap the small QR code on the card. The QR code opens full screen with the ride name and the invite code under it ( Or Enter Code ), so riders can type the code if their camera won't scan. Tap Done to close it. You can also swipe it down to close it. Share the QR Code as a Picture Show the QR code full screen. Tap Share QR Code . Pick how to send it: text, email or any app. It sends a picture of the QR code card along with the ride link. You can print it or post it for a club ride. Scan a QR Code to Join Open your phone's Camera and point it at the QR code. Tap the link that appears. If you have OnMyLead, you go straight to the ride. If not, the ride's page opens on onmylead.com with a button to get the app. Tap Join Ride . See Join a Ride. Opened a ride link on your computer? The ride's web page shows its QR code. Scan it with your phone to open the ride there. The QR code holds only the ride's link and invite code. It doesn't show the meeting point. On a private ride, anyone who scans it can join, so share it with care.

title: Report or Block a Rider
summary: Report a rider or a ride to the OnMyLead team, and block a rider to hide their chat messages. Nobody is told who reported or blocked them.
headings: Report a Rider From the You Tab
What Happens After You Report a Rider
text: If a rider or a ride isn't right, report it to the OnMyLead team. If you'd rather not hear from a rider, block them. Neither one tells the other person it was you. If anyone is in danger, call 911 first. Report a Rider From the You Tab Tap the You tab. Under Help , tap Report a Rider . Tap the rider. The list shows riders you've messaged, added as friends, ridden with or share a group with, and riders you blocked. Type in Search to find one by name. Pick what's wrong, add details if you like, and tap Send Report . Riders you've never ridden with or messaged aren't listed, so nobody can look riders up by name. Report a Rider Open the ride and tap Riders . In the Going list, tap the rider. Tap Report Rider . Under What's Wrong , pick Harassment , Threats , Unsafe Riding , Spam or Scam , Fake Account , Inappropriate Photo or Something Else . Add details under Anything Else (Optional) if you like. Tap Send Report . To close the report without sending it, swipe it down or tap Cancel . You can also press and hold one of the rider's messages in ride chat or group chat, then tap Report Rider . From a direct message, tap ••• then Report Rider , or press and hold one of their messages. The message goes with your report. In Out Riding, tap ••• next to a rider. See See Who's Out Riding Nearby. Report a Post or Comment In Social, tap ⋯ on a post and tap Report This Post , or tap Report under a comment. Pick what's wrong, add details if you like, and tap Send Report . You can also report a rider from their profile. When three different riders report the same post or comment, it's hidden until the OnMyLead team looks at it. See Like, Comment and Post in Social. Report a Ride Open the ride's page. Scroll to the bottom and tap Report Ride . Under What's Wrong , pick Unsafe Plan , Spam or Scam , Offensive Content or Something Else . Add details if you like, then tap Send Report . Reports go to the OnMyLead team, not to the rider or the organizer. OnMyLead looks at every report, and the person reported isn't told who sent it. What Happens After You Report a Rider The OnMyLead team is emailed about every report straight away. Your messages with the rider are saved with the report: your direct messages, and what either of you wrote in the last 30 days in a group chat or ride chat you share. Only the OnMyLead team can read them, and only to look into your report. Deleting a message or leaving a group afterwards doesn't remove the copy. If the rider broke the rules, OnMyLead can suspend their account for 1, 7, 30 or 90 days, or ban it for good. They're signed out within the hour and can't sign in until the suspension ends. You aren't told what action was taken, and they aren't told who reported them. If you see This account is suspended when you sign in, your account was suspended for breaking the rider rules. If you think it's a mistake, contact us. Report an Event On an event's page, scroll down and tap Report This Event (you need to be signed in, and it isn't shown to the event's hosts). Pick what's wrong ( Spam or Scam , Fake Event , Offensive Content , Inappropriate Photo , Unsafe Plan or Something Else ), add a note if you like, and tap Send Report . It goes to the OnMyLead team as a report about the event's host, with the event attached. The host isn't told who sent it. The team can hide the event or take down a photo. Block a Rider Blocking hides a rider's chat from you. Open the ride and tap Riders . In the Going list, tap the rider. Tap Block Rider . Tap Block to confirm. You can also block from: Ride chat or group chat: press and hold their message, then tap Block Rider . A report: tap Block This Rider , or Also Block This Rider after you send it. What Blocking Does You don't see their messages or polls in ride chat or group chat. You don't get chat notifications or pop-ups from them. They aren't told, and they can't see that you blocked them. Neither of you sees the other in Out Riding, their direct messages are hidden from you, and they

title: Use OnMyLead on a Tablet
summary: On an iPad or Android tablet the map fills the screen, with the riders, the ride details and your buttons beside it.
headings: Draw a Route and Add Waypoints
text: OnMyLead works the same on a tablet as on a phone, with the same account, rides and Pro plan. A tablet just gets layouts made for the bigger screen: the map fills it, and the riders, the ride details and your buttons sit beside the map instead of on top of it. Using OnMyLead on a tablet or the website is a Pro feature. See Free and Pro. On a Free account, a tablet or the website opens a screen with Join a Ride , Your Rides , See OnMyLead Pro and Your Account . Joining a ride, the ride page and Ride Mode always work, so you can follow the leader on any device for free. Turn It Either Way Hold the tablet upright or sideways; every screen works both ways. Phones stay upright. You can also run OnMyLead next to another app (Split View or Slide Over on an iPad, split screen on Android). The layout follows the size of the window: in a narrow window you get the phone layout, and it switches back as the window grows. Getting Around On a tablet, Rides , Find , Groups and You run down the left edge of the screen instead of along the bottom. The blue Map Mode button sits under Find and opens your offroad map full screen. On Rides , with the tablet sideways, Join a Ride , Create a Ride , Find a Ride , Events , Map Mode , your toolkit and help stay on the left, and your rides, group, public rides, feed and badges are beside them. Upright, it's one column. See Your Home Screen. Ride Mode on a Tablet The live map fills the screen. Riders sit in a list on the left with how fresh each rider's location is. Tap the arrow beside a rider to get directions to them. Tap Hide , or swipe the list to the left, to see more map; tap Show Riders to bring it back. The list starts open with the tablet sideways and folded with it upright. Your buttons (the route strip, quick replies and status buttons) sit in a panel on the right. Swipe it down or tap Hide to fold it, just like on a phone. Mechanical Issue and EMERGENCY always stay on screen. Directions and Add Waypoint sit just above the buttons panel. The ride name, your sharing timer and any announcement stay at the top of the left side. Tap Message at the top of the buttons panel to type a message to the group. It opens as a card in the middle of the screen. On a tablet, Ride Mode's pop-up cards (Share Your Location, EMERGENCY ) and sheets close when you swipe them down, just like on a phone. The round target button at the bottom of the map, just left of the buttons panel, centers the map on you. See Use Ride Mode. Follow Me sits just left of that button and keeps the map moving with you as you ride. Drag the map to look around and it pauses; tap Paused to follow you again. See Follow Me on the Map. Tap ⤢ Full Map at the top of the buttons panel to hide the riders list, the ride name and the buttons. A slim bar stays at the bottom right with the route line and EMERGENCY . See Use Ride Mode. Controls in that bar brings everything back (or swipe the bar up). Navigate, Draw a Route, Waypoints and Find a Ride have Full Map too; on a tablet their bar sits in the bottom-left corner. See Full Map. The Ride Page Once you've joined a ride, the ride and its details stay on the left, and Map , Riders and Chat open on the right. You can read the chat or check the route without losing the meeting time and place. Leave Ride is at the bottom of the left side of the ride page, and at the bottom of the Riders list in Ride Mode. See Join a Ride. Scout on a Tablet In Scout ( Find Places to Ride ), the distance slider, the filters and the list of places sit on the left and the map fills the rest of the screen, sideways or upright. A place's page puts its details on the left and its map beside them. Draw a Route and Add Waypoints With the tablet sideways, the route tools and the waypoint list sit in a panel beside the map. Swipe the panel up or tap Hide to fold it. With the tablet upright, the panel floats in the bottom corner of the map; swipe it down to fold it. A long swipe the way the panel folds (up beside the map, down

title: Use Ride Chat
summary: Message everyone on the ride or just the leader, post announcements, and clear or resolve your own messages.
headings: Clear or Resolve Your Own Message
Report or Block Someone in Chat
text: Every ride has its own chat for the riders on it. Use it to plan before the ride and check in after. Only riders who have joined the ride can read or post in it. Don't type while driving or riding. In Ride Mode, use the one-tap quick replies instead. See Send a Status or Quick Reply. In Ride Mode you can also tap Message to send the group a short message of your own, or one of your saved quick replies, once you've pulled over. See Type Your Own Message. Open Ride Chat Open the ride from the Rides tab. Tap Chat in the row of sections under the ride's name. Tap Ride Chat at the top of the card to hide or show the messages. Hidden, it shows the message count and the latest message. The chat shows the newest 30 messages. To see older ones, tap the button above them, such as Show 12 Earlier . Send a Message Under Send To , pick who it's for: Everyone: every rider on the ride. Leader Only: only you and the ride's leader see it. The leader's name is shown on the option. Type in the Message box. Tap Send to Everyone or Send to Leader . Your message shows in the chat straight away as Sending… , then Sent . If it doesn't go through, it stays as Not Sent with Retry and Remove . Messages can be up to 500 characters. If you send more than 10 messages in a minute, you're asked to wait a minute. The ride's leader is every rider with the Leader role. If nobody has been given that role, the organizer leads. Leader-only messages are kept private by the server, not just hidden in the app. If you're the leader, you won't see the Leader Only option. Post an Announcement Organizers and co-organizers can post an announcement for the whole group. Under Send To , pick Announcement (Pinned, Read Aloud) . Type in the Announcement box. Tap Post Announcement . The newest announcement is pinned near the top of the ride page. In Ride Mode it shows as a banner at the top with an amber edge and a megaphone, under the sender's name, and is read aloud, so riders don't have to look at their phones. Tap the banner to hear it again. Clear or Resolve Your Own Message Tap ••• next to a message you sent. Choose one: Mark Resolved: the message gets a green Resolved tag for everyone. Tap Reopen to undo it. Marking your latest announcement resolved takes it off the pinned spot. Clear: removes the message from the ride chat for everyone. Tap Clear again to confirm. This can't be undone. Only the person who sent a message can clear it or mark it resolved. Quick Replies in Chat Quick replies sent from Ride Mode, like On My Way , also show in the ride chat in italics. So do messages typed in Ride Mode with Message . With no service, a quick reply or message from a rider close by arrives over Bluetooth and shows here marked Via Bluetooth until OnMyLead has it. See Share With Nearby Riders With No Service. Message Pop-Ups When a new message arrives on a ride you're on, a pop-up slides in at the top of the screen, whatever screen you're on. Tap the pop-up to open the ride. Tap Dismiss to close it. When several are waiting, it shows +2 More and Dismiss All . Pop-ups close on their own after a few seconds, and announcements stay up a little longer. If the sender clears a message or marks it resolved before you see it, its pop-up goes away. Pop-ups and notifications follow your choices in Notifications . See Notification Settings. Report or Block Someone in Chat Press and hold someone else's message, then tap Report Rider or Block Rider . See Report or Block a Rider.

title: Your Garage
summary: Add your rig or side-by-side with a photo, fill details from the VIN, track every part of the build and see your fuel range.
headings: Fill In Details From the VIN
text: The Garage keeps your machines in one place: a photo, the details, every part you've added and how far a tank will take you. Open Your Garage Go to the You tab. Under Your Gear , tap Garage . You need to be signed in. Add a Machine Tap Add a Machine . Under What Are You Adding? , pick Vehicle or SXS/UTV . Tap Choose Photo to add a photo from your library (optional). On Android, the system photo picker opens, and OnMyLead only gets the photo you pick. Fill in a Nickname , or the Year , Make and Model . You need a nickname or a make and model. Trim is optional. Add the rest if you like: VIN , Purchase Price ($) , Engine Hours and Odometer (Miles) . Under Fuel and Mileage , enter Tank (gal) , any Extra Fuel (gal) you carry and Miles per Gallon . Use your real-world trail mileage, not the sticker. Under Trail Fit , enter the machine's Width (Inches) at its widest point, tire to tire. Trails with a width limit then tell you whether it fits, on the trail card, a trail's page and when you plan a ride on a trail. See Map Layers and Trails. Tap Add to Garage . Fill In Details From the VIN Type the 17-character VIN . Tap Fill Year, Make and Model From VIN . Check the year, make, model and trim it fills in. If there's no match, enter the details by hand. A VIN is 17 letters and numbers and never uses I, O or Q. See Your Fuel Range Once a machine has a tank size and mpg, its page shows a Fuel Range card: Full Range : how far you can go on your tank plus extra fuel. Safe Turnaround : a third of your full range. Turn around by this many miles out. Safe Trip : two thirds of your full range, the longest round trip that still keeps a third in reserve. It uses the thirds rule: a third out, a third back, a third in reserve. If a machine has no range yet, tap Add Fuel Range . Your Garage also powers the fuel check on a ride. See Fuel Range. Track Your Build Tracking parts, the Build Sheet and the CSV export are Pro features. See Free and Pro. Your machines, their specs and the fuel range stay free. Open a machine. Tap Add a Part or Extra . Pick the Area , like Wheels & Tires , Suspension , Lighting or Recovery . Enter the Item , and if you like the Brand , Cost ($) , Installed date (like 2026-05-01) and Notes . Tap Add . Parts are grouped by area with a subtotal for each. At the bottom you'll see the Build Total , and if you entered a purchase price, the Purchase Price and All In total. To change or remove a part, tap it, then tap Save or Remove Item . Export Your Build Under Export on a machine's page: Build Sheet shares your machine and its parts as text, to send in a message or paste anywhere. CSV saves the build list as a spreadsheet file you can send to Files, email or a spreadsheet app. Edit or Delete a Machine Open the machine. Tap Edit Machine to change its details or photo, then tap Save Changes . Or tap Delete , then confirm. The machine and all its build items are removed.

title: Control Your Music While You Ride
summary: Play, pause, skip songs and change the volume of the music on your phone from Ride Mode and Navigate, without leaving OnMyLead.
text: Music Controls let you pause, skip and turn the music up or down without switching apps, so the group map stays on your screen. They control the music already playing on your phone, from the app you play it in. Music controls are a Pro feature. See Free and Pro. On a Free account, the music button carries a Pro tag. Your music app itself keeps playing as usual. Open Music Controls In Ride Mode or Navigate , tap the round Music button with the music note. It sits on the right, just above Center on Me . The Music sheet shows what's playing and which app it's in, with big Previous Song , Play or Pause and Next Song buttons, and the volume with − and + . Swipe the sheet down or tap Close to go back to the map. In Full Map, the Music button sits in the bar at the bottom, between Controls and EMERGENCY . The buttons are big enough to use with gloves on, but pull over before you look at your phone. What Works on Your Phone Play, Pause and Skip Volume --- --- --- Android phone or tablet Any music or podcast app: Spotify, YouTube Music, Apple Music, Pandora, Amazon Music and more Yes iPhone or iPad Apple Music Yes, for any app onmylead.com No No On iPhone and iPad, Apple lets other apps control only Apple Music. When Spotify or another app is playing, the Music sheet says Playing in Another App and gives you the volume, plus Open Spotify if Spotify is on your phone (that leaves OnMyLead). Use the buttons on your headset or helmet communicator to skip. When nothing is playing, Play starts Apple Music. On Android, the buttons control whichever app last played music. To see the song name and the app's name, tap Show Song Names , then switch on OnMyLead Music Controls under Notification Access in Settings. Android shares what's playing only with apps you allow there. OnMyLead doesn't read your notifications, and the buttons work without it. On iPhone, tapping Show Song Names asks to let OnMyLead see the Apple Music song. If you said no before, it opens OnMyLead in Settings, where you can switch on Media & Apple Music . Hide the Music Button Don't want it? Tap Hide Music Button at the bottom of the Music sheet, or go to the You tab and switch off Music Controls . The button disappears from Ride Mode and Navigate. Switch Music Controls back on in the You tab any time. The setting is kept on each phone or tablet separately. From 2.1 you can also show or hide it from the map: tap the round Map Settings button, then switch Music Button under Map Buttons . What you listen to stays on your phone. OnMyLead doesn't send it to the server or show it to other riders.

title: Invite Friends and Get 50% Off Pro
summary: Invite a riding buddy who's new to OnMyLead. When they finish their first ride, you both get Pro Annual at half price for the first year.
text: Invite a riding buddy who's new to OnMyLead. When they finish their first ride, you both get Pro Annual for $14.99 your first year instead of $29.99. The discount comes from the App Store or Google Play, so it's billed the same way as any Pro subscription. Invite a Friend On the You tab, under Settings , tap Invite Friends . You can also tap Invite Friends, Both Get 50% Off at the bottom of the Pro screen. Tap Share Invite and send it, or tap Copy Link . Your invite link is your friend link, so your friend can also add you as a friend. See Add Friends. What Your Friend Does Opens your link and creates a new OnMyLead account within 7 days. Finishes a ride: leads one or joins one that starts (goes live), runs for at least 10 minutes and is ended. A ride that's ended without ever starting doesn't count. That's it. You both get a notification in the inbox, and the discount shows on Invite Friends and on the Pro screen. Claim Your Discount On Invite Friends (or the Pro screen), find You Earned 50% Off Pro Annual . Tap Claim 50% Off . On iPhone and iPad, the App Store opens with your personal offer code filled in. Confirm it there. If the App Store doesn't open, the code is shown on the card: tap Redeem Your Code to try again. On an Android phone or tablet, Google Play opens Pro Annual at the discounted price. Confirm the purchase there. Once the store confirms it, your plan changes to Pro . The first year costs $14.99. After that, Pro Annual renews at the regular price unless you cancel. See Manage Your Subscription. Already Paying for Pro On Google Play: Google Play offers are for new subscriptions only, so instead your next bill moves back 6 months. Tap Apply Your Reward . On the App Store: your code is used at your next renewal. A monthly plan moves up to Pro Annual at half price. On the website, the card says to claim the discount in the app. The Fine Print Each rider can earn the discount once. Your other invites still show under Your Invites . Your friend's account has to be new. Riders who already had an account can't be invited. You have 6 months to claim the discount. A discount you claimed in one store works in that store only. An Apple code is redeemed on an iPhone or iPad, and the Google Play offer on Android. If you see Invites aren't open right now , invites are paused. A discount you already earned can still be claimed.

title: The Rider Safety and Liability Agreement
summary: Why OnMyLead asks you to agree before you ride, what the agreement says, where to read it again, and what gets saved when you tap I Agree.
text: The first time you open OnMyLead, a Before You Ride screen shows the Rider Safety and Liability Agreement. Every rider agrees to it before using the app: on iPhone, iPad, Android phones and tablets, and on onmylead.com after you sign in. What It Says In short: you ride at your own risk, and you're responsible for riding safely. Riding and driving can lead to injury, death and damage, and you accept those risks. Never look at, type on or tap your phone while your vehicle is moving. Pull over first, or let a passenger use the app. Only ride where it's legal and allowed. Maps, routes, trails and waypoints, including ones other riders share, can be wrong, closed or on private land. OnMyLead is not an emergency or safety service. Alerts can be late or never arrive. In an emergency, call 911. See Emergencies and Staying Safe. Always call 911 in an emergency. The EMERGENCY button, Crash Alert, Need Help and the Emergency Siren only alert other riders on your ride who use OnMyLead. They don't call or text 911 or any rescue service, and they can be late or not work at all with no signal, a dead battery or Bluetooth out of range. If anyone is hurt or in danger, call 911 or your local emergency number first, then tell your group. You're responsible for what you do and for any accident you cause, and you release RUS Offroad LLC and OnMyLead from liability for your riding and your use of the app. If you're under 18, a parent or guardian agrees for you. The full text is at onmylead.com/rider-agreement. It's part of the Terms of Use. Agree to It Read the agreement on the Before You Ride screen. Scroll to see all of it. Tick the box that says I have read and agree to the Rider Safety and Liability Agreement, I accept the risks of riding, and I will always call 911 in an emergency . Tap I Agree . The button stays grey until the box is ticked. You're asked once, the first time you open the app. You won't see it again on that phone, tablet or browser, even after signing out, unless the agreement changes, in which case everyone is asked to agree to the new version. If you agree before you sign in, that answer counts for the account you sign in with next on that device. If you use a new phone or reinstall the app, it checks your account and doesn't ask again. Version 2 of the agreement (November 6, 2026) adds Always Call 911 in an Emergency , so after you update to OnMyLead 2.1 the Before You Ride screen shows once more. Read it, tick the box and tap I Agree to keep riding. No signal? Tapping I Agree works offline, so you can still use Ride Mode and Help and SOS. The app sends the record as soon as it's back online. The Terms of Use and Privacy Policy links on the screen open those pages. Go back to return to the agreement. Read It Again In the app: on the You tab, tap Safety Agreement at the bottom. On the website: Rider Safety Agreement at the bottom of the onmylead.com homepage, or go to onmylead.com/rider-agreement. What Gets Saved When you tap I Agree, OnMyLead saves a record of it: your account, email address and ride name, the version you agreed to and a fingerprint of its exact words, the time, the app version, the kind of device and its system version, your language, IP address and browser. Other riders never see it. The record can't be changed or deleted, and it's kept if you delete your account, because it's a legal record of what you agreed to. See the Privacy Policy.

title: Use OnMyLead on CarPlay
summary: During a ride, OnMyLead shows on your car's CarPlay screen with one-tap status buttons, your group, EMERGENCY and alerts when a rider falls behind.
text: If your truck, Jeep or car has Apple CarPlay, OnMyLead shows on the car's screen during a ride. You get big buttons for the status taps you use most, your group, and EMERGENCY, so you can keep your phone in the mount and your eyes on the trail. CarPlay works with iPhone. iPad, Android phones and Android tablets don't have it, and OnMyLead doesn't support Android Auto. CarPlay is part of OnMyLead Pro, including the Pro Trial. On a Free account the car screen says CarPlay Is Part of OnMyLead Pro , and Ride Mode, status taps and EMERGENCY keep working on your phone. See Free and Pro. Start CarPlay Connect your iPhone to the car, with a cable or wirelessly, the way you usually start CarPlay. Tap OnMyLead on the car screen. If you don't see it, swipe across the car's home screen, or add it in your iPhone's Settings General CarPlay your car Customize . Open Ride Mode for your ride on your phone. The car screen follows it. Until Ride Mode is open on your phone, the car screen says No Ride Running . What's on the Car Screen The top of the screen shows the ride's name and how the group is doing: Group Together , how many riders are separated, or the latest status another rider tapped. The buttons: Group lists every rider on the ride, with the leader and tail gunner marked. OK , Stopped , Need Fuel , Mechanical Issue and Need Help send that status to the group, the same as tapping it in Ride Mode on your phone. Regroup Here shows for the organizer and leader. Other riders get Running Late in its place. EMERGENCY asks once, Send EMERGENCY with your location to everyone on the ride? , and tap Alert My Group to send it. Cancel sends nothing. Typed messages, your own quick replies and the map stay on your phone. CarPlay only allows a few buttons, and typing while driving isn't safe. Alerts on the Car Screen When another rider taps a status, like Need Fuel , Mechanical Issue , Need Help or EMERGENCY , it pops up as an alert with their name. Tap OK to close it. OK taps don't alert anyone. The leader and the tail gunner also get an alert when a rider falls out of the Ride Bubble, the same alert the phone speaks. Language The car screen uses the language you picked in OnMyLead. See Language. Troubleshooting OnMyLead isn't on the car screen. Update OnMyLead from the App Store, then reconnect your iPhone to the car. The car screen says No Ride Running. Open Ride Mode for your ride on your phone. The car screen says CarPlay Is Part of OnMyLead Pro. Your account is on Free. Check You Subscription on your phone. A button did nothing. Status taps need the same signal as on your phone. With no service, they wait and send when you're back in range, just like in Ride Mode.

title: Choose the Voice for Spoken Alerts
summary: Pick the natural-sounding voice that reads Ride Mode alerts out loud, hear each one first, and download a better free voice that works with no service.
text: Ride Mode reads some things out loud so you don't have to look at your phone: announcements from the leader, Regroup Point Set , a rider falling behind the group (leader and tail gunner) and a Mechanical Issue tap. OnMyLead reads them in the most natural voice on your phone, and you can pick a different one. Every voice OnMyLead uses is stored on your phone, so spoken alerts keep working with no service. Picking a voice is a Pro feature. See Free and Pro. On a Free account, alerts are still read out loud with the Automatic voice. If you picked a voice before version 2.0, the app keeps it. Alerts are read in the language the app is in (see Change the App's Language). If the voice you picked speaks a different language, your phone's own voice for the app's language reads them instead. Pick a Voice Go to the You tab and tap Voice . Automatic is on to start. It uses the most natural voice on your phone, and the line under it says which one. Tap Play next to any voice to hear it say "Regroup point set. Sam is falling behind." Tap a voice to use it for spoken alerts. Tap Automatic to go back. Voices marked Premium sound the most natural, then Enhanced , then Standard . On Android, voices don't have names, so they're listed by language, such as US English Voice 1 , with Natural or Standard under each. If you delete the voice you picked, OnMyLead goes back to Automatic. Your choice follows your account to every device you sign in on. A phone or tablet that doesn't have that voice uses its best one. See Use OnMyLead on More Than One Device. Get a More Natural Voice Phones come with small standard voices, which can sound robotic. Better voices are a free download, and once downloaded they work with no service. If your phone has only standard voices, the Voice screen shows how to get one. iPhone and iPad: Open Settings Accessibility Read & Speak ( Spoken Content on older iOS) Voices English . Download a Premium or Enhanced voice, such as Zoe, Ava or Evan. You can play a sample there first. Premium voices are a few hundred MB, so download them on Wi-Fi. Go back to OnMyLead's Voice screen and tap Check Again . Automatic picks the new voice. Siri's own voice can't be used by apps. Android phones and tablets: Open Settings and search for Text-to-speech . Choose Speech Services by Google , then Install Voice Data , and download your language. Go back to OnMyLead's Voice screen and tap Check Again . Voices that need an internet connection are never used, so alerts don't go quiet when you lose service. Website: your browser decides which voices onmylead.com can use. Tips Spoken alerts play through whatever your phone is connected to: the speaker, earbuds or helmet comms. Spoken alerts still pause while your own phone has no service and other riders look quiet. See Ride Bubble.

title: Approvals and the Waitlist
summary: How join requests work on rides where the organizer approves riders, and how the waitlist fills open spots on a full ride.
headings: Leaving the Waitlist or a Request
text: Organizers can choose to approve each rider on a public ride, and can cap how many riders or vehicles come along. Here's what happens on both sides. Rides That Need Approval When creating a public ride, the organizer picks I Approve Riders under Joining . See Create a Ride. If You're Asking to Join Open the ride page. Tap Request to Join . The page shows "Your request is waiting for the organizer." You get a notification when you're approved. Until then you don't see the exact meeting point or the group. This is the same whether you found the ride on Find or opened it with its link, QR code or invite code. Only riders the organizer invited through a riding group skip approval. See Invite Riders. If You're the Organizer You get a notification when someone asks to join. Then: Open the ride page. The Riders section shows a red count of requests waiting. Tap Riders . Under Waiting for You , tap Approve or Decline next to each rider. If you set Max Riders or Max Vehicles and the ride is already full, a rider you approve goes on the waitlist instead. They move up automatically when a spot opens. The Waitlist If the organizer set Max Riders or Max Vehicles and the ride is full, new riders go on the waitlist. That includes riders the organizer approves and riders invited through a riding group. The page shows "You're on the waitlist. You'll move up automatically if a spot opens." When a rider leaves, riders on the waitlist move up in the order they joined, as long as they fit. You get a notification when you have a spot. The Spots line on the ride page shows how full the ride is, like "8 of 10 vehicles". Riders on the ride can see how many are on the waitlist under the Going list. Leaving the Waitlist or a Request Open the ride page and tap Withdraw at the bottom, then confirm. Or swipe left on the ride on the Rides tab and tap Leave . You can ask again later with the ride's link or code. If the ride is cancelled, riders who asked to join or are on the waitlist get a notification and an email too.

title: Ask the Group with a Ride Poll
summary: Leaders post a quick question in ride chat, like a lunch stop or the pace, and every rider votes with one tap.
text: A ride poll is a quick question in the ride chat with a few choices. Every rider on the ride gets one vote, can change it, and sees the live counts. Who Can Post a Poll The ride's leader, the organizer and co-organizers can post polls. Every rider on the ride can vote. Creating a poll: This is a Pro feature. See Free and Pro. On a Free plan, picking Quick Poll shows Create Ride Polls , marked Pro, instead of the poll form. Voting stays free for everyone. From version 2.0, voting on a poll is also a Pro feature. On a Free account, the vote line carries a Pro tag. Reading a poll and its results stays free. Post a Poll Open the ride and tap Chat . Under Send To , pick Quick Poll . Tap a starter to fill it in, or type your own: Lunch Stop? (Yes, No) How's the Pace? (Too Slow, Just Right, Too Fast) Saturday or Sunday? Morning or Afternoon? Type or edit the Question . Fill in Choice 1 and Choice 2 . Tap Add Choice for more, or Remove to drop one. Tap Post Poll . The poll shows in the chat for everyone, and riders get a pop-up saying "Poll from" your name. Poll Limits 2 to 5 choices, each different. The question can be up to 200 characters. Each choice can be up to 60 characters. Vote Open the ride and tap Chat . Tap a choice. It's marked Your Vote . To change your vote, tap another choice. Each choice shows its count and a bar for its share of the votes, and the leading choice is shaded darker. Under the choices you'll see the total, such as 3 Votes , or No Votes Yet . Remove a Poll The person who posted the poll can tap ••• next to it and tap Clear . The poll and its votes are removed for everyone.

title: Emergencies and Staying Safe
summary: What the EMERGENCY button does and doesn't do, how Need Help works, and how to ride safer with OnMyLead. OnMyLead is not an emergency service.
text: OnMyLead is not an emergency service. It does not contact 911, search and rescue, or anyone outside your ride. If anyone is hurt, call 911 or your local emergency number first. OnMyLead helps your group keep track of each other. Phones lose signal, batteries die, and positions can be late or wrong, so use it alongside your own plan, not instead of one. Every rider agrees to the Rider Safety and Liability Agreement before using the app: you ride at your own risk, never use the phone while moving, and only ride where it's allowed. See The Rider Safety and Liability Agreement. Everything on this page is free on every plan. None of it needs Pro. What EMERGENCY Does The EMERGENCY button in Ride Mode alerts everyone on your ride at once. In Ride Mode, tap EMERGENCY . It stays on screen even when the bottom panel is folded. Read the Emergency screen. If you're sharing your location, it shows your coordinates in large type, so you can read them out on a call. Press and hold Alert My Group for 1.5 seconds. A bar fills across the button and it says Keep Holding . When the bar is full, your phone buzzes, the screen closes and the alert goes out. If you let go early, it says Not sent and nothing goes to the group. With VoiceOver or TalkBack, double tap and hold, or use the Send action. If anyone is hurt, tap Call 911 to open your phone's dialer. Tap Cancel to close the screen without sending anything. In Full Map, EMERGENCY stays in the slim bar at the bottom of the screen, so it's still one tap away. When the alert goes out: Every rider on the ride gets a notification, "EMERGENCY: your name needs help now", with "Tap to see where they are." It shows in red on their Ride Mode screen. If you're sharing your location, they see you on the map and can tap Navigate to get directions to you. Help and EMERGENCY notifications are always on for every rider, even in quiet hours, and they come through even from a rider someone has blocked. Their phones sound a loud Emergency Siren until they silence it, unless they turned it off. See Hear the Emergency Siren. You see a card showing whose phones have the alert. If you sent it by mistake, tap Cancel on the card and the group is told to ignore it. See Send a Status or Quick Reply. Crash Alert can also send it for you: if your phone detects a hard hit or a rollover in Ride Mode and you don't tap I'm OK within 30 seconds, your group gets the EMERGENCY alert with your location. See Use the Tilt Meter and Crash Alert. What EMERGENCY Doesn't Do It doesn't call or text 911, emergency services, or anyone else. It doesn't reach anyone who isn't on the ride. With no service, it reaches only riders on the ride within Bluetooth range (about 30 to 100 meters, passed along by up to six phones), and it waits on your phone and sends by itself when you get signal. If any nearby rider's phone gets signal first, it sends the alert for you. See Share With Nearby Riders With No Service. Need Help Need Help is for when you need the group but it isn't an emergency. It sends with one tap, shows in red for the group, and notifies everyone on the ride the same way, including during quiet hours. When things are sorted, tap Resolved, I'm OK so the group knows. Ride Safer Call 911 first in an emergency, then alert your group. Share your location for the whole ride , so Ride Bubble and the group can see you, and so riders can find you if you call for help. See Share Your Location. Send a family link to someone at home, and tell them when you expect to be back. See Share a Family Link. Download the ride's map before you lose signal. The map keeps working offline, but positions only update with a connection. See Offline Maps. Allow notifications so you hear when someone needs help. See Notification Settings. Allow location Always , so your group can see you with your phone locked. On Android, allow location While Using the App : the Sharing Your Location notification keeps your group seeing you with the phone locked. Need Help and E

title: Leader, Sweep and Tail Gunner
summary: Who rides up front, who rides at the rear, and how to make someone leader, pick a tail gunner or hand off the ride.
text: Every group ride needs someone up front and someone at the back. OnMyLead shows the riding order on the roster: the leader first, the tail gunner last, everyone else in between. The Roles Organizer : the rider who created the ride (or was given it). Runs the ride page, starts and ends Ride Mode, and leads unless someone else is made leader. Leader : rides up front. Messages sent to the leader in ride chat go to them. Tail Gunner : rides at the rear so nobody gets left behind. In OnMyLead, the tail gunner is the sweep. Rider : everyone else. On the Riders section of the ride page, the line at the top of the Going list shows who is Leader and who is Tail Gunner (or "Not picked yet"). On the Map In Ride Mode the leader and the tail gunner stand out from everyone else: the leader is the biggest dot, in blue with a blue name tag, and the tail gunner is the next biggest, in violet with a violet name tag. Every other rider is a graphite dot with a dark name tag. The riders list uses the same colors. A blue line also follows behind the leader on every rider's map, so the group can see exactly where the leader went. The leader can turn it off for everyone in Map Settings . See Follow the Leader's Trackline. Make Someone Leader The organizer can put another rider up front while still organizing. On the ride page, tap Riders . Tap the rider's name in the Going list. Tap Make Leader . To take the lead back, tap their name and tap Remove as Leader . You can make more than one rider a leader. Pick a Tail Gunner The organizer or the leader can pick the one rider who rides at the rear. On the ride page, tap Riders . Tap the rider's name. Tap Make Tail Gunner . There's only one tail gunner at a time. Picking someone new moves the job to them. To clear it, tap the tail gunner's name and tap Remove as Tail Gunner . The leader and organizers ride up front, so they can't also be tail gunner. Hand Off the Lead A rider who was made leader can pass the lead to someone else. On the ride page, tap Riders . Tap the rider's name. Tap Hand Them the Lead , then Hand Off . They lead from here, messages to the leader go to them, and you stay on the ride as a rider. Give Away the Whole Ride The organizer can hand the entire ride to another rider, for example if you can't make it. On the ride page, tap Riders . Tap the rider's name. Tap Give Them the Ride , then Give Ride . They become the organizer and the leader. You stay on the ride as a rider and can't undo this yourself. Leave a Ride You Organize Can't make it? You don't have to cancel the ride on everyone. Tap Leave Ride at the bottom of the ride page (or under Riders in Ride Mode). Who Takes Over? lists everyone who has joined, leaders and co-organizers first. Tap who should run it. Tap Give Ride and Leave . They become the organizer and the leader, and you're off the ride. Your location sharing for the ride stops. You can rejoin later as a rider with the ride's link or code. Rather call it off? Tap Cancel the Ride Instead . If nobody else has joined yet, Leave Ride offers to cancel the ride, since there's nobody to hand it to. See Edit, Cancel or Delete a Ride. If you were made leader (but aren't the organizer) and you leave, the lead goes back to the organizer. Roles can only go to riders who have joined the ride, and they can't change after the ride has ended or been cancelled. The rider gets a notification when they're made leader, made tail gunner or given the ride. Leading a ride earns toward the Trail Boss badge, and riding at the rear as tail gunner earns toward Tail Gunner . See Earn Badges and Ranks.

title: Map Layers and Trails
summary: Switch between satellite and topo, pick which roads, trails and land boundaries show in Map Features, and tap a trail or a piece of land to see who can ride it.
headings: See Who Can Ride a Trail
text: OnMyLead's maps can show public trails and roads over satellite imagery or a topo map. Tap a trail to see its name and which vehicles are allowed on it. Satellite, topo and the trails layer are Pro features. See Free and Pro. On a Free account, Map Style carries a Pro tag and the map shows the standard map. Open the Layers The round Map Settings button (a two-slider icon) is in the top-left corner of the map, level with the compass on the right (the compass shows once the map is turned away from north). While a screen's top bar is showing, both sit just under it so nothing covers them; in Full Map they move up to the top of the screen and stay there. On an iPad or Android tablet, Ride Mode puts the button just right of the riders column, and Map Mode, the route builder and the waypoints map held sideways put it just right of the panel. On onmylead.com the compass is with the zoom buttons instead. You'll find it on: Ride Mode's map Map Mode A ride's waypoints map The route builder The area picker for offline maps Tap it to open Map Settings (below). Swipe the sheet down, tap the map, or tap X to close it. In Ride Mode the leader and the ride's organizers also see Leader Trackline in Map Settings, to turn the line behind the leader on or off for everyone. See Follow the Leader's Trackline. Map Settings From 2.1 the stacked-layers button is the round Map Settings button, with a two-slider icon, and it opens Map Settings , one sheet for everything about the map. On a phone it slides up from the bottom; on a tablet held sideways it sits on the right so you can watch the map change. The map stays lightly visible behind it, so each change shows as you make it. Swipe it down, tap the map, or tap X to close it. A small blue dot on the button means the map isn't showing the standard set. Map Style : Satellite , Topo and 3D Terrain , each shown as a picture. The one you're using has a blue ring and a check. On the Map : four big switches, each with a strip of map showing the lines it draws: Streets and Roads : highways, paved roads, dirt roads and street-legal-only roads. Off-Road Trails : motorized trails and tracks, including width-limited trails. Hiking Trails : foot and horse trails. Land Boundaries : national forests, BLM land, national and state parks. Turning it on leaves Property Lines off; turn that on under Every Map Feature . A switch is on while any of its lines shows. Tapping it turns them all off, or all on. Every Map Feature : tap Fine-Tune to open the full list below, one row per kind of line or land. Leader Trackline : for the leader and organizers in Ride Mode. Your Dot (Ride Mode and Map Mode): Dot Style picks how your own dot looks: Red, White and Blue (a glossy navy dome with a white arrow inside a red band and a white rim, the default; a white star when your phone can't tell which way you're facing), Safety Orange (an orange 3D dome with a white arrow and a silver rim), Hi-Viz Dome (lime with a black arrow), Reflective Ring , Floating Arrowhead or Classic (the cyan dot). Dot Size sets how big it is: Small , Medium or Large . Both are also on the You tab. Picking a style or size other than Red, White and Blue at Medium is part of OnMyLead Pro; on Free the picker shows the Pro tag and your dot stays the default. Following (Ride Mode and Map Mode): Follow Me keeps your dot on screen; Zoom Out at the Edge zooms out one step the first time your dot nears an edge, then the next time the map centers on you and moves with you; Zoom In at Intersections (on the Mapbox map) closes in on a junction so you can see which way to go. See Follow Me. Map Buttons (Ride Mode and Map Mode): Tilt Meter (iPhone, iPad and Android) and Music Button (where music controls are available). Download This Ride's Map (Ride Mode), Offline Maps , and who the map data comes from. The Your Dot, Following and Map Buttons settings are the same ones as on the You tab, so a change shows everywhere. The round 3D button from earlier 2.1 test builds is gone:

title: Plan a Trip and Packing List
summary: Make a packing checklist for a trip, tick things off as they go in the rig, and reset or copy it for next time.
headings: Link a Trip to a Ride
text: The Trip Planner keeps a packing list for each trip. Tick items off as they go in the rig, and reuse the list next time. Open the Trip Planner Go to the You tab. Under Your Gear , tap Trip Planner . You need to be signed in. Plan a New Trip Tap Plan a New Trip . Enter a Trip Name , like "Moab long weekend". Add dates if you like: Starts and Ends , written like 2026-10-12. Ends is optional. If you have machines in your Garage, pick the one you're Taking . Tap Create Trip . Free accounts plan one trip at a time. A trip counts until its last day has passed. Planning several trips at once is part of Pro. See Free and Pro. Add Items On the trip, tap Add an Item . Enter the Item , like "Tow strap". Set How Many with the number box or the minus and plus buttons. Pick a Category , like Recovery , First Aid , Camping or Food & Water . Add Notes if you like, such as size or where it lives in the rig. Tap Add . Items are grouped by category, each showing how many are packed. Start From a Starter List Tap Add a Starter List and pick one, like Day Ride , Overnight / Camping , Desert , Mountain / Snow , Recovery Kit , First Aid , Tools & Spares or Starlink / Power . One tap adds the items. You can add more than one list, and nothing is added twice. This is a Pro feature. See Free and Pro. Tick Items Off Tap anywhere on an item's row to check it off. Tap again to uncheck it. The bar at the top shows how much is packed. When everything is checked, it turns green and says so, like All 24 packed. To change or remove an item, tap Edit on its row, then tap Save or Remove Item . After the Trip Under After the Trip : Uncheck All puts every item back to not packed. The list stays. Copy to a New Trip starts a new trip with the same list. This is a Pro feature. See Free and Pro. On the Free plan, the buttons that need Pro carry a small gold Pro tag, so you know before you tap. Tapping one shows what Pro includes. During your Pro Trial and on Pro there are no tags. Link a Trip to a Ride When you create or edit a trip, you can pick a ride you've joined under For a Ride . The trip then shows a link to that ride. This is a Pro feature. See Free and Pro. Edit or Delete a Trip Open the trip. Tap Edit Trip to change the name, dates, machine or ride, then tap Save . Or tap Delete , then confirm. The trip and all its items are removed. Gear Suggestions A trip's page may show Gear From RUS Offroad , with products that fit your list and machine. See Gear From RUS Offroad.

title: Redeem a Promo Code
summary: Got an OnMyLead promo code? Redeem it in the app through Apple to get OnMyLead Pro with the offer it includes.
headings: Redeem a Code in the App
Redeemed It in the App Store Instead?
text: OnMyLead promo codes are Apple offer codes for OnMyLead Pro. You redeem them through Apple, right from the app. Redeem a Code in the App On the You tab, under Settings , tap Subscription . Tap Redeem Promo Code . Enter your code in Apple's window and follow the steps to confirm. Apple shows what the code gives you before you confirm. Once Apple accepts the code, OnMyLead checks it and your plan changes to Pro . This can take a moment. You can also tap Redeem Promo Code at the bottom of the Pro screen. A 50% off code you earned by inviting a friend opens from Invite Friends with the code already filled in. See Invite Friends and Get 50% Off Pro. Redeem a Code on Android On Android, OnMyLead promo codes are Google Play promo codes. On the You tab, under Settings , tap Subscription . Tap Redeem Promo Code . Google Play's Redeem Code page opens. Enter your code and follow the steps to confirm. Come back to OnMyLead. Once Google Play has the code, your plan changes to Pro . You can also redeem a code in the Play Store app: tap your profile picture, then Payments & Subscriptions Redeem Code . A Google Play code works only on Google Play, and an Apple offer code works only in the App Store. Redeemed It in the App Store Instead? That works too. Open OnMyLead afterwards, signed in to your account, with signal. The app picks up the code on its own and turns on Pro. Good to Know A promo code becomes an OnMyLead Pro subscription with your Apple Account. Manage or cancel it like any subscription. See Manage or Cancel Your Subscription. Promo codes can only be redeemed in the app on your phone or tablet, not on the website. If your plan doesn't change to Pro, make sure you have signal and are signed in to the right OnMyLead account, then tap Restore Purchases . See Restore Purchases.

title: Hear the Emergency Siren
summary: When a rider in your group sends EMERGENCY or a Crash Alert goes out, your phone sounds a loud siren until you silence it. Here's how it works and how to turn it off.
headings: With OnMyLead Closed or in the Background
Hear It or Turn It Off
text: OnMyLead is not an emergency service. The siren only reaches riders on your ride. If anyone is hurt, call 911 or your local emergency number first. When another rider on your ride sends EMERGENCY , your phone sounds a loud siren so you notice it over wind, engines and helmets. It keeps going until you silence it. It's free on every plan and it starts on. What Sounds the Siren A rider presses and holds Alert My Group on the Emergency screen in Ride Mode, or sends EMERGENCY from CarPlay. A rider's Crash Alert countdown runs out, or they tap Alert My Group Now on it. See Use the Tilt Meter and Crash Alert. Need Help and the other status buttons don't sound the siren; they come with the usual notification sound. Your own EMERGENCY never sounds the siren on your phone. With OnMyLead Open The siren takes over the whole screen, on any screen in the app, and it says who needs help. Your phone buzzes with it, it plays even with the ring/silent switch on silent, and any music you're playing turns down under it. On Android, with OnMyLead open, the siren plays at your phone's media volume, so keep media volume up on a ride. Tap Show Me Where to silence it and open Ride Mode with their location, so you can tap Navigate to them. Tap Silence Siren to silence it and stay where you are. If you lock your phone or switch to another app before silencing it (say, to call 911), the siren stops and a quiet notification stays on your lock screen; tap it to see where they are. If more than one rider needs help, the newest shows first, with how many more riders need help. Silence Siren silences all of them; Show Me Where silences only that rider's, and the next rider who needs help shows right after. The siren stops by itself if the rider cancels their EMERGENCY or taps another status like I'm OK (with no service, a cancel doesn't travel over Bluetooth, so ask them to tap I'm OK ). If they take back that I'm OK, the siren doesn't come back; a rider who still needs help taps EMERGENCY again. An EMERGENCY you've silenced never sounds again on that phone, and one older than 10 minutes doesn't sound when you open Ride Mode later; it still shows in red there. One that reaches you late while Ride Mode is open (say the rider had no service when they sent it) still sounds when it arrives. With OnMyLead Closed or in the Background The EMERGENCY notification plays the siren as its sound, for about 27 seconds. Tap the notification to open Ride Mode at their location; the siren doesn't start again in the app. iPhone and iPad: the siren follows your ring/silent switch, like any notification. It's a Time Sensitive notification, so it comes through a Focus if you allow Time Sensitive notifications for OnMyLead in Settings Notifications OnMyLead . Android phones and tablets: the siren has its own notification channel, Emergency Siren , and plays as an alarm, so you hear it with the ringer on silent. Do Not Disturb can still hold it back; to let it through, open Settings Apps OnMyLead Notifications Emergency Siren and allow it to override Do Not Disturb. If you turn the Emergency Siren channel off there, EMERGENCY notifications come with the usual ride alert sound instead. With No Service With Bluetooth Sharing (on every plan for EMERGENCY), an EMERGENCY from a rider within Bluetooth range sounds the siren in Ride Mode too. If OnMyLead is in the background, you get a notification with the siren that says it was sent over Bluetooth. On the Website Ride Mode on onmylead.com sounds the siren while the page is open. Your browser may only play it after you've tapped or clicked the page once. The website doesn't send notifications. Hear It or Turn It Off Go to the You tab. Under Settings , tap Notifications . Tap Play Siren to hear it for three seconds. Switch Emergency Siren off if you'd rather not hear it. EMERGENCY notifications still come through, with the normal notification sound. With Sync Across Devices (Pro), your choice follows your account to your other devices.

title: 3D Terrain
summary: See the satellite map on the real shape of the land in Ride Mode and Map Mode, with contour lines and peak heights in feet, and tilt and turn it.
headings: On iPhone, iPad, Android and the Website
text: 3D Terrain shows the satellite map draped over the real shape of the land, so you can see ridges, canyons and climbs before you ride them. Contour lines and peak heights are drawn on top, along with every trail layer. Turn On 3D Terrain Open Ride Mode or Map Mode. Tap the round Map Settings button (two sliders) in the top-left corner of the map. Under Map Style , tap 3D Terrain . The map tilts to show the land in 3D. To lay it flat again, tap Satellite or Topo under Map Style . Your choice is remembered and used in Ride Mode and Map Mode. Other maps, like the route builder and Find a Ride, show plain satellite while 3D Terrain is picked. 3D Terrain is a map style, so like the other map styles it's a Pro feature. See Free and Pro. Move Around in 3D Tilt : drag up or down with two fingers. The further you tilt, the steeper the land is drawn: looking straight down it's true to life, and at the steepest tilt hills and canyons stand up to three times their real height, so a ridge reads at a glance. Tilt back and it settles down again. Turn : twist with two fingers. The compass in the corner shows north; tap it to face north again. Zoom and pan : pinch and drag, as on any map. On the website, right-drag or hold Ctrl and drag to tilt and turn (two fingers on a touch screen), or use the zoom, compass and tilt buttons in the bottom-left corner. Tilting further raises the land there too. What's on the Map Contour lines : thin white lines, with every fifth line heavier and labeled in feet when you zoom in. Peaks : mountain names with their height in feet. Trails and roads : the same public trail, road, closure and rider trail lines as the flat maps. See Map Layers and Trails. Your ride : rider dots, the route, waypoints, planned stops and the regroup pin in Ride Mode; your recording, followed trail, Track Line and the distance finder in Map Mode. Follow Me and Center on Me work the same as on the flat map. With No Signal 3D Terrain needs a signal, or an area saved for it ahead of time. In Offline Maps, add 3D Terrain to a download. With no signal, the 3D map shows over saved areas; anywhere else the app shows the flat downloaded map instead, so you always have a map. On iPhone, iPad, Android and the Website 3D Terrain works the same on iPhone, iPad, Android phones and tablets, and on the website in Ride Mode and Map Mode. Every map in the app is drawn by Mapbox from 2.1, so the other maps look the same as this one, just flat. See Map Layers and Trails.

title: Use the Tilt Meter and Crash Alert
summary: See your vehicle's roll and pitch, get warned before a steep lean, and have OnMyLead alert your group if it detects a crash.
text: The tilt meter shows how far your vehicle leans side to side ( Roll ) and tips nose up or down ( Pitch ), using the motion sensors in your phone or tablet. It works with no signal. Crash Alert uses the same sensors to spot a likely crash in Ride Mode and tell your group if you don't answer. See Your Tilt The Tilt tile shows your roll and pitch over the map: In Map Mode , under your speed and the dash. In Ride Mode , on the left side of the map above the panel. On a tablet it sits in the map's bottom-left corner. It hides in Full Map and when there isn't room. The numbers turn amber as you get close to your limit and red at it. Tap the tile to open the full Tilt screen, with an axle seen from behind that leans with your roll, two wheels seen from the side that tip with your pitch, and the biggest lean each way under each one. Tap Reset Max to clear those (it shows once the meter is calibrated). You can also open it from the You tab: tap Tilt and Crash Alert . The screen stays on while it's open, so you can leave it up on your mount. Turn the Tilt Meter Off Don't want it? At the top of the Tilt screen, under the Crash Alert switch, tap Tilt Meter On to turn it off. The Tilt tile leaves Map Mode and Ride Mode, the Tilt screen hides the readings, and tilt warnings stop. Crash Alert keeps working on its own switch. Tap Tilt Meter Off to bring it back. The switch follows your account to your other devices. The same switch is under Map Buttons in Map Settings : tap the round Map Settings button on Ride Mode's or Map Mode's map and switch Tilt Meter . Calibrate It for Your Mount The tilt meter is off until you calibrate it, because your phone probably doesn't sit flat in its mount. Until then the Tilt screen shows Calibrate instead of readings, and the tile in Map Mode and Ride Mode says Calibrate Tilt . Tilt warnings don't buzz, and Crash Alert only watches for hard hits, not rollovers. Place your phone where it will be mounted, with the vehicle on flat and level ground. Open Tilt and press Calibrate , then Calibrate again to confirm. That reading becomes level, and the meter turns on. After that the button says Zero : press it again whenever you move the phone or switch vehicles. The calibration is kept on this phone only, since each phone sits differently. Tap Clear Zero to remove it, which turns the meter off until you calibrate again. Tilt Warnings With Warn Me on, your phone buzzes when you lean past your limit for more than a moment, and again every few seconds while you stay past it. Set your own limits with Roll Limit and Pitch Limit (10° to 45°; they start at 25° roll and 30° pitch). Turn on Say It Out Loud to also hear the angle, such as "Roll 28 left". Every vehicle tips at a different angle, and load, tires and ground all change it. The limits are reminders, not a promise you won't roll. On a motorcycle, turn Warn Me off, since leaning into turns is normal. To hide the tile, turn the Tilt Meter off at the top of the screen. Your limits and these switches follow your account to your other devices. Crash Alert Crash Alert is on unless you turn it off. To turn it on or off, open the Tilt screen and tap the Crash Alert On / Crash Alert Off switch at the top. The switch follows your account to your other devices. While Ride Mode is open, it watches for a hard hit or (once you've zeroed the tilt meter) a rollover while you're riding, followed by your vehicle stopping. When it sees one: A full-screen countdown starts at 30 seconds, with vibration and a spoken warning. Tap I'm OK to cancel. Nothing is sent. If nobody taps I'm OK , your group gets the same EMERGENCY alert as the Emergency button, with your location, plus a chat message saying your phone detected a possible crash. Tap Alert My Group Now to send it straight away. To cancel and stop Crash Alert for now, tap I'm OK, Turn Off Crash Alert under the buttons. Turn it back on from the top of the Tilt screen. If a sheet such as Map Settings is open when the countdown starts

title: Offroad Park Trails
summary: Every map shows the trails of offroad parks like Hidden Falls, colored by the park's own levels and named, so you know a park before you ride it.
text: OnMyLead draws the trails of offroad parks on every map: Ride Mode, Map Mode, the route builder, waypoints, Find a Ride and the maps on onmylead.com. Hidden Falls Adventure Park, Katemcy Rocks, Wolf Caves, General Sam's, Hollister Hills, Hungry Valley, Ocotillo Wells, Interlake, SMORR, Sand Mountain and about fifty more parks and OHV areas are in, with their trail names and, where the park rates its trails, the park's own levels. See a Park's Trails Open any map and zoom in to about a county's width. Park trails draw as solid lines with a dark edge , so they don't look like the dashed amber agency trails or the mint dotted rider trails.
