From farther out, each park's name sits on the map with how many trails and miles are mapped (trails only, not the park's roads), so you can see where the parks are while you pan across the state. Zoom in closer and the trail names appear along the lines. Park trails show for everyone, signed in or not, and they're on unless you turn them off. What the Colors Mean Where a park rates its trails (Hidden Falls does, level 1 to 5), the line takes the color of that level, the same colors as trailhead signs and rider trails: Green : level 1 and 2, the easiest. Blue : level 3. White : level 4. Red : level 5, the hardest. Amber : a trail the park hasn't rated. Thin white : a park road. Red dashes : a trail the park has closed. The key is in Map Settings : tap Fine-Tune under Every Map Feature , and the Park Trails row in the Trails group shows the four level colors. Tap a Trail Tap a park trail to see its card: the park's name, the trail's name, its level (or Park Road / Trail when it has none), its length, and whether it's one way. The card reminds you that levels and lines come from OpenStreetMap, the open map that riders and parks contribute to, so check the park's posted map too: trails change after storms and work days, and a park may re-rate a trail before the map catches up. Turn Park Trails Off Tap the round Map Settings button on any map, tap Fine-Tune under Every Map Feature , then tap the Park Trails row in the Trails group to turn it off. The same choice is on the You tab as Park Trails on Maps . Either one changes every map, on every device you're signed in on. Park Trails is free for everyone, like Rider Trails, so it stays even without Pro. With No Signal A park you've looked at while connected stays on your phone, so its trails draw again at the park with no service. Parks you've never opened need a signal the first time. Where the Trails Come From Park trails are OpenStreetMap data (© OpenStreetMap contributors), published under the Open Database License, which allows OnMyLead to show them with that credit. OnMyLead never copies a park's own copyrighted map. A park that isn't on the map yet simply isn't mapped in OpenStreetMap; anyone, including the park, can add its trails there and they'll come into OnMyLead with the next park update. If a line is wrong or a trail is gone, use Contact Us on the You tab and name the park and the trail. The OnMyLead team can take a line off the map right away.

title: Check In
summary: Let the group know you've made it to the meeting spot with one tap, and see who's already there.
text: Checking in tells the organizer and the rest of the group that you're at the meeting spot and ready to ride. Check In Open the ride page. Tap I'm Here and Ready . The button changes to "Checked in at" and the time you tapped it. You can check in once you've joined the ride, until the ride ends. Checking in doesn't use your location. It does need a connection, so if the trailhead has no signal, check in before you lose it. See Who's Here On the ride page, tap Riders . Riders who checked in show Here under their name in the Going list. Organizers use this to see who's made it before starting Ride Mode. Once you've checked in, you can't undo it. Need help getting to the meeting spot? Directions are on the ride page once you've joined. See Directions.

title: Events
summary: Find rallies, poker runs and ride weekends, see the agenda and join the group rides. Pro riders post events with photos, co-hosts and Ride Managers.
headings: Add Photos, the Agenda and Group Rides
text: Events are the big days: a rally, a poker run, a club weekend or a meetup. An event has its dates, a place, photos, an Agenda of what's happening and when (group rides, poker runs, concerts, raffles, shows, food), and the Group Rides you can join. Anyone can see events. Pro riders create them. Event or Public Ride? They're different things, and an event can hold public rides. A Public Ride is one ride on one day: a leader, a meeting point and a time. Anyone nearby finds it in Find a Ride , joins it, and you ride together in Ride Mode. See Find a Ride and Create a Ride. An Event is a bigger gathering, like a rally, poker run or ride weekend. It has dates, a place, photos, an agenda and Going or Interested , and it can hold several group rides that you join one by one. Just riding? Create a Public Ride. Running a rally or a weekend? Create an Event and add its rides to it. In the app, Event or Public Ride? on Events, Find a Ride, Create a Ride and Create an Event opens the same explanation. Tap What's the Difference? to open it and Hide to close it. It's the same on iPhone, iPad, Android and the website. Find an Event On the Rides tab, tap the gold Events card (under Create a Ride, Find a Ride and Map Mode). Coming Up lists public events, soonest first. With location allowed, it shows the ones within your distance (the same distance as Public Rides Near You); tap the distance chip to change it. Tap an event to open it. Yours lists the events you host, co-host, or said you're going or interested in, including ones from the last 30 days. Event links look like onmylead.com/e/ followed by a code. Anyone can open one, even without the app; on the website, names of riders only show once you sign in. On Android the link opens in the app. On iPhone and iPad it opens on onmylead.com for now. On an Event's Page Going and Interested tell the hosts you're coming (tap again to take it back). The count is public; the names of riders going show only to signed-in riders. Share sends the event's link. Directions opens the place in Apple Maps or Google Maps. Agenda shows each day in time order. Group rides and poker runs are marked red, raffles, contests and shows gold, everything else blue. Group Rides lists the event's rides, with their label (like Day 1: Easy Group ), time, area, how many are going and the Ride Manager . Tap See Ride and Join to open the ride and join it as usual. A private ride shows Invite Only: Ask a Host unless you're already on it. A ride that's part of an event shows Part of and the event's name at the top of its page. Presented By Some events are presented (sponsored) by a company. Those show Presented by and the name in gold on their card in Events and near the top of their page. When RUS Offroad presents an event, the page also has Shop RUS Offroad , which opens the RUS Offroad store. Hosts can't add this themselves: the OnMyLead team sets it for a sponsor. Interested in presenting an event? Use Contact Us. Create an Event (Pro) Open Events and tap Create an Event . On Free, the button carries a small gold Pro tag and opens the Pro prompt. Give it a name and details, and pick Public (shows in Events for everyone) or Link Only (only people with the link). Under When , pick the first day and the start time. For more than one day, tap Several Days and pick the last day (up to 31 days). Under Where , search a place or tap the map, and check the Place Name . Everyone who sees the event sees this place, so pick a public spot like a venue, park, campground or trailhead. Add a website or ticket link if there is one, and tap Create Event . From 2.1 the map under Where is on every device, not only the website, and opens near where you are: tap it to drop the place, and drag the pin to fine-tune it. The event opens, ready for the rest. Add Photos, the Agenda and Group Rides Hosts see extra buttons on the event's page: Add Photos picks up to 12 photos (on iPhone, iPad and Android you can also Take a Photo ). The app shrinks each

title: Offline Maps
summary: Download a ride's map or any area before you leave, so the map and route are still there when the signal drops. A Pro feature.
text: Out on the trail the signal often drops. Download a map before you leave and the map keeps working with no signal: satellite photos, topo and trail lines for the area you saved. This is a Pro feature. See Free and Pro. Maps already on your phone keep working on the Free plan. On the Free plan, the buttons that need Pro carry a small gold Pro tag, so you know before you tap. Tapping one shows what Pro includes. During your Pro Trial and on Pro there are no tags. Offline maps keep the map, not the tracking. With no signal, your phone can't send or receive positions. Riders show where they were last seen, and positions update again when phones get a connection. Offline maps are in the app on your phone or tablet only, not on the website. Open Offline Maps On the You tab, tap Offline Maps . Or, on any map with the layers button, open the layers panel and tap Offline Maps . The screen shows how much space your maps use, how much is free on your phone, your downloads under On This Phone , and your upcoming rides under Your Rides . Areas you downloaded on your other devices (signed in with the same account) show under On Your Other Devices . Tap Download to save the same area here, or Hide to stop seeing it. See Use OnMyLead on More Than One Device. Download a Ride's Map The quickest way. It saves satellite, topo and trails around the ride's route. If your map style is 3D Terrain, Download This Ride's Map on the ride's map saves 3D Terrain too. The ride list on Offline Maps saves the flat maps only; use Download a Map Area to add 3D Terrain there. From Offline Maps: Under Your Rides , find the ride. Each one shows about how much space it needs. Tap Download . From the ride's map: Open Ride Mode or the ride's waypoints map. Tap the round Map Settings button. Tap Download This Ride's Map . Your Rides lists upcoming rides you've joined that have a mapped route. Downloading a ride again replaces its earlier download, which is handy if the route changed. Download Any Area On Offline Maps, tap Download a Map Area . Move and zoom the map until the frame holds the area you'll ride. The frame's size in miles shows in its corner. Pick the maps to save: Satellite , Topo and Trails . All three are on to start. You can also pick 3D Terrain so the 3D map works there with no signal. It's a bigger download (a 20-mile-square area is roughly 150 MB more), so it's only ticked to start if your map style is 3D Terrain. Check the estimate under the choices. Tap Download This Area . The download is named after the nearest town when your phone can find one. If you see Too big for one download. Zoom in a little. , the area is too large to save with enough detail to ride by. Zoom in, or save it as two downloads. Watch and Manage Downloads Each download on On This Phone shows its maps, its size and how it's going. Pause stops a download for now. Resume carries on from where it stopped. Finish appears when some pieces didn't download. The download shows how many are missing; tap Finish to try them again. Delete takes it off your phone. Tap Delete again to confirm, or Keep . One download runs at a time. If you close the app during a download, it's paused; open Offline Maps and tap Resume . Deleting a download only removes pieces that no other download also uses, so overlapping maps keep working. When the Signal Drops You don't need to do anything. The app checks for a connection while a map is open. When it can't reach the internet: A No Signal tag with Downloaded Map appears under the layers button. The map shows what's saved on your phone. Zoomed in past what you saved, it stretches the closest saved detail. The satellite view switches to USGS aerial photos from your download, since the live satellite view can't be saved ahead of time. The ride's route and waypoints are saved on your phone once you've opened the ride, so they're still on the map too. Download before you leave, while you have good signal. Then open the ride once so its route is on your phone. W

title: Restore Purchases
summary: Bring your OnMyLead Pro subscription back after getting a new iPhone, reinstalling the app, or signing in again.
headings: If It Says No Purchase Was Found
text: If you pay for OnMyLead Pro but your plan shows Free, for example on a new iPhone or after reinstalling the app, use Restore Purchases . It finds your Pro subscription with Apple and turns Pro back on. Restore Your Subscription Sign in to your OnMyLead account. On the You tab, under Settings , tap Subscription . Tap Restore Purchases . If Apple asks, sign in with the Apple Account you used to buy Pro. When it works, the app says Your Pro subscription is restored. and your plan shows Pro . You can also tap Restore Purchases at the bottom of the Pro screen. If It Says No Purchase Was Found The app says No OnMyLead Pro purchase found for this Apple ID. when the Apple Account on this iPhone has no active OnMyLead Pro subscription. Check that: You're signed in to the same Apple Account you used to subscribe. The subscription is still active. Look in iPhone Settings your name Subscriptions . You have signal. Restore on Android On Android, Restore Purchases looks for OnMyLead Pro on the Google account signed in to the Play Store. If it finds none, the app says No OnMyLead Pro purchase found for this Google account. Check that the Play Store is signed in to the Google account you used to subscribe, and that the subscription is still active in the Play Store app under Payments & Subscriptions Subscriptions . You don't need to restore on a different kind of device. Pro bought on an iPhone shows on your Android phone or tablet as soon as you sign in to the same OnMyLead account, and the other way round. One Subscription, One Account An Apple subscription gives Pro to one OnMyLead account at a time. If you restore it while signed in to a different OnMyLead account, Pro moves to that account. Make sure you're signed in to the account you want Pro on before you tap Restore Purchases . Restore Purchases works in the app only, on iPhone, iPad or Android. Once Pro is on your account, it also works when you use OnMyLead on the website.

title: Ride Day and Weather
summary: See the forecast for the meeting area and check whether your ride gets back before sunset, right on the ride page.
text: The Ride Day card on the ride page shows the weather for the meeting area and how your ride lines up with daylight, so nobody gets surprised by a storm or the last miles in the dark. Where to Find It Open the ride page. Ride Day is in the Details section. It shows on upcoming and live rides. The Forecast Ride Day shows the meet day's forecast: The conditions, such as Clear, Partly Cloudy, Rain or Thunderstorms The high and low temperature The chance of rain The wind speed, and gusts when they're much stronger than the wind The forecast shows up about two weeks before the ride. Until then the card says when it will appear. The forecast is for the ride's general meeting area, not the exact spot. The last forecast your phone loaded is saved, so it still shows at a trailhead with no signal. It only updates when you have a connection. Weather Warnings Ride Day adds a heads-up when the forecast calls for: Thunderstorms (watch for lightning and flash floods in washes) A 60% or higher chance of rain Gusts of 35 mph or more A high of 100°F or more A low of 32°F or below Daylight Check Ride Day shows sunrise and sunset at the meeting area, with a bar that shows when the ride runs against the daylight. If the ride has a Back By time (the Expected Finish you set when creating the ride), Ride Day tells you: How long before sunset the group is back When it's cutting it close: back less than 45 minutes before sunset When the group will be back after dark, with a reminder to bring lights If there's no finish time, the card says to add a Back By time so it can check it against sunset. Countdown At the top of an upcoming ride's page, a tag counts down to the meeting time, such as "Tomorrow", "In 4 Days" or "Starts in 25 min".

title: Starlink Dish Status and Power Planner
summary: See your Starlink dish's live status on its Wi-Fi, keep your plan details handy, and work out how long your batteries will run it.
headings: If It Can't Reach Your Dish
text: The Starlink page shows how your dish is doing, keeps your plan details in one place, and works out how long your batteries will run it. Open the Starlink Page Go to the You tab. Under On the Trail , tap Starlink . See Your Dish's Live Status Join your Starlink's Wi-Fi network on your iPhone. On the Starlink page, tap Connect to My Dish . If your iPhone asks to let OnMyLead find devices on your local network, allow it. While the page is open, Your Dish stays live and shows: Whether the dish is online, and its current state. Download Now , Upload Now and Latency . Sky Blocked , Dropped Pings and Up For . Any alerts from the dish. The last 15 minutes as a bar chart, with dropouts in red. Where the dish is facing, GPS, and its software and hardware versions. After the first time, the page reconnects by itself when you open it. It stops reading the dish when you leave the page. This uses your dish's built-in local connection, which SpaceX doesn't officially support. A Starlink update can break it. Everything else on the page keeps working. If It Can't Reach Your Dish If you see Can't Reach Your Dish : Make sure your iPhone is on your Starlink Wi-Fi. Allow local network access in your iPhone's Settings , under OnMyLead . The page keeps trying every 10 seconds. Tap Retry Now to try straight away. If it says your dish answered but couldn't be read, a Starlink software update may have changed things. Try again later. Reading the dish only works in the iPhone app, not on the website. RUS Starlink Mini Mount V2 Below Your Dish , the Starlink page shows an ad for the RUS Offroad Starlink Mini Mount V2 (Morelock Series), a Starlink Mini mount that installs on a Milwaukee Packout and also works with magnets. Tap Shop the Mount to open its page at rusoffroad.com. The price comes from the RUS Offroad store when it can be reached, and shows $249 when it can't. Save Your Plan Starlink doesn't share plan or usage details with other apps, so you can jot them down here. Check your usage in the Starlink app. If you have machines in your Garage, pick one under Setup For , or General . Each one keeps its own setup. Under My Plan , fill in Plan , Monthly Cost ($) and Data Cap (GB) . Pick your Dish and what it's Powered By . Add Notes like your mount, cable length or router settings. Tap Save . You need to be signed in to save. Plan Your Power Under Power Budget : Enter your Dish Watts . If you picked your dish, the typical range is shown. Enter Hours per Day you'll run it. Under Battery Size In , choose Watt-Hours or Amp-Hours + Volts , then enter your battery size. Set Usable % . Use about 90 for lithium and 50 for lead-acid. If you have solar, enter Solar Watts and Sun Hours per day. The page shows your Battery Runtime , what the Dish Uses / Day , what Solar Adds / Day , and your daily balance in green or red. These are estimates. Snow melt, heat and heavy use draw more power. You can use the power calculator without signing in, but you need to sign in to save it.

title: Gear From RUS Offroad
summary: Why you may see product suggestions from RUS Offroad on your machine's page and your trip packing list, and how they're picked.
text: OnMyLead is made by RUS Offroad. In a couple of places, the app may suggest RUS Offroad products that fit your machine or your packing list. The section is always labeled Gear From RUS Offroad . Where You'll See It On one of your machines in your Garage, with products that fit that machine. On a trip in the Trip Planner, with products that fit your packing list and the machine you're taking. Each suggestion shows the product, its price and how it fits, like "Fits your" followed by your machine, or "Fits most machines." Buy or Browse Tap Buy to open that product on the RUS Offroad store inside the app. Tap Shop more at rusoffroad.com to browse the whole store. Purchases happen on the RUS Offroad website, not through OnMyLead or your Apple subscription. When It Doesn't Show The section only appears when something fits. You won't see it if nothing matches, if the store can't be reached, or if suggestions are switched off for a while.

title: Get Directions in Apple Maps or Google Maps
summary: Hand off to Apple Maps or Google Maps for turn-by-turn directions to the meeting point, along the route, to the destination, or to a rider.
headings: Get Directions to the Meeting Point
text: OnMyLead hands you over to Apple Maps or Google Maps for turn-by-turn directions on the road. Off road, follow the leader and the route on the OnMyLead map. On Android, directions open in Google Maps, since Android phones and tablets don't have Apple Maps. Only the place you want to go is sent to the maps app, nothing about you. Directions are a Pro feature. See Free and Pro. On a Free account, the Directions buttons carry a Pro tag. Directions to a rider who taps Need Help, EMERGENCY or Mechanical Issue, or who falls behind the group, always stay free. Get Directions to the Meeting Point Open the ride from the Rides tab. On the Details section, find the Directions card. Tap a row: Meeting Point: the exact meeting spot. Along the Route: follows the ride's route through stops on the way, ending at the end of the route. Destination: the ride's destination, if the organizer added one. Pick Apple Maps or Google Maps , unless you've already chosen one (below). The Directions card shows while the ride is scheduled or live. Meeting Point and Along the Route only show for riders who have joined the ride, because the exact meeting spot and the route are private to them. See Privacy. Get Directions in Ride Mode In Ride Mode, tap Directions just above the bottom panel, on the left. Tap a row: Regroup Point: where the leader asked everyone to meet up, when one is set. Meeting Point Continue Along the Route: picks up from where you are on the route. Destination Pick your maps app, if asked. You can also get directions from other places in Ride Mode: Tap the Regroup point set. Tap to navigate banner. Tap Navigate on a rider's alert card. Open the Riders list and tap Navigate , or Go to Last Seen for a rider whose position is old. Tap a waypoint on the map. See Waypoints and Planned Stops. Directions along the route pass through up to 8 stops picked from the route, and the maps app keeps to roads it knows between them. Off-road parts of the route may differ, so follow the OnMyLead map there. Choose Your Maps App Tap the You tab. Under Settings , tap Directions . Pick Ask Each Time , Apple Maps or Google Maps . Tap Done . Every Navigate and Directions button in the app uses this choice. With Ask Each Time , the app asks which one to open every time. Google Maps opens in its app if you have it installed, and in your browser if you don't.

title: Ride Summary and Ride Again
summary: After a ride ends, see your distance and route, who finished, share a ride card, and set up the same ride again in a few taps.
text: When the organizer ends a ride, everyone who was on it gets a summary on the ride page. Organizers can also start the same ride again with one tap. See Your Ride Summary On the Rides tab, find the ride under Past Rides . Tap it. The summary is at the top of the ride page. The summary has three parts. Your Ride Your Distance and how long you were Out For , plus a map of your route. Only you can see your route. Your stats come from sharing your location in Ride Mode. If you didn't share, there's no track for you on that ride. See Location Sharing. Your distance counts only the miles you actually rode. OnMyLead leaves out: spots where your phone said its location was rough (off by more than about 100 m, or 330 ft), such as indoors or with Approximate Location on; GPS jumps, where your dot bounces away and straight back, or moves while your phone says you're standing still; time when your location was off for more than five minutes, such as with the app closed. The miles across that gap aren't guessed with a straight line, so turn sharing on before you roll out. If your distance looks short, check that your phone has a good location (see Make Your Location Accurate) and that you shared for the whole ride. Moving Time , Average Speed , Top Speed and Climbing are part of Advanced Ride Statistics. This is a Pro feature. See Free and Pro. Your full stats are saved either way. The Group Who finished the ride: the riders still on it when it ended. With Pro, you also see the group's totals: the Longest and Average distance and the Group Top Speed . These are totals only, and nobody's route is shown. Ride Card A picture of the ride to share with friends or on social media. Pick a layout: Standard , Full Stats or Big Number . Tap Share Ride Card . Standard is free. Full Stats and Big Number are Premium Ride Cards. This is a Pro feature. See Free and Pro. The card never shows the meeting point or anyone's route. Ride Again Organizers can set up the same ride again without filling everything in. Open the ended ride's page. In the You're Organizing card, tap Ride Again . The Create a Ride form opens with the name, details, meeting point and route already filled in. The day is set to the next one on the same weekday. Check the day and times. Tap Create Public Ride or Create Private Ride . On a ride that hasn't ended yet, the same button is called Copy This Ride . Ride Again creates a new ride, so it counts toward your monthly rides on Free. See Create a Ride. Advanced Ride Statistics, Premium Ride Cards and full ride history work with Pro from either store: the App Store on iPhone and iPad, or Google Play on Android. Past Rides Ended and cancelled rides move to Past Rides on the Rides tab. Free shows your last 5. Full ride history is a Pro feature. Nothing is deleted, so older rides show again with Pro. See Free and Pro. To remove a ride from your Past Rides, swipe left on it and tap Leave (or Delete if you organized it). On onmylead.com, click the button at the end of the ride's row instead.

title: Search for a Place
summary: Find a trailhead, off-road park, town, street address or coordinates for a meeting point, a destination or the map.
text: Wherever OnMyLead asks for a place, you can type its name instead of hunting on a map: a trailhead, an off-road park, a campground, a town or a street address. Where You Can Search Creating a ride : Search a Place or Address sets the meeting point, and Search a Destination fills in where the ride ends up. See Create a Ride. Find a Ride : Search Near a Place shows rides near the place you pick instead of near you. Tap Back to Near Me (or Clear ) to go back. See Find a Ride. Route builder : Search moves the map to a place before you draw. See Draw a Route. Waypoints map : Search moves the map to a place so you can drop a waypoint or planned stop there. See Waypoints and Planned Stops. Search Tap the search box and type at least three letters. Results show as you type. Each one says what it is and where, like "Trailhead in Moab, Utah". Tap the one you want. What happens next depends on where you searched: For a meeting point, the coordinates and place name fill in for you. You can still edit the Place Name . In the route builder, the map moves to the place and marks it. Nothing is added to your route. On the waypoints map, the map moves to the place and marks it. Press and hold (or click) the map there to drop a waypoint. If nothing turns up, try the full name, a street address with the town, or a nearby town. Search by Coordinates Type coordinates as latitude and longitude, like 38.5733, -109.5498 , and pick the result. This works for spots that don't have a name. Good to Know Search covers places in the United States. Results near you, or near where the map is looking, come first. Search needs a connection. With no signal you'll see No signal for place search. Try again with service. Only the words you type and a rough area are sent to the search service, never who you are or your exact location. On the Website The same searches work on onmylead.com. When you create a ride on the website, you can also click the map to drop the meeting point and drag the pin to fine-tune it. See Create a Ride on the Website. Place Data Places come from OpenStreetMap (map data © OpenStreetMap contributors), searched through Photon, a free service with no account.

title: Change the Look (Light Mode, Themes and Color Blind Mode)
summary: Switch between Dark, Light and Match Phone, pick one of four themes, and turn on Color Blind Mode.
text: OnMyLead starts in the dark Night Navy look. Go to You Appearance to change it. The app redraws as soon as you tap, and it opens the same way next time. Light mode, Match Phone and the themes are Pro features. See Free and Pro. Dark mode, the Navy theme and Color Blind Mode stay free. If you picked a look before version 2.0, the app keeps it. Mode Mode What it does --- --- Dark The dark look OnMyLead has always had. The default. Light Light backgrounds with dark text. Easier to read in bright sun. Match Phone Follows your phone's own Dark Mode setting and switches when your phone does. Themes Each theme comes in a dark and a light version. Buttons stay logo red and links stay logo blue in every theme. Night Navy : the classic OnMyLead look. Carbon : true black. On phones with an OLED screen it uses a little less battery. Desert : warm sand and dust tones. Forest : deep pine green. The maps look the same in every theme, and so do the name tags on the map, so riders always read them the same way. Color Blind Mode Turn on Color Blind Mode if red and green (or blue and yellow) are hard to tell apart. It changes: Rider status colors: OK is sky blue, falling behind is yellow and separated is orange-red, and Ride Mode adds a symbol (✓, ! or ✕) next to a rider who needs a look. Trail ratings, trail spots (obstacles, hazards, water crossings and viewpoints) and your Track Line days. The Appearance screen shows a preview of these colors as you switch. Changing the look only changes how OnMyLead looks on your screen. Other riders don't see your choice. On Your Other Devices Your choice follows your account to every device you sign in on. A change from another device shows the next time you open the app (or right away if you just opened it), so the screen never changes in the middle of a ride. See Use OnMyLead on More Than One Device. On a Tablet On iPad and Android tablets the four themes sit side by side in one row. Everything else works the same as on a phone.

title: Change the App's Language
summary: OnMyLead uses your phone's language when it speaks it, and English when it doesn't. Pick another language any time from the flag on Home or You > Language.
text: OnMyLead speaks 12 languages. The first time you open it, it uses your phone's language if it's one of them, and English if it isn't. You can switch at any time, and the app redraws in the new language straight away. Language Flag shown --- --- English 🇺🇸 Español (Spanish) 🇪🇸 Português (Portuguese) 🇧🇷 Français (French) 🇫🇷 Deutsch (German) 🇩🇪 Italiano (Italian) 🇮🇹 Русский (Russian) 🇷🇺 中文（简体） (Chinese, Simplified) 🇨🇳 日本語 (Japanese) 🇯🇵 한국어 (Korean) 🇰🇷 हिन्दी (Hindi) 🇮🇳 Bahasa Indonesia (Indonesian) 🇮🇩 Change the Language On Home , tap the flag at the top, next to the bell. It shows the flag and two letters of the language the app is in now (for example 🇺🇸 EN). You can also go to You Language . Tap a language. Each one is listed in its own words, so you can find yours whatever the app is showing now. The app redraws in that language and brings you back to the Language screen. To go back to following your phone, tap Match Phone at the top of the list. It shows which language your phone is set to. What Changes and What Doesn't The whole app switches: Home, Ride Mode, Map Mode, ride and group pages, chat, Events, Social, Friends, Garage, Trips, Starlink, Tilt, Pro and every setting, along with the alerts and messages OnMyLead shows you. Places on the Leaderboard and along the Ride Mode line are written your language's way (2.º in Spanish, 2. in German, 2 位 in Japanese), and counts like "1 Coming Up" use the right singular or plural. Spoken alerts in Ride Mode are read in your language. If the voice you picked under You Voice speaks another language, your phone's own voice for your language reads them instead. Status buttons and the built-in quick replies (like Need Fuel or Flat Tire ) show in each rider's own language, so a rider who reads Spanish sees them in Spanish even if you sent them in English. A Ride Mode message you type with the same words as a built-in quick reply (like "on my way") shows as that quick reply. What riders write themselves (posts, comments, chat messages and your own quick replies) shows exactly as they wrote it. Push notifications on your lock screen, the Terms of Use and the Privacy Policy are still in English. The CarPlay screen in your car uses the same language as the app. Things riders write stay the way they wrote them: ride names, chat, posts, group names and trail names. On iPhone and iPad, the permission messages (location, camera, photos, motion) also show in your language. Distances stay in miles. Your Other Devices Your choice is saved to your account, so when you sign in on your iPad, an Android phone or tablet, or onmylead.com, it switches too (see Sync Across Devices). If you leave it on Match Phone , each device follows its own language. Device Differences iPhone and iPad: you can also set OnMyLead's language in the iPhone Settings app OnMyLead Language . With Match Phone picked in the app, it follows that setting. Android phones and tablets (Android 13 and later): you can also set it in Settings System Languages App languages OnMyLead . With Match Phone picked in the app, it follows that setting. onmylead.com: once you're signed in, the flag is on Home and the Language row is on You. Match Phone follows your browser's language. The signed-out homepage stays in English.

title: Delete Your Account
summary: Permanently delete your OnMyLead account and its data from the You tab, and what to do about a Pro subscription first.
text: You can delete your OnMyLead account yourself, right in the app. It happens straight away and can't be undone. Before You Delete If you pay for OnMyLead Pro, cancel it with Apple too. Apple bills the subscription, so deleting your account doesn't stop it. See Manage Your Subscription. Delete Your Account Go to the You tab. Scroll to the bottom and tap Delete Account . Read the message, then tap Delete Account to confirm. You're signed out and taken back to the start. What Gets Deleted Your account and profile. Rides you organize. They're removed for everyone on them. Your Garage, trips and riding groups. Your messages and location history. This can't be undone. To ride with OnMyLead again later, you'd make a new account. One thing is kept: the record that you agreed to the Rider Safety and Liability Agreement, because it's a legal record. See The Rider Safety and Liability Agreement. If You See Deletion Requested Sometimes the app shows Deletion Requested instead of signing you out. That means your request was sent and your account and its data will be deleted within 7 days. If you pay for Pro, cancel it in your Apple subscriptions so you aren't billed again. Need Help? If the delete doesn't go through, Contact Us and pick Account and Sign-In .

title: Release Notes
summary: What's new in every OnMyLead update. Latest: 2.1.
headings: 2.1 Bluetooth Sharing With No Service, Every Map on Mapbox, 3D Terrain and the Badge Leaderboard
2.0 A New Home, Social, Events and Map Mode
1.0.1 Android, Battery Saver and Trail Names
text: OnMyLead 2.1 keeps your group talking where the signal ends: with no cell service, riders on the same ride pass spots, status taps, EMERGENCY alerts and messages to each other over Bluetooth, phone to phone, and every phone passes them along the group (seeing riders and sharing over Bluetooth is part of OnMyLead Pro; on every plan your phone passes alerts along and EMERGENCY goes out, and every rider without Pro gets a fresh 30-day Pro trial with this update). When a rider sends EMERGENCY or their Crash Alert goes out, every other rider's phone now sounds a loud siren until they silence it. The new Leaderboard ranks riders by the badges they earned by riding. 3D Terrain is a new map style for Ride Mode and Map Mode that shows the real shape of the land, so you can see the ridges, canyons and climbs ahead. And every map in the app is now drawn by Mapbox, so Ride Mode, Map Mode, the route builder and Find a Ride look and work the same on your phone, tablet and onmylead.com. Bluetooth Sharing: when there's no cell service, Ride Mode passes your spot (while you're sharing with the ride), your status taps, EMERGENCY, quick replies and typed messages to nearby riders on the same ride over Bluetooth, about 100 to 300 feet between phones, and every phone passes along what it hears, up to six phones down the line, so the back of the group can reach the front. Phones that get a newer spot for any rider pass that on too, and a phone with signal shares what OnMyLead knows with the riders near it that have none. The card under your tap says whose phone got it over Bluetooth and who has seen it, even while it waits for signal. Messages heard over Bluetooth show in chat marked Via Bluetooth. When any phone on the ride gets signal, it sends what it heard so everyone else sees it too. Everything is encrypted for your ride only, and the radio idles when you have service and nobody is in range. Seeing riders and sharing your spot, taps and messages over Bluetooth is part of OnMyLead Pro (and the Pro Trial); on every plan your phone passes everything along, and EMERGENCY, Need Help and Crash Alerts go out over Bluetooth. Turn it off any time on the You tab. New in Pro: Bluetooth Sharing with no service (EMERGENCY, Need Help, Crash Alerts and passing things along stay free), CarPlay, customizing your dot (Dot Style and Dot Size) and adding group photos. Everyone can still see group photos, and on Free your dot is the Red, White and Blue dot. So nobody loses anything the day 2.1 arrives, every rider who doesn't have Pro gets a fresh 30-day Pro trial, even if you had one before, and Home shows the date it ends. Safety stays free on every plan. Group Spread on the leader line: a thin measuring line under the rider dots runs from the leader to the tail gunner, with how far back the last rider is in the middle (such as 0.8 mi) and small ticks every round step, so you can see how far apart the group really is. It works on routes and Freerides, and with Bluetooth Sharing when there's no service. The big miles-done number above the line is gone, and the line about your place is centered under it. Emergency Siren: when another rider on your ride sends EMERGENCY, from the button, CarPlay or a Crash Alert that ran out, your phone sounds a loud siren on a full-screen alert until you tap Silence Siren or Show Me Where. With OnMyLead open it plays even with the ring/silent switch on silent and turns your music down under it; with the app closed the notification itself plays the siren (on Android as an alarm, so you hear it with the ringer on silent). With no service it sounds over Bluetooth too. It stops by itself if the rider cancels or taps I'm OK. It's on for everyone; switch it off or tap Play Siren to hear it in Notification Settings. A new rider dot with the arrow built in: every live rider is a glossy disc with a white rim and a white arrow pointing the way they're heading, and it keeps pointing their last way while they're stopped. The leader is the big
